EDCS-00380630.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest. Mansuetus [dedicated this].
EDCS-00380630.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by a person named Mansuetus.

EDCS-00380636.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Ennebon as the son of Secundionis.

EDCS-00380637.translation: Julius Andostennis, his son, fulfilled [this vow] willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-00380637.summary: This is a votive inscription by Julius Andostennis fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-00380645.text_edition: \n Vivus Caius Iulius Leonis libertus Niger sibi et Iuliae Leonis libertae Hilarae et Caio Iulio Leonis liberto Adiuco fratri\n
EDCS-00380645.translation: Caius Julius Niger, freedman of Gaius Julius Leonis, [set this up] for himself, and for Iulia Hilara, freedwoman of Gaius Julius Leonis, and for his brother Caius Julius Adiuctus, freedman of Gaius Julius Leonis.
EDCS-00380645.summary: This funerary inscription records the setting up of a monument by a freedman for himself, his wife, and his brother, all of whom were freedmen of the same patron.

EDCS-00380646.translation: To the divine Manes and the memory of Marcianus.
EDCS-00380646.summary: This is a dedication to the Manes and memory of an individual named Marcianus.

EDCS-00380647.translation: Adjacent to the sacred, bordering the sacred, Apollinaris, illustrious, powerful in his dignities, governor of the forum and judge of the world, lived thus by his merits; he kept calm amidst the turbulent waves of causes, and by his counsel brought back peace among discordant kingdoms warring with arms. Yet, while doing these things, he wrote for perpetual remembrance and after such gifts, seated in the chair of the supreme pontiff, he renounced worldly affairs. And you who will pray here with tears to the right-hand god, pour out prayers over the tomb; unknown to no one and to be read by the world, may Sidonius be invoked by you. On the twelfth day before the Kalends of September, with Zenone as Emperor.
EDCS-00380647.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Apollinaris, a high-ranking official and judge who also engaged in philosophy and poetry, likely dating to the reign of Emperor Zenon (474-491 AD).

EDCS-00380649.text_edition: \n restitutio Calvi filii Caius Acidilius pater et filia M\n
EDCS-00380649.translation: Restoration by Calvus, son of Gaius Acidilius, and his daughter M[...].
EDCS-00380649.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something by a father and daughter, likely a public work or monument.

EDCS-03000601.summary: This inscription lists three personal names, likely indicating ownership or belonging.

EDCS-03000602.summary: This inscription identifies Embeter as the wife of Erda Hauteten.

EDCS-03000605.translation: To the spirits of the underworld and to the memory of Mercae.
EDCS-03000605.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed spirit of Mercae.

EDCS-03000607.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription setting up a monument for a son named Corca.

EDCS-03000609.translation: To the divine Manes of Venenia.
EDCS-03000609.summary: This is a dedication to the divine Manes of an individual named Venenia.

EDCS-03000610.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Asiatica, aged 70.
EDCS-03000610.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Asiatica, who died at the age of 70.

EDCS-03000611.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Iulius Mercator.
EDCS-03000611.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iulius Mercator.

EDCS-03000612.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Aunati
EDCS-03000612.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirit of Aunati, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-03000614.summary: A dedication to Publius Attius, possibly related to a public monument or honorary inscription.

EDCS-03000615.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Regalis
EDCS-03000615.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirit of Regalis, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-03000617.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Mercurialis
EDCS-03000617.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirit of Mercurialis, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-03000618.translation: [To the divine Manes] and to the memory of Virilis, the very dear maker of tunics, [set up] for himself while alive.
EDCS-03000618.summary: This funerary inscription records a man, Virilis, who was a tunic-maker, setting up a monument for himself and his wife.

EDCS-03000619.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Acorra
EDCS-03000619.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirit of Acorra, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-03000620.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Maternus
EDCS-03000620.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirit of Maternus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-03000621.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the burial of Constantius, described as 'noble'.

EDCS-03300673.summary: This is a short inscription intended to be a memorial to Avitus.

EDCS-03300674.summary: A short epitaph or farewell wishing Valerius safe passage, likely in the afterlife.

EDCS-03700601.translation: Lucius Iulius Venustus, while alive, made this monument for himself and for his wife Savina, daughter of Cenialis, and for his daughter Vetustina, who has died.
EDCS-03700601.summary: A funerary monument self-funded by Lucius Iulius Venustus for himself and his deceased wife and daughter, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-03700608.translation: Silvinus [paid] three and a quarter sextarii [of wine] for a denarius, one asse [of oil] for a sextarius, and one [measure] of honey for a sescunx; [and one jar] for an as.
EDCS-03700608.summary: An inscription detailing the prices of various goods like wine, oil, and honey, possibly from a shop or a receipt, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04100002.translation: To the departed spirits and the memory of Domitia Veria, deceased.
EDCS-04100002.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Domitia Veria.

EDCS-05000605.translation: Oracinus, son of Patrix, Iunior L.
EDCS-05000605.summary: This inscription appears to record the name and possibly lineage or affiliation of an individual named Oracinus.

EDCS-05200499.summary: This inscription likely refers to vinegar belonging to or produced by the Manlii family.

EDCS-06100403.translation: On the death of Avitus. Ha Silex, son of Avitus, [...].
EDCS-06100403.summary: This inscription begins by marking the death of Avitus and names his son, Ha Silex, likely for a funerary monument.

EDCS-06100410.text_edition: \n Cai Iun et Titi Caius Iunxs \n
EDCS-06100410.translation: Caius Iunius [set this up] for Caius Iunius and Titus.
EDCS-06100410.summary: This inscription records Caius Iunius dedicating something, possibly a tomb or monument, to Caius Iunius and Titus.

EDCS-06100411.translation: Postumus, son of Dumnorigis, a vergobretus, gave the water of Mars for ten days and nights from his own funds.
EDCS-06100411.summary: This inscription records a dedication of water by Postumus, a vergobretus (a Gallic chief magistrate), for a specified period.

EDCS-08300453.translation: To Tranquillus, the linen merchant, thus.
EDCS-08300453.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Tranquillus, identified as a linen merchant.

EDCS-08500465.translation: To Lucius Iunius, a seller of linseed.
EDCS-08500465.summary: This inscription is a dedication or record of an individual named Lucius Iunius, identified by his profession as a linseed seller.

EDCS-08500466.text_edition: \n ino Anicianni sic filius Mercurio Augusto votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08500466.translation: [...ino Anicianni]. Thus, his son paid a willing and deserved vow to Mercurius Augustus.
EDCS-08500466.summary: This inscription records a son fulfilling a vow to the god Mercurius Augustus, likely in memory of his father, Aniciannus.

EDCS-08500467.text_edition: \n Silvinus Connixii filius Iunoni votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08500467.translation: Silvinus, son of Connix, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Juno.
EDCS-08500467.summary: This is a votive inscription by Silvinus to Juno.

EDCS-08500468.text_edition: \n Marcus Iulius Pyrus Matu hanc aedem \n
EDCS-08500468.translation: Marcus Julius Pyrus [built?] this temple to Matu-.
EDCS-08500468.summary: This is a dedication inscription for a temple, with Marcus Julius Pyrus as the likely dedicator.

EDCS-08600498.text_edition: \n Deo Erriape sic Taurianus et Andustinus et Taurianus lapidem post annos III deposuerunt votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-08600498.translation: Taurianus, Andustinus, and Taurianus willingly and deservedly placed this stone after 3 years and paid their vow to the god Erriapus.
EDCS-08600498.summary: This is a votive inscription by Taurianus, Andustinus, and Taurianus to the god Erriapus, marking the placement of a stone.

EDCS-08600499.text_edition: \n Deo Eriappo Castinus agens pro salute sua et suorum votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08600499.translation: Castinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Eriappos for the health of himself and his family.
EDCS-08600499.summary: This is a votive inscription by Castinus to the god Eriappos for his and his family's health.

EDCS-08600775.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Silex.
EDCS-08600775.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by an individual named Silex.

EDCS-08600777.translation: To the god Jupiter Best and Greatest, Placida Consueti.
EDCS-08600777.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus made by Placida Consueti.

EDCS-08600778.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by individuals, including Maximinus.

EDCS-08600779.translation: Aelius, son of [---], willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-08600779.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Aelius, son of [---].

EDCS-08600781.summary: This inscription simply records the name Aemilius Nigrinus.

EDCS-08600784.translation: Erriapo Montanus willingly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-08600784.summary: This is a votive inscription by Erriapo Montanus, likely a private dedication.

EDCS-08600785.text_edition: \n Iulia Paterna votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08600785.translation: Iulia Paterna willingly and deservedly paid her vow.
EDCS-08600785.summary: This is a votive inscription by Iulia Paterna.

EDCS-08600786.text_edition: \n @(obito) Birrioni viva -risila B uxsor sic et O salve\n
EDCS-08600786.translation: Birrio having died, his wife B...risila erected this, and greetings.
EDCS-08600786.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating the deceased Birrio and erected by his wife.

EDCS-08600787.text_edition: \n Ilurgorri Severus Semperri filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08600787.translation: Ilurgorri Severus, son of Semperri, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-08600787.summary: This is a votive inscription by Ilurgorri Severus.

EDCS-08600789.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and the other gods, Quintus Vedius Silvanus, a marble worker, who came from the retinue after five years, willingly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-08600789.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintus Vedius Silvanus, a marble worker, dedicated to Jupiter and other gods, mentioning his return after five years, likely from military service.

EDCS-08600790.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Amandus Andosteni filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08600790.translation: Amandus, son of Andosteni, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-08600790.summary: This is a votive inscription by Amandus to Jupiter.

EDCS-08600793.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or funerary text, mentioning Aelius C. Diphilus.

EDCS-08900475.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus and Marcus Julius Philippus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-08900475.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Marcus Julius Philippus and his son Marcus Julius Philippus Caesar, likely from the Severan period.

EDCS-09001527.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Claudius Tacitus, Pious, Fortunate, Invictus Augustus, with tribunician power.
EDCS-09001527.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Marcus Claudius Tacitus, mentioning his titles and tribunician power, dating to his reign (275-276 AD).

EDCS-09001529.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly recording a legal or administrative act by someone named Vergobretos.

EDCS-09200352.translation: Marinus, son of Taurinus, willingly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-09200352.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marinus, son of Taurinus, likely a private dedication.

EDCS-09200354.text_edition: \n Publi Fabi Pupi harpagion ad lippitudinem Publi Fabi Pupi mixtum militare Publi Fabi Pupi dialepidos ad diathesis sic Publi Fabi Pupi diasmyrnes lene\n
EDCS-09200354.translation: The mixture of Publius Fabius Pupi for sore eyes, the eye salve of Publius Fabius Pupi, the ointment of Publius Fabius Pupi, gently.
EDCS-09200354.summary: This is a label for a medicinal preparation, likely for eye ailments, belonging to Publius Fabius Pupi.

EDCS-09200367.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Martius, son of Marcellinus.

EDCS-09201206.translation: Sent out standing, Eros son of Caesar aged 16, Xantus son of Caesar aged 15.
EDCS-09201206.summary: This inscription records two young individuals, Eros and Xantus, both identified as sons of Caesar, with their ages, possibly related to a military or administrative context.

EDCS-09201207.translation: C. Sollicana Secunda dedicated this for her husband and herself.
EDCS-09201207.summary: This is a funerary or dedicatory inscription set up by C. Sollicana Secunda for her husband and herself.

EDCS-09201208.translation: To the departed spirits of Quintus Titucius Silvinus.
EDCS-09201208.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring the departed spirit of Quintus Titucius Silvinus.

EDCS-09201248.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Vareniae Montani filiae Montanillae Quintus Solonius Philippus uxsori sic rarissimae nnorum XXII\n
EDCS-09201248.translation: To the divine spirits of Varenia Montanilla, daughter of Montanus. Quintus Solonius Philippus to his most rare wife, aged 22 years.
EDCS-09201248.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Varenia Montanilla, erected by her husband Quintus Solonius Philippus.

EDCS-09202280.translation: To the departed spirits, Pompeia [dedicated this] for her father Quintus Pompeius Chresimus.
EDCS-09202280.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Pompeia for her father Quintus Pompeius Chresimus.

EDCS-09300407.translation: Gaius Caecilius of the Galeria tribe gladly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-09300407.summary: This is a votive dedication by Gaius Caecilius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302585.translation: Ombecco gladly paid his vow to the god Silvanus, as was deserved.
EDCS-09302585.summary: This is a votive dedication to the god Silvanus by Ombecco, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09400519.translation: To the Spirits of the departed, for Bani.
EDCS-09400519.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bani, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400520.translation: To the Spirits of the departed, for Lupianus the innkeeper, for his Lupia, aged 30, and for Masus, aged [---].
EDCS-09400520.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lupianus and Masus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400521.translation: To the Spirits of the departed, for Matrinus.
EDCS-09400521.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Matrinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400522.translation: To the eternal Spirits of the departed, for Nurisius.
EDCS-09400522.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Nurisius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400523.translation: To the Spirits of the departed, for Paullus, son of Avitus.
EDCS-09400523.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Paullus, son of Avitus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400524.translation: For Prepusae. To the Spirits of the departed.
EDCS-09400524.summary: This is a funerary inscription mentioning Prepusae, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400525.translation: To the Spirits of the departed, in memory of Publius, son of Paulus.
EDCS-09400525.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius, son of Paulus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400526.translation: To the Spirits of the departed, for Sedulus.
EDCS-09400526.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sedulus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400527.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Silvinus, aged 75.
EDCS-09400527.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Silvinus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400528.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Solinus.
EDCS-09400528.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Solinus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400529.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Sumen.
EDCS-09400529.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sumen, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400530.translation: To Venus, aged 50, his messmate set this up.
EDCS-09400530.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Venus, likely for a soldier or member of a collegium, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400531.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Vicana.
EDCS-09400531.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vicana, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09401115.translation: Iulia Dannoesa made this for her son Lucius Julius Laetus, under the supervision of Modestus, son of Solimarus.
EDCS-09401115.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Iulia Dannoesa for her son, possibly in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09401118.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a tombstone or a dedication, for Ulpius Genialis, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09401474.translation: Quintus Sergius Macrinus dedicated this temple to the Divine Powers of the Emperors and to the god Mercury Felix, fulfilling his vow willingly and deservedly from his own resources.
EDCS-09401474.summary: This is a dedication of a temple to the Imperial deities and Mercury Felix by Quintus Sergius Macrinus, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09401475.translation: Quintus Sergius Macrinus donated this new temple to the Divine Powers of the Emperors and to the god Mercury Felix, fulfilling his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-09401475.summary: This is a dedication of a new temple to the Imperial deities and Mercury Felix by Quintus Sergius Macrinus, similar to EDCS-09401474 and likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09401477.translation: To the god Mars, of April.
EDCS-09401477.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mars, possibly related to the month of April or an individual named Aprilis, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09401478.translation: To the spirits of the departed, in memory of Asicus Secundianus, aged 97.
EDCS-09401478.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Asicus Secundianus, who died at the age of 97.

EDCS-09401479.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Aunilla.
EDCS-09401479.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription dedicated to Aunilla.

EDCS-09401480.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Cantia.
EDCS-09401480.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription dedicated to Cantia.

EDCS-09401481.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Dometianus, aged 10.
EDCS-09401481.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Dometianus, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-09401482.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Eburnius Iulianus, aged 45.
EDCS-09401482.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Eburnius Iulianus, who died at the age of 45.

EDCS-09401483.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Iulius Pequliaris.
EDCS-09401483.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription dedicated to Iulius Pequliaris.

EDCS-09700672.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Donata Donaticna, from her own funds.
EDCS-09700672.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Donata Donaticna, erected at her own expense.

EDCS-09701069.translation: To the god Carpento, Publius, son of Titullus, willingly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-09701069.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Carpento, dedicated by Publius, son of Titullus.

EDCS-09701072.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Donata Donaticna, placed this from her own funds.
EDCS-09701072.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Donata Donaticna, erected at her own expense.

EDCS-09701073.translation: Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, son of the divine Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the divine Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time, (decreed concerning) the Limon for 10 miles and the boundaries for 6 miles.
EDCS-09701073.summary: This is an imperial rescript from Emperor Hadrian concerning administrative matters related to roads (Limon) and boundaries.

EDCS-09701566.summary: This inscription is a personal name, likely of a freedman, found in an ancient Roman context.

EDCS-09800237.summary: This is a simple tomb inscription recording the burial of Peculia.

EDCS-09800238.summary: This inscription is a personal name, likely of a Roman citizen, found in an ancient Roman context.

EDCS-09800239.translation: To the departed spirits and in memory of Aelianus. A public monument for Aelius and his daughter, by the freedman Marianus Aelianus.
EDCS-09800239.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to Aelianus, Aelius, and his daughter, erected by Marianus Aelianus.

EDCS-09800242.translation: To the departed spirits of Licinia Primitiva. Licinius Fortunatus, a veteran, erected this.
EDCS-09800242.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Licinia Primitiva, set up by her husband, a veteran named Licinius Fortunatus.

EDCS-09800244.translation: To the departed spirits and in memory of Reginius Cocus, aged 28.
EDCS-09800244.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Reginius Cocus, who died at the age of 28.

EDCS-09800248.translation: Atarillus, son of Atarillus, the wine merchant.
EDCS-09800248.summary: This inscription names Atarillus, son of Atarillus, and identifies him as a wine merchant.

EDCS-09800582.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus, consul, father of the fatherland, and to Marcus Julius Philippus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, and to Otacilia Severa Augusta, mother of our Augustus and of the camps. The conventus of the Convenae (city) [is responsible for this] 1000 paces.
EDCS-09800582.summary: This is a dedication honouring Emperor Philip the Arab, his son, and his wife, erected by the conventus of the Convenae, likely marking a distance or road.

EDCS-09800583.text_edition: \n Domino nostri Marco Aurelio Carino nobillissimo Caesari principi [iuventutis ------\n
EDCS-09800583.translation: To our Lord Marcus Aurelius Carinus, most noble Caesar, prince [of youth...].
EDCS-09800583.summary: This is a dedication to Carinus, who held the title of Caesar, with the beginning of the inscription lost.

EDCS-10400155.translation: To the departed spirits of Julia Paulina, daughter of Sergius. Marcus Sergius Paulus set this up for his mother.
EDCS-10400155.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Julia Paulina, dedicated by her son, Marcus Sergius Paulus.

EDCS-10400156.translation: Fuscus, son of Tottonis, while alive, for himself and his wife Neuresen, daughter of Senda, and for his deceased son Lucilius and daughter Lucilia.
EDCS-10400156.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a family, including children who died before the parents, commissioned by the father, Fuscus, during his lifetime.

EDCS-10400158.translation: Rufus, son of Sembexon, is deceased. Pusilla, wife of Rufus and daughter of Troccus, is deceased. Rufinus, son of Rufus, while alive. Primulus, son of Rufus, while alive. For themselves and their families.
EDCS-10400158.summary: This is a funerary inscription for multiple family members, commissioned by two surviving sons during their lifetime.

EDCS-10400159.translation: Hanarro, son of Dannorix, having died, who was magistrate four times and quaestor, and his wife Aldeni, daughter of Donnus.
EDCS-10400159.summary: This epitaph commemorates Hanarro, a twice-elected magistrate and quaestor, and his wife Aldeni.

EDCS-10400160.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Author of good weather, Valerius Iustus [dedicated this].
EDCS-10400160.summary: This dedicatory inscription records Valerius Iustus offering to Jupiter for favorable weather.

EDCS-10400161.translation: To Fortuna Augusta, Marcus Valerius Iustus [dedicated this] in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-10400161.summary: Marcus Valerius Iustus made a votive dedication to the deified Empress Fortuna Augusta.

EDCS-10400162.translation: Sacred to Minerva Belisama, Quintus Valerius Montanus [dedicated this] in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-10400162.summary: Quintus Valerius Montanus made a votive dedication to Minerva Belisama.

EDCS-10400163.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Longinus, twice chief magistrate; Valeria, wife of the excellent man.
EDCS-10400163.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to Longinus, a former chief magistrate, by his wife Valeria.

EDCS-10400164.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Caius Frontonius; Quintus Iulius Tauricus [dedicated this].
EDCS-10400164.summary: Quintus Iulius Tauricus dedicated this epitaph to Caius Frontonius.

EDCS-10400165.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Gaius Julius Fuscianus, dearest husband; his wife Iulia Alpina.
EDCS-10400165.summary: Iulia Alpina dedicated this epitaph to her beloved husband, Gaius Julius Fuscianus.

EDCS-10400166.translation: To Nonia Evanthis, incomparable wife, who lived 28 years, 5 months, 27 days; Titus Terentius Marcellus, soldier.
EDCS-10400166.summary: This epitaph records the life details of Nonia Evanthis, who died at age 28, and was dedicated by her husband, Titus Terentius Marcellus, a soldier.

EDCS-10400167.summary: Primulus dedicated this epitaph to his mother, Serana.

EDCS-10400168.translation: To T. O. A. Haloisso, Gaius Pomptinius Superbus.
EDCS-10400168.summary: Gaius Pomptinius Superbus dedicated this inscription, possibly to a deity or a deceased person named Haloisso.

EDCS-10400169.translation: Laetinus, son of Laetus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the goddess Andeis.
EDCS-10400169.summary: A votive inscription to the goddess Andeis, dedicated by Laetinus.

EDCS-10400170.translation: Sergius Paulus to his most chaste wife.
EDCS-10400170.summary: A funerary dedication by Sergius Paulus to his wife.

EDCS-10400171.translation: Dunomagius, son of Toutannorigis, his brother and heir, ordered this to be made from his will for Tiberius Julius Niger, son of Ittixo, a centurion of the Fourth Cohort of Aquitanians, and had it carried out under the supervision of Lepidus, son of Dannos.
EDCS-10400171.summary: A funerary monument for a centurion, ordered by his brother and heir and executed by a supervisor.

EDCS-10400282.translation: Bound by eternal sleep, here lies Nymfius. His pious soul enjoys heaven and sees the stars. May he rest peacefully, his body embraced by the tomb. His holy faith trod down the sad darkness, and your deserving fame carried him to the stars of heaven. For he will be immortal, since his living glory will flourish through future peoples. All the province wished for him, their own parent, and public prayers welcomed your life, which was once given at your expense. The council of elders and the jubilant crowds through the stands hailed you, and our nurturing homeland called to you, and spoke through your hallowed voice. Now confused cities are filled with grief, and anxious crowds of elders sit bewildered, just as bodies grow stiff with a severed head, and just as a flock mourns when its leader is lost. His wife Serena, in her great grief, dedicates this tombstone to you, her dear husband. Always his inseparable companion, she gave herself to his support for eight years. Life with you was sweet, her anxious companion. Hoping for eternal light, she wishes this [life] to be brief.
EDCS-10400282.summary: This lengthy funerary epitaph, set up by his wife Serena, commemorates Nymfius, praising his virtues, public service, and piety, and lamenting the profound grief his death has caused.

EDCS-10400332.translation: For Iullus Occasius and for Bonexsa, daughter of Senixsus, his wife, and for Prima, his mother; for Sennagus, son of Paullus.
EDCS-10400332.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates several individuals, likely a family, possibly dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400333.translation: To Bonna, daughter of Rusticus. By Taurinus, son of Rusticus.
EDCS-10400333.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to Bonna by Taurinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400334.translation: Antonius Vindemialis set this up to the god Ageio, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-10400334.summary: This dedication records a votive offering to the god Ageio by Antonius Vindemialis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400336.translation: Egloge fulfilled a vow to the god Erge.
EDCS-10400336.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Erge by Egloge, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400337.translation: Illanis, son of ---, willingly and deservedly fulfilled a vow.
EDCS-10400337.summary: This votive inscription records an offering made by Illanis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400341.translation: Andere, son of Sapalo, willingly and deservedly fulfilled a vow to the god Erge.
EDCS-10400341.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Erge by Andere, son of Sapalo, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400342.translation: Andoston, son of Andos, Vitalis, and Narhonsus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled vows to the god Erge.
EDCS-10400342.summary: This inscription records multiple votive offerings to the god Erge by Andoston, Vitalis, and Narhonsus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400343.translation: A[---]nic fulfilled a vow to the god Erge, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10400343.summary: This votive inscription records an offering to the god Erge by A[---]nic, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400344.translation: Oro, son of Belexennis, willingly and deservedly fulfilled a vow to the god Erge.
EDCS-10400344.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Erge by Oro, son of Belexennis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400345.translation: To the god Erge, good one.
EDCS-10400345.summary: An incomplete dedication to the god Erge, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10400347.translation: Sacred offering to Erge from Coelia.
EDCS-10400347.summary: A dedication to the god Erge by Coelia, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10400348.translation: Erge dedicated this votive offering to the god and fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-10400348.summary: A votive inscription to the god Erge, recording the fulfillment of a vow, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10400349.translation: Hannas gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the temple of Erge.
EDCS-10400349.summary: A votive inscription to the temple of Erge, recording the fulfillment of a vow by Hannas, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10400350.translation: Lucius Iulius Novalis gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Erge.
EDCS-10400350.summary: A votive inscription to the god Erge, recording the fulfillment of a vow by Lucius Iulius Novalis, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10400351.translation: Licinia, daughter of Licinius, gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the god Ercianus.
EDCS-10400351.summary: A votive inscription to the god Ercianus, recording the fulfillment of a vow by Licinia, daughter of Licinius, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10400353.translation: Erhe Anossi’s daughter fulfilled her vow to the god Erge.
EDCS-10400353.summary: A votive inscription to the god Erge, recording the fulfillment of a vow by Erhe Anossi’s daughter, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10400354.translation: Rustica, daughter of Paratus, gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the god Erge.
EDCS-10400354.summary: A votive inscription to the god Erge, recording the fulfillment of a vow by Rustica, daughter of Paratus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10400355.translation: To the god Erge from Sori Hannas.
EDCS-10400355.summary: A dedication to the god Erge by Sori Hannas, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10400356.translation: [---] fulfilled his/her vow to the god Erge gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-10400356.summary: An incomplete votive inscription to the god Erge, recording the fulfillment of a vow, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10400363.translation: Alpinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Mars.
EDCS-10400363.summary: A dedication to the god Mars by Alpinus, likely a soldier, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400364.translation: Candida willingly and deservedly paid her vow to the god Mars.
EDCS-10400364.summary: A dedication to the god Mars by Candida, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400365.translation: Calius willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Mars.
EDCS-10400365.summary: A dedication to the god Mars by Calius, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400366.translation: Taurinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Mars.
EDCS-10400366.summary: A dedication to the god Mars by Taurinus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400368.translation: His son Belexconis willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10400368.summary: A dedication by the son of Belexconis, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400370.translation: Vitalis willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10400370.summary: A dedication by Vitalis, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400371.translation: Taurinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10400371.summary: A dedication by Taurinus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400375.translation: To the god Ageio, from Bassari.
EDCS-10400375.summary: A dedication to the god Ageio by Bassari.

EDCS-10400376.translation: Gaius Fabius Montanus, son of Gaius Fabius Alardossus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10400376.summary: A dedication by Gaius Fabius Montanus, son of Gaius Fabius Alardossus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400377.translation: To the god Fagus, from Bonxus, son of Taurinus.
EDCS-10400377.summary: A dedication to the god Fagus by Bonxus, son of Taurinus.

EDCS-10400379.translation: To the god Fagus, Pompeia, daughter of Caius, gladly fulfilled her vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400379.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Fagus by Pompeia.

EDCS-10400380.translation: To the god Hercules, Andossus gladly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400380.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Hercules by Andossus.

EDCS-10400381.translation: To Hercules, Festus gladly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400381.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Hercules by Festus.

EDCS-10400382.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Hercules by Poblicius Rufus.

EDCS-10400384.translation: Bihotus set this up to Hercules Invictus in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-10400384.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Hercules Invictus by Bihotus.

EDCS-10400387.translation: To Jupiter, the god, Clamosa, a citizen of the Treveri, gladly fulfilled her vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400387.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter by Clamosa, a Treveran citizen.

EDCS-10400388.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Iulia Ingenua gladly fulfilled her vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400388.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Iulia Ingenua.

EDCS-10400389.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Nigrinus, son of Aptus, and Optuma, daughter of Gallus, gladly fulfilled their vows as deserved.
EDCS-10400389.summary: This inscription records a joint votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Nigrinus and Optuma.

EDCS-10400390.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Gnaeus Pompeius Martus gladly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400390.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Gnaeus Pompeius Martus.

EDCS-10400391.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Lucius Pompeius Masclinus gladly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400391.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Lucius Pompeius Masclinus.

EDCS-10400394.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, the Salutary One, Ulpianus Amfilus, freed from a serious illness.
EDCS-10400394.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter by Ulpianus Amfilus after recovering from an illness.

EDCS-10400395.translation: Bonxorius, son of Faustinus, willingly paid his vow to the god Mars, as was deserved.
EDCS-10400395.summary: This is a votive inscription where Bonxorius paid a vow to the god Mars.

EDCS-10400396.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mars by Lucidus.

EDCS-10400398.translation: Masculus, freedman of Ingenua, willingly paid his vow to the god Mercury, as was deserved.
EDCS-10400398.summary: This is a votive inscription by Masculus, a freedman, dedicated to Mercury.

EDCS-10400400.translation: To the Tutelary God, Titus Aurelius, for his health.
EDCS-10400400.summary: This is a dedication to a Tutelary God by Titus Aurelius for his own health.

EDCS-10400401.translation: Andos, son of Barosis, paid his vow.
EDCS-10400401.summary: This is a votive inscription by Andos, son of Barosis, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400402.translation: vus, son of Iarbonis, willingly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-10400402.summary: This is a votive inscription by vus, son of Iarbonis, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400403.translation: Sabini's slave, willingly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-10400403.summary: This is a votive inscription by the slave of Sabinus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10400408.translation: To Tiberius Claudius, emperor, consul 26 times, father of the fatherland, from the citizenry of Convenae.
EDCS-10400408.summary: This is a public dedication from the citizens of Convenae to Emperor Tiberius Claudius, noting his honors and consulships.

EDCS-10400411.translation: Tiberius Publius Sabinus made tables with bases for the villagers of the Florentine village at his own expense.
EDCS-10400411.summary: This is a public benefaction by Tiberius Publius Sabinus, who provided tables and bases for the Florentine village.

EDCS-10400413.translation: Bonxsus, his brother, made this for the death of Dannadinnis, son of Dannadinnis, in Rome.
EDCS-10400413.summary: A funerary dedication by a brother for the deceased Dannadinnis, likely from Rome.

EDCS-10400414.translation: Alfia, daughter of Lohis, known as Bulluca.
EDCS-10400414.summary: A simple epitaph identifying Alfia, daughter of Lohis.

EDCS-10400415.translation: Aucta, his mother, [made this] for Amandus, freedman of Optatus.
EDCS-10400415.summary: A funerary monument erected by a mother for her freedman son.

EDCS-10400416.translation: To the Divine Spirits: Salisius for his most devoted son, Andossicus.
EDCS-10400416.summary: A dedication to the Divine Spirits for a devoted son named Andossicus.

EDCS-10400417.translation: Sabina, daughter of Fronto, [made this] according to the will for Andossus, son of Primulus, upon his death.
EDCS-10400417.summary: A posthumous dedication made by a wife according to the deceased's will.

EDCS-10400418.translation: Urbanus, son of Attacon, and Sennacius, son of Attacon, heirs, took care to have this made for the death of Attacon, son of Siricco.
EDCS-10400418.summary: Sons acting as heirs commissioned this monument for their deceased father.

EDCS-10400419.translation: Fressus and Quintus set up this sacred monument to the Divine Spirits for Aurelia Lana, their dearest wife.
EDCS-10400419.summary: A funerary dedication by two individuals, Fressus and Quintus, for their dearest wife Aurelia Lana.

EDCS-10400420.translation: Bonnoris, son of Dunohoricis, [made this] while alive for himself, and for his living wife Rhexoni, daughter of Hotarris, and for his living stepson Sabinus, son of Seniponnis.
EDCS-10400420.summary: A self-dedicatory funerary monument for the dedicator, his wife, and his stepson.

EDCS-10400421.translation: Silex, wife and heir according to the will, [made this] for her son Borso, son of Adeilus, and for her son Odoxus, son of Lohitton, and for her son Andostennus, son of Andossus.
EDCS-10400421.summary: A funerary inscription made by a wife and heir for multiple deceased sons.

EDCS-10400423.summary: A fragmented inscription possibly dedicating a monument to a brother.

EDCS-10400424.translation: Fuscinus, son of Fusco, arranged for this to be made according to the will of Severa, daughter of Silvanus, his wife.
EDCS-10400424.summary: This funerary inscription records that Fuscinus commissioned the monument in accordance with the will of his deceased wife, Severa.

EDCS-10400426.translation: Here lies Hahanna, daughter of Seranus.
EDCS-10400426.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription for Hahanna, daughter of Seranus.

EDCS-10400428.translation: While alive, Gaius Julius Atticus, freedman of Erotis, and his freedwoman Salviola, and his deceased freedman Gaius Julius Victor, son of Atticus, aged 18.
EDCS-10400428.summary: This inscription records the burial of Atticus, his freedwoman Salviola, and his son Victor, who died at 18.

EDCS-10400429.translation: For Julia Ane, daughter of Sorinus.
EDCS-10400429.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Julia Ane, daughter of Sorinus.

EDCS-10400430.translation: To Rufio, freedman of Publius Licinius Montanus, son of Hautenson, son of Haiscotarris.
EDCS-10400430.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Rufio, a freedman, and specifies his parentage.

EDCS-10400431.translation: While alive, Narcissus, freedman of Primulus, for himself, his wife Julia, and their descendants. May anyone deceased entering this burial place be excluded from this monument and burial spot.
EDCS-10400431.summary: This is a self-dedicated funerary monument for Narcissus, his wife Julia, and their descendants, with a clause prohibiting the burial of others.

EDCS-10400433.translation: Fronto for himself and his wife Grata Pompeia, freedwoman, deceased; for his mother Andreccon, deceased; and for his daughter Procula, deceased. This monument will not pass to an heir, nor to the heir of an heir.
EDCS-10400433.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated by Fronto for himself, his deceased wife, mother, and daughter, with a stipulation against inheritance.

EDCS-10400434.translation: To the divine spirits. For Paula, mother. Primula, Paulus, and Paulinus.
EDCS-10400434.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Primula, Paulus, and Paulinus to their deceased mother, Paula.

EDCS-10400435.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the name and parentage of Primu.

EDCS-10400436.translation: Rufinus, son, arranged for this to be made according to the will for Rufino, son of Silexcon.
EDCS-10400436.summary: This funerary inscription records that Rufinus commissioned the monument in accordance with the will for Rufino.

EDCS-10400437.translation: To Tus, son of Rusticus, and his wife Montana, a place for burial was given to their son.
EDCS-10400437.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription dedicating a burial plot to a son.

EDCS-10400439.translation: To the Divine Shades. Secundus, son of Mundus, and Ingenua, daughter of Calvinius, his wife.
EDCS-10400439.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Secundus and his wife Ingenua.

EDCS-10400440.translation: From Sembecconis, daughter of Herossis, Prima the freedwoman, by her will.
EDCS-10400440.summary: This inscription records a bequest by Prima, a freedwoman, concerning her burial.

EDCS-10400441.translation: Living: Senius, son of Orcolus, for himself, and for his deceased wife Fausta, daughter of Hanabus, and for his daughter Albina, and for his son Albino.
EDCS-10400441.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated by Senius for himself and his family members.

EDCS-10400442.translation: Living: Silvanus, son of Iacessis, for himself, and for his deceased wife Prisca, daughter of Harontarris, and for his living son Proculus, and for his son Propinquus.
EDCS-10400442.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated by Silvanus for himself and his family members.

EDCS-10400443.summary: This inscription seems to be a property marker or a dedication by Valerius Saturninus.

EDCS-10400452.translation: Valeria Severa lived 30 years and died on the 3rd day before the Nones of July in the consulship of Rufinus and Eusebius. Pac [or Vah?] Patroclus the presbyter, for himself in peace.
EDCS-10400452.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valeria Severa, dated by the consuls Rufinus and Eusebius.

EDCS-10400453.translation: Burial of P. Severinus, 15 days before the Kalends of March, in the consulship of Valerius.
EDCS-10400453.summary: This inscription records the burial date of P. Severinus, dated by the consulship of Valerius.

EDCS-10400454.translation: To the god Borienus, Monsus, son of Taurinus, paid his vow.
EDCS-10400454.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Borienus by Monsus.

EDCS-10400455.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Iulius Primilinus [paid his vow or dedicated this].
EDCS-10400455.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Iulius Primilinus.

EDCS-10400456.translation: To the god, Cornelius Faustus [dedicated this].
EDCS-10400456.summary: This inscription records a dedication to a god by Cornelius Faustus.

EDCS-10400457.translation: His son Neuri fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400457.summary: This inscription records that Neuri's son fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-10400459.translation: Rutundus, son of Hontharris, while alive, [dedicated this] for himself and for his wife, Clara, while alive, and for his daughter Rufina, while alive.
EDCS-10400459.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Rutundus for himself, his wife Clara, and his daughter Rufina.

EDCS-10400461.translation: Antonius Vindemialis willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-10400461.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Antonius Vindemialis to Jupiter.

EDCS-10400463.translation: Felicissimus Siradi willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest for the safety of his masters and his own.
EDCS-10400463.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Felicissimus Siradi to Jupiter for the safety of his masters and himself.

EDCS-10400464.translation: Senius Conditus, son of Congus, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400464.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Senius Conditus, son of Congus.

EDCS-10400466.translation: Taurus, son of Sosonnis, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Alardostus.
EDCS-10400466.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Taurus, son of Sosonnis, to the god Alardostus.

EDCS-10400467.translation: Nescato's son Asspercius and his wife.
EDCS-10400467.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or memorial for Asspercius, son of Nescato, and his wife.

EDCS-10400468.translation: Annosus, son of Pompeianus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-10400468.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Annosus, son of Pompeianus, to Jupiter.

EDCS-10400469.translation: Titus Minicius Harbelex willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-10400469.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Titus Minicius Harbelex to Jupiter.

EDCS-10400475.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Andostenus, son of Andosus Bihoxus.
EDCS-10400475.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the deceased Andostenus, son of Andosus Bihoxus.

EDCS-10400477.translation: Baicorrix, a god, son of Hannaxus Axionnis, willingly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400477.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the deity Baicorrix, son of Hannaxus Axionnis.

EDCS-10400478.translation: Bonbelex, son of Harbelexsis, died; his wife Anderexso, daughter of Condannos, placed this.
EDCS-10400478.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Bonbelex, son of Harbelexsis, and was set up by his wife Anderexso.

EDCS-10400479.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valeria, to her dearest husband Silvanus.
EDCS-10400479.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Valeria to her beloved husband Silvanus.

EDCS-10400480.translation: Bonxson, deceased; his wife Edunn Da.
EDCS-10400480.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning the deceased Bonxson and his wife Edunn Da.

EDCS-10400481.translation: For Sabinianus, son of Sabinus. Uria, daughter of Harbelexis, mother.
EDCS-10400481.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Uria, daughter of Harbelexis, to her son Sabinianus.

EDCS-10400482.translation: To Tutela, Bonius, son of Spurius, willingly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400482.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the deity Tutela by Bonius, son of Spurius.

EDCS-10400483.translation: To the god Expercennius Silex, willingly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400483.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the deity Expercennius Silex.

EDCS-10400484.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Silania, daughter of Seranus, and for Faustianus, grandson.
EDCS-10400484.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Silania, daughter of Seranus, and her grandson Faustianus.

EDCS-10400485.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valeria Hermione, to her husband Lucius Titullius Antonius.
EDCS-10400485.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Valeria Hermione to her husband Lucius Titullius Antonius.

EDCS-10400486.translation: Lucius Titullius Antonius [erected this] for his most devoted wife and dearest son Antonianus.
EDCS-10400486.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Titullius Antonius to his wife and son, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10400487.translation: Sulpicius, son of Fortis, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Abelio.
EDCS-10400487.summary: This is a votive inscription from an individual named Sulpicius to the god Abelio, likely dating to the Roman period in Gaul or Hispania.

EDCS-10400488.translation: Hunnu, son of Hulohoxis, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Iscitto.
EDCS-10400488.summary: This is a votive inscription from an individual named Hunnu to the god Iscitto, likely dating to the Roman period in Gaul or Hispania.

EDCS-10400489.translation: Sabinus, son of Mandatus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Iscitto.
EDCS-10400489.summary: This is a votive inscription from an individual named Sabinus to the god Iscitto, likely dating to the Roman period in Gaul or Hispania.

EDCS-10400490.translation: Gaius Montinus Pompeius erected [this] for his most beloved wife, Titullia Antonia, for the departed spirits.
EDCS-10400490.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Montinus Pompeius to his wife Titullia Antonia, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10400491.translation: Cisontes, son of Cissonbonus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Abellio.
EDCS-10400491.summary: This is a votive inscription from an individual named Cisontes to the god Abellio, likely dating to the Roman period in Gaul or Hispania.

EDCS-10400492.translation: Taurinus, son of Bonecon, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Abelio.
EDCS-10400492.summary: This is a votive inscription from an individual named Taurinus to the god Abelio, likely dating to the Roman period in Gaul or Hispania.

EDCS-10400493.translation: For Proculus, son of Pr, and his wife Verana, the Senate and People of Rome wish him good health and prosperity.
EDCS-10400493.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or honorific text for Proculus and his wife Verana, possibly related to public works or civic honor, with an unknown precise date.

EDCS-10400494.translation: For the departed spirits of Valeria Hermione, dearest daughter of Titullia Antonia.
EDCS-10400494.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Valeria Hermione, daughter of Titullia Antonia, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10400495.translation: For the departed spirits of Claudius Laetus and Eresenus, son of Halscon.
EDCS-10400495.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Claudius Laetus and Eresenus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10400496.translation: Bontar, son of Hotarr, to his father Senarr, son of Hotarr, and to his mother Elona, daughter of Senarr, by his will.
EDCS-10400496.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Bontar for his parents, Senarr and Elona, according to a will.

EDCS-10400497.translation: Death of Severus, son of Berhaxsis, for himself, made while alive, and for Exsorata, daughter of Castianus, his wife, and for their son Secundus, and for their mother Anderesena, and for their son Silvinus, and for their daughter Silvina.
EDCS-10400497.summary: This inscription records the deaths of Severus and his family members, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-10400498.translation: Anderitia, daughter of Hanacon, willingly and deservedly paid her vow to the springs.
EDCS-10400498.summary: This is a votive offering by Anderitia to the springs.

EDCS-10400499.translation: Fabia Festa willingly and deservedly paid her vow to the god Ilixon.
EDCS-10400499.summary: This is a votive offering by Fabia Festa to the god Ilixon.

EDCS-10400500.translation: He paid his vow to Ilixo M.
EDCS-10400500.summary: This is a short votive inscription to a deity named Ilixo M.

EDCS-10400501.translation: Secundinus, son of Verecundus, to the god Ilixon.
EDCS-10400501.summary: This is a dedication, likely votive, by Secundinus to the god Ilixon.

EDCS-10400503.translation: Quintus G. Amoenus willingly paid his vow to the mountains.
EDCS-10400503.summary: This is a votive offering by Quintus G. Amoenus to the mountains.

EDCS-10400505.translation: Andem, son of Namron, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the Nymphs.
EDCS-10400505.summary: This is a votive offering by Andem to the Nymphs.

EDCS-10400506.translation: Cassia Touta of Segusiava and others willingly and deservedly paid their vow to the Nymphs.
EDCS-10400506.summary: This is a collective votive offering by Cassia Touta and others to the Nymphs.

EDCS-10400507.translation: Titus Claudius Rufus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the Nymphs.
EDCS-10400507.summary: This is a votive offering by Titus Claudius Rufus to the Nymphs.

EDCS-10400508.translation: To the Nymphs, Fabius gladly paid his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-10400508.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a vow to the Nymphs by Fabius.

EDCS-10400509.translation: To the Nymphs, Lucanus and Erotis gladly paid their vows as was deserved.
EDCS-10400509.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a vow to the Nymphs by Lucanus and Erotis.

EDCS-10400510.translation: To the Nymphs, Manu Sacra and Rutaena gladly paid their vows as was deserved.
EDCS-10400510.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a vow to the Nymphs by Manu Sacra and Rutaena.

EDCS-10400511.translation: To the Nymphs, Montana, daughter of Montanus, gladly paid her vow as was deserved.
EDCS-10400511.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a vow to the Nymphs by Montana, daughter of Montanus.

EDCS-10400512.translation: To the Nymphs, Caius Rufonius Dexter gladly paid his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-10400512.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a vow to the Nymphs by Caius Rufonius Dexter.

EDCS-10400513.translation: To the Nymphs, Caius Valerius Optatus gladly paid his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-10400513.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a vow to the Nymphs by Caius Valerius Optatus.

EDCS-10400514.translation: To the August Nymphs, Valeria Hellas gladly paid her vow as was deserved.
EDCS-10400514.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a vow to the August Nymphs by Valeria Hellas.

EDCS-10400515.translation: The slave-woman gladly paid her vow as was deserved.
EDCS-10400515.summary: This is a votive inscription by an unnamed slave-woman.

EDCS-10400516.translation: The daughter of Virillio gladly paid her vow as was deserved.
EDCS-10400516.summary: This is a votive inscription by an unnamed daughter of Virillio.

EDCS-10400517.translation: To the departed spirits, Aevadia dedicated [this] to her father Hermogenes and [to] her mother Secundina.
EDCS-10400517.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a monument to departed parents, Hermogenes and Secundina, by their daughter Aevadia.

EDCS-10400519.translation: Arixo, a god, freely and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400519.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Arixo, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10400520.translation: Erianos, son of Serio, freely and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars Arixonus.
EDCS-10400520.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Mars Arixonus by Erianos, son of Serio.

EDCS-10400521.translation: Valerius Rusticus, son of Lucius, and his daughter Campana, and his daughter Lucana, daughter of Lucanus, set this up for their departed parents, Lucius Valerius Lucanus and Lucana, daughter of Lucanus.
EDCS-10400521.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by children for their deceased parents.

EDCS-10400522.translation: Antullus, son of Iullinus, [set this up] for Silvana, wife of Sabinus, daughter of Sabinus.
EDCS-10400522.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, for Silvana, wife of Sabinus.

EDCS-10400523.translation: Harsorus, son of Senixso, and his wife Hautense, daughter of Somenaris, and his sons Oxso and Severus, have been buried here, having died; Seranus, son of Harsorus, erected this monument during his lifetime.
EDCS-10400523.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Harsorus and his family, erected by his son Seranus during his lifetime.

EDCS-10400524.translation: Marcus Valerius Potens freely and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Beisirissus.
EDCS-10400524.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Beisirissus by Marcus Valerius Potens.

EDCS-10400525.translation: VNIAXTO, the freedman, freely and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400525.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by a freedman dedicated to UNIAXTO.

EDCS-10400526.translation: Caius Coelius Bassinus freely and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400526.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by Caius Coelius Bassinus.

EDCS-10400527.translation: [Someone], son of Sabinus, freely and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400527.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by an individual identified only as the son of Sabinus.

EDCS-10400529.translation: Sextus Pompeius Sabinus, father, and Serana, daughter of Seranus, [set this up] for their son Sextus Pompeius Sabinianus.
EDCS-10400529.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by parents for their son, Sextus Pompeius Sabinianus.

EDCS-10400531.translation: Festa, a freedwoman, and her children, heirs of Modestus, son of Faustus.
EDCS-10400531.summary: This inscription is an epitaph for Festa and her children, identified as heirs of Modestus, son of Faustus.

EDCS-10400533.translation: Licinius Faustus and Modesta gladly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-10400533.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Licinius Faustus and Modesta.

EDCS-10400534.translation: To the Divine Manes. Crispa, mother, made this for her most devoted daughter Primilla, who lived 4 years, and her granddaughter.
EDCS-10400534.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Primilla, the daughter of Crispa, recording her age and relationship to the dedicator.

EDCS-10400535.translation: Silex to Jupiter Best and Greatest, [dedicated] at Salinis.
EDCS-10400535.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Silex at the location of Salinis.

EDCS-10400536.translation: Lucius Pompeius Paulinianus gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Mountain Gods, to Silvanus, and to Diana.
EDCS-10400536.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated by Lucius Pompeius Paulinianus to various deities including the Mountain Gods, Silvanus, and Diana.

EDCS-10400537.translation: To the mountains of Ageion. Metellinia, daughter of Quintus, gladly fulfilled her vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400537.summary: This is a votive inscription to the mountains of Ageion, erected by Metellinia.

EDCS-10400538.translation: To the god Ageion. The villagers of the ironworkers, from [their] vow.
EDCS-10400538.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Ageion, dedicated by the pagani ferrarienses (villagers of the ironworkers).

EDCS-10400539.translation: To the god Ageion. Paulinus of Taurini gladly fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-10400539.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Ageion, erected by Paulinus of Taurini.

EDCS-10400540.translation: To Ageion the god, Labusius paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10400540.summary: A votive dedication to the god Ageion by Labusius.

EDCS-10400541.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Valeria, daughter of Lucius Vara, paid her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10400541.summary: A votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Valeria.

EDCS-10400542.text_edition: \n Deo Stoloco Decimus Cilius Iustinus votum solvet sic levens sic mereta sic\n
EDCS-10400542.translation: To the god Stolocus, Decimus Cilius Iustinus paid his vow, as he was willing and deserving.
EDCS-10400542.summary: A votive dedication to the god Stolocus by Decimus Cilius Iustinus.

EDCS-10400543.translation: Secundus Sembedonis, on behalf of himself and of the villagers of Aquensium, placed this sacred offering to the numen of Augustus.
EDCS-10400543.summary: A sacred offering to the numen of Augustus by Secundus Sembedonis on behalf of the villagers of Aquensium and himself.

EDCS-10400545.translation: To the Nymphs, for his own health, Severius Seranus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10400545.summary: A votive dedication to the Nymphs for health by Severius Seranus.

EDCS-10400546.translation: To Mars the Unconquered, Gaius Minicius Potitus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10400546.summary: A votive dedication to Mars Invictus by Gaius Minicius Potitus.

EDCS-10400547.translation: To the August Nymphs, Lucius Victorius Censorinus, son of Gaius, and Bihossius Amianti, and Pompeia, daughter of [---], and Verinia Vera paid their vows willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10400547.summary: A joint votive dedication to the August Nymphs by Lucius Victorius Censorinus, Bihossius Amianti, Pompeia, and Verinia Vera.

EDCS-10400548.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for T(itus) Porcius Optatus.
EDCS-10400548.summary: A tomb inscription for T. Porcius Optatus dedicated to the Manes.

EDCS-10400549.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Caius Valerius Valerianus Sanctus, a most distinguished man, quaestor of the province of Baetica, his tutor, the most distinguished boy Iulius Sanctus, his son, arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-10400549.summary: A tomb inscription for C. Valerius Valerianus Sanctus, a former quaestor of Baetica, arranged by his son and tutor Iulius Sanctus.

EDCS-10400550.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Primulus, son of Primus, for himself and his wife and his most dutiful son Verecundus.
EDCS-10400550.summary: A tomb inscription for Primulus, his wife, and his son Verecundus.

EDCS-10400551.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury by Caius.

EDCS-10400552.translation: Modesta, daughter of Modestus, set this up for her wife, Iuliana, daughter of Odosius.
EDCS-10400552.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Modesta, daughter of Modestus, for her wife Iuliana.

EDCS-10400561.translation: Sacred to Herauscorritse by Gaius Valerius Valerianus.
EDCS-10400561.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a deity named Herauscorritse by Gaius Valerius Valerianus.

EDCS-10400562.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Marcus Silvanius Silvinus willingly pays his vow as is deserved.
EDCS-10400562.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Marcus Silvanius Silvinus.

EDCS-10400563.translation: To the Most Holy Tutela, Chrysanthus [dedicated this].
EDCS-10400563.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Tutela by Chrysanthus.

EDCS-10400564.translation: Verus, who served as flamen, duumvir, quaestor, and master of the district, having fulfilled his duty as legate to Augustus, obtained permission for the nine peoples to join the Gauls. Returned to the city, he dedicates this altar to the genius of the district.
EDCS-10400564.summary: This inscription records Verus dedicating an altar to the genius of the district after holding several civic and military offices.

EDCS-10400566.translation: Aemilius Placidus of Pompaelo, aged 23, lies here.
EDCS-10400566.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Aemilius Placidus, who died at the age of 23.

EDCS-10400567.translation: Caius Antonius Blandus and Caius Antonius Valentinus, grandsons and heirs of Antonia Secundina, and Lucius Cornelius Valentinus, their adoptive father, had this erected in accordance with the testament of Antonia Secundina, mother of Caius Antonius Blandus, and of the same Secundina.
EDCS-10400567.summary: This funerary monument was erected by the heirs and adoptive father of Antonia Secundina, in accordance with her will.

EDCS-10400568.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the name of Gaius Valerius Silvanus, possibly an epitaph or dedication.

EDCS-10400569.translation: To Valeria Prisca, Sextus Valerius [dedicated this].
EDCS-10400569.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial for Valeria Prisca by Sextus Valerius.

EDCS-10400571.translation: Eizia died on the seventh day before the Ides of May.
EDCS-10400571.summary: This is a brief funerary notice recording the death date of Eizia.

EDCS-10400572.translation: To the god Mars, Lucius Attius Sabinianus [dedicated this].
EDCS-10400572.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mars by Lucius Attius Sabinianus.

EDCS-10400573.translation: To Mars the Lord, Licinius Myrtillus willingly pays his vow as is deserved.
EDCS-10400573.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mars Dominus by Licinius Myrtillus.

EDCS-10400574.translation: Berullius, slave of Tiberius Claudius Sabinianus, for himself and his family, willingly pays his vow to Mars Lilhunno as is deserved.
EDCS-10400574.summary: This votive inscription to Mars Lilhunno was made by Berullius, a slave, for himself and his family.

EDCS-10400575.translation: As a vow to Mars Lehunno for his own health and that of his family, Tiberius Claudius Faustinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400575.summary: An altar dedicated to Mars Lehunno by Tiberius Claudius Faustinus for his family's health.

EDCS-10400576.translation: To Mars Lehunno, Tiberius Claudius Sotericus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow for his son Domesticus.
EDCS-10400576.summary: An altar dedicated to Mars Lehunno by Tiberius Claudius Sotericus for his son.

EDCS-10400578.translation: For the health of Lucius Attius Secundus, Lucius Attius Vitalis willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400578.summary: An altar dedicated to an unknown deity by Lucius Attius Vitalis for the health of Lucius Attius Secundus.

EDCS-10400581.summary: An incomplete inscription possibly dedicated to Quirinus.

EDCS-10400584.summary: A fragment of an inscription with illegible text.

EDCS-10400585.translation: To the god Apollo, Marcianus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400585.summary: An altar dedicated to Apollo by Marcianus.

EDCS-10400586.translation: To Hercules Tolliandosso the Invincible, Primigenius, son of Sembius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400586.summary: An altar dedicated to Hercules Tolliandosso the Invincible by Primigenius.

EDCS-10400587.translation: Sacred to Minerva, Marcus Attius Sabinianus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400587.summary: An altar dedicated to Minerva by Marcus Attius Sabinianus.

EDCS-10400591.translation: To the goddess Tutela, Nexius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10400591.summary: An altar dedicated to the goddess Tutela by Nexius.

EDCS-10400592.translation: To the tutelary deity of this place, Titulinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10400592.summary: This is a votive inscription by Titulinus to a local tutelary deity, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10400593.translation: Ingenua willingly and deservedly paid her vow to the Winds.
EDCS-10400593.summary: This is a votive inscription by Ingenua to the Winds, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10400594.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of Domitia Charitina, Aurelius Tertinus, centurion of the 30th Legion, for his most deserving wife, who deserved so well of me.
EDCS-10400594.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Domitia Charitina, dedicated by her husband Aurelius Tertinus, a centurion, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10400595.translation: [...]uleius, while alive, a soldier of the Sixth Legion, a veteran, and for Silabina, daughter of Bortossus, and for his own family.
EDCS-10400595.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a veteran of the Sixth Legion and his family, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10400596.translation: To Gaius Afranus Graphicus, freedman of Clarus, scribe, instructor, and player of the game of latrunculi, curator of Roman citizens, and to Tertulla, his wife, according to his will.
EDCS-10400596.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Afranus Graphicus, a freedman who held various civic and professional roles, and his wife Tertulla, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10400597.summary: This is likely a funerary or dedicatory inscription mentioning Gaius Antistius Severus, who held the priestly office of flamen, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10400600.translation: Tertulla, mother, made this for Gaius Afranius (?) Clarus and [Afranius] Tertullus.
EDCS-10400600.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument set up by Tertulla for her deceased sons, Gaius Afranius (?) Clarus and Afranius Tertullus.

EDCS-10400601.translation: While alive, Albinus, freedman of Silvinus, for himself and for Cambuxa, a freedwoman.
EDCS-10400601.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Albinus, a freedman, for himself and his freedwoman partner, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10400603.translation: To the Divine Shades of Gaius Antistius Arullianus.
EDCS-10400603.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Antistius Arullianus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10400604.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Antistia Talseia, likely from a tombstone, with an unknown approximate date.

EDCS-10400607.translation: To the Divine Shades of Balexeia, daughter of Censorinus, mother, [dedicated by?] Gaius? Julius Ce[---].
EDCS-10400607.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Balexeia, daughter of Censorinus and a mother, with a partially preserved dedication, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10400608.translation: While alive, Belexeia, daughter of Dunai, for herself and for Macro, son of Bersegius, her husband, and for Sabina, daughter of Macro. This monument shall not follow an heir.
EDCS-10400608.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Belexeia for herself, her husband Macro, and their daughter Sabina, stipulating that the burial plot is not inheritable, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10400609.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Secundus, to his wife Belissima.
EDCS-10400609.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Secundus to his deceased wife Belissima.

EDCS-10400611.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication from Toutaronia to her son Dunaio, possibly on a funerary monument.

EDCS-10400613.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Faustae, daughter of Orcuarius.
EDCS-10400613.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Faustae, daughter of Orcuarius.

EDCS-10400614.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Ligurius, having been entreated, [erected this] for his dearest Faustilla.
EDCS-10400614.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Faustilla, set up by her husband Lucius Ligurius, likely from a tombstone, with an unknown approximate date.

EDCS-10400616.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a funerary dedication or an epitaph, with an unknown approximate date.

EDCS-10400617.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication from Aelia Pancarpe to her husband.

EDCS-10400618.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely commemorating Lucius Julius Flore[--].

EDCS-10400619.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Lucius Julius Helicon, her most cherished husband. Iulia Onesime [dedicates this].
EDCS-10400619.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulia Onesime to her beloved husband, Lucius Julius Helicon.

EDCS-10400620.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Lucius Julius Onesicrates, her most dutiful son. Iulia Onesime [dedicates this].
EDCS-10400620.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulia Onesime to her dutiful son, Lucius Julius Onesicrates.

EDCS-10400621.translation: To Lucius Julius Pal[--], freedman of Lucius, and to Gaius Iulius F[--] and Iulia [---] of the Iulii.
EDCS-10400621.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication potentially honoring multiple individuals from the Iulius family.

EDCS-10400623.translation: To Titullus Seranus, his son, and to Tutiluxsa Sole[--], daughter of Mutius, wife of the son.
EDCS-10400623.summary: This inscription seems to record a dedication to Titullus Seranus and his wife, possibly as a family monument.

EDCS-10400625.translation: Laurcus, son of Montanus, while alive, [erected this] for himself, and for his mother Prima Justa, daughter of Faustus, his wife Festa, his deceased daughter Laurina, and their freedmen and descendants.
EDCS-10400625.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Laurcus for his family, including his wife and deceased daughter, likely from a tombstone, with an unknown approximate date.

EDCS-10400626.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Macria Prisca, his daughter, had this made for Macrius Serenus, her father.
EDCS-10400626.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Macria Prisca to her father, Macrius Serenus.

EDCS-10400627.text_edition: \n Vivus Martial<i=L>s Quadrat<i=L> filius sib<i=L> et @(obitae) Maxumillae Iul<i=L>i filiae uxori et natis suis \n
EDCS-10400627.translation: Martialis Quadratus, while alive, for himself, for his daughter Maxumilla Iulia, his wife, and for his children.
EDCS-10400627.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Martialis Quadratus, who set it up for himself, his wife, and children.

EDCS-10400628.translation: In good health, Matico, son of Ocellio, for himself and his family.
EDCS-10400628.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Matico, son of Ocellio, set up for himself and his family while alive.

EDCS-10400630.translation: To Gaius Octavius Faustus, son of Ahoissus, according to the will, by the authority of Saleduna Illa, his wife, daughter of Illa.
EDCS-10400630.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Gaius Octavius Faustus, established by his wife according to the terms of his will.

EDCS-10400631.translation: To the living Oiso, daughter of Oll[---], Caius Iulius Coera[nus] made this.
EDCS-10400631.summary: This funerary inscription records that Caius Iulius Coera[nus] made the monument for the living Oiso, daughter of Oll[---].

EDCS-10400632.translation: Osa, daughter of Herr[i], and Taros, son of Herr[i].
EDCS-10400632.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records the names of Osa and Taros, possibly siblings, both children of Herr[i].

EDCS-10400635.translation: [---] for the daughter of Ingenui[us?] and for Rusticus, son of [---]di.
EDCS-10400635.summary: This fragmented inscription records a dedication to an unnamed daughter of Ingenui[us?] and Rusticus, son of [---]di.

EDCS-10400636.translation: In good health, Severa, daughter of Tautinnus, for herself and her family.
EDCS-10400636.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Severa, daughter of Tautinnus, set up for herself and her family while alive.

EDCS-10400638.translation: In good health, Taurinus, son of Deri, for himself and Orguarra, daughter of Taurus, his wife, and for his sons Sambus and Tauricus, and his heirs. Let them have the right to enter up to my monument, 10 feet wide. This monument of ours shall not follow the heir, nor the heir of the heir.
EDCS-10400638.summary: This funerary inscription is set up by Taurinus, son of Deri, for himself, his wife, his sons, and his heirs, specifying burial rights and restrictions.

EDCS-10400640.translation: To Torsteginnus, son of Urupatis, and to Sabina, daughter of Primus, his wife, and to Verecunda, his daughter, and their family, according to the will.
EDCS-10400640.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication to Torsteginnus, his wife Sabina, and daughter Verecunda, established according to a will.

EDCS-10400641.translation: How sweet you were, how kind, who while alive lay in my bosom, always aware of sleep and bed. Oh, it was done badly, Myia, that you perished. If anyone approached, you would bark. Rival of your mistress, licentious one. Oh, it was done badly, Myia, that you perished. The tomb now holds you deep, unaware. You can neither be fierce nor jump, nor shine for me with sweet bites.
EDCS-10400641.summary: This is an epitaph for a beloved dog named Myia, mourning her death and recalling her affectionate and protective nature.

EDCS-10400665.translation: Died with good memory Brittula on the 18th day before the Kalends of April in the third year of the reign of the lord.
EDCS-10400665.summary: This is an epitaph recording the death of Brittula, specifying the date and the regnal year, likely from a tombstone, with an unknown approximate date.

EDCS-10400666.translation: The passing of Heraclia of good memory, after the Kalends of July, on the fifth day, in the sixth year of the reign of our lord.
EDCS-10400666.summary: This is an epitaph recording the death of Heraclia, specifying the date and the regnal year, likely from a tombstone, with an unknown approximate date.

EDCS-10400667.translation: Died with good memory Antonianus on the 22nd day before the Kalends of December in the ninth year of the reign of our lord.
EDCS-10400667.summary: This is an epitaph recording the death of Antonianus, specifying the date and the regnal year, likely from a tombstone, with an unknown approximate date.

EDCS-10400668.translation: Here lies Ursinicus, a servant of Christ, innocent and a foreigner, aged 8 years, 2 months, and 10 days.
