EDCS-10401036.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sunutia Urbana, set up by her husband and former master, Sunutius Hippolytus.

EDCS-10401038.translation: To the Divine Shades; Marcus Calventius Sabinianus, while alive, for himself and his wife Tarquinia Fastina.
EDCS-10401038.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Calventius Sabinianus and his wife Tarquinia Fastina, set up by Sabinianus during his lifetime.

EDCS-10401039.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Anaxagoras erected this for his wife Tatinia.
EDCS-10401039.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his deceased wife, Tatinia.

EDCS-10401040.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Priscilla, who died at sixteen years of age, daughter of Perpetuus. Calvilinus Serdi dedicated this at his own expense.
EDCS-10401040.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Calvilinus Serdi for Priscilla, the sixteen-year-old daughter of Perpetuus.

EDCS-10401041.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Trilicius, deceased, aged 35. Pixticenus had this erected.
EDCS-10401041.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Pixticenus for Trilicius, who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-10401043.summary: This inscription likely records a family name or a series of individuals named Valerius Pri.

EDCS-10401044.summary: This is a memorial inscription dedicated to a person named Valeria.

EDCS-10401045.translation: To Valeria Hiberina. Her mother Quartilla set this up, and also to her most devoted husband Publius Lucius. She set this up.
EDCS-10401045.summary: A funerary monument set up by a mother for her daughter Valeria Hiberina and her husband.

EDCS-10401046.translation: To the memory of Veneria, deceased, aged...
EDCS-10401046.summary: This is a partial memorial inscription for a deceased person named Veneria.

EDCS-10401047.translation: To the divine spirits, for the memory of Veneria, deceased, aged 25.
EDCS-10401047.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of the deceased Veneria, aged 25.

EDCS-10401048.translation: To the divine spirits. Her children Verecunda donated (this).
EDCS-10401048.summary: A funerary inscription stating that Verecunda's children donated the monument.

EDCS-10401049.translation: To the divine spirits. Vervicia, deceased, aged 30, provided for this; her mother donated and set this up.
EDCS-10401049.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that Vervicia's mother provided for and donated the monument for her deceased daughter, aged 30.

EDCS-10401050.translation: Of Viator, deceased, aged 61. His wife set this up. A citizen of Vienna?
EDCS-10401050.summary: A funerary epitaph for Viator, who died at 61, set up by his wife, possibly a citizen of Vienna.

EDCS-10401051.translation: To the divine spirits. To Victa.
EDCS-10401051.summary: A brief funerary inscription dedicated to the deceased Victa.

EDCS-10401052.translation: To the divine spirits. Vindicianus, deceased, aged 70.
EDCS-10401052.summary: A funerary inscription for Vindicianus, who died at 70.

EDCS-10401053.translation: To the divine spirits and for the memory of Vipsania Censoria.
EDCS-10401053.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Vipsania Censoria.

EDCS-10401054.translation: To the divine spirits. Volucer, brother of Constantius, set this up.
EDCS-10401054.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Volucer for his brother Constantius.

EDCS-10401055.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ulattia Venantia, who died at the age of 26.

EDCS-10401056.translation: To the shades of the departed, her husband placed this for Ursa, deceased at 33 years of age.
EDCS-10401056.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Ursa, erected by her husband.

EDCS-10401057.summary: A fragmented funerary epitaph, likely for a woman named S(e)lumia.

EDCS-10401066.translation: [...]ae Etta[...] placed this for herself while alive.
EDCS-10401066.summary: A funerary epitaph for Etta, who dedicated it for herself during her lifetime.

EDCS-10401076.translation: He lived 24 years, 3 months, 5 days before the Kalends of the reign of our lord Turismund.
EDCS-10401076.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of an individual who died before the Kalends of a date during the reign of Turismund.

EDCS-10401077.translation: Here rests with good remembrance the humble Christian Mommolenus, who lived approximately seventy years, in whom there was no malice, who was cheerful without anger. He received his passing on the 6th day before the Ides of August, where he spent seven days in Augusta, in the 5th year of the reign of our lord King Chlodovei.
EDCS-10401077.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Mommolenus, a humble Christian who lived about seventy years and died on August 8th in the 5th regnal year of King Chlodovei.

EDCS-10401078.translation: Here rests in peace. Aucilia Pascasia, may the Holy Spirit help.
EDCS-10401078.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aucilia Pascasia, invoking the Holy Spirit.

EDCS-10401081.translation: Born on the Kalends of April, died on the same day. Ous, son of Fotconi, Anecdotus, in the first indiction. Placed.
EDCS-10401081.summary: This inscription records the birth and death of Ous, son of Fotconi, on the same day, April 1st, within the first indiction.

EDCS-10401084.translation: Burial of Adelfa, aged 3 years and three days, after the sixth consulship of our lord Honorius Augustus. Placed by Maurusius, father, and Ursa, mother.
EDCS-10401084.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Adelfa, aged three years and three days, placed by her parents Maurusius and Ursa, after the sixth consulship of Honorius Augustus.

EDCS-10401085.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Ivenes, from the temple of Jupiter, for himself and his family.
EDCS-10401085.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deified dead by Ivenes, likely from the vicinity of a temple of Jupiter.

EDCS-10401086.translation: Capito, son of Lucius, and his wife Iulia, gladly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to the August Iunoes, [dedicating] a portico and a wall.
EDCS-10401086.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Iunoes, comprising a portico and wall, by Capito and his wife Iulia.

EDCS-10401087.translation: Maglomatunius Atto, a marble worker, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10401087.summary: This is a votive inscription by Maglomatunius Atto, a marble worker.

EDCS-10401088.translation: Marcus Claudius Severus, the aedile, by permission of the council of the Nitobroges state, placed this at his own expense, for the divine spirit of Augustus.
EDCS-10401088.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a public work by Marcus Claudius Severus, an aedile, funded by himself, with the permission of the local council.

EDCS-10401090.translation: For the health of Claudius Rufus.
EDCS-10401090.summary: This is a dedication or dedication fragment for the well-being of Claudius Rufus.

EDCS-10401091.translation: Silvinus, son of Scipio, priest, gave a basin to the Augustan Tutela.
EDCS-10401091.summary: This is a dedication of a basin to the goddess Tutela Augusta by Silvinus, a priest.

EDCS-10401092.translation: Lucius Valerius Communis, a citizen of Aquae, placed a temple with its statue, fulfilling a vow, gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-10401092.summary: This inscription records the erection of a temple and statue by Lucius Valerius Communis, a citizen of Aquae, in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-10401093.translation: The people of Senonia dedicated this to Claudius Lupicinus, a most distinguished consular man, their patron, for his illustrious merits.
EDCS-10401093.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by the people of Senonia to their patron, Claudius Lupicinus, a distinguished former consul.

EDCS-10401094.translation: The people of Autissiodurum wish that the province, fortunate through you, might decree to Claudius, a most distinguished consular man, for your so great merits, tables and statues.
EDCS-10401094.summary: This inscription expresses the desire of the people of Autissiodurum for the provincial council to honor Claudius, a former consul, with decrees and statues for his significant merits.

EDCS-10401096.translation: Iulius Icco, son of Atto, a soldier of the I Alpine Cohort, 55 years old, 35 years in service, is buried here; his heirs piously made this.
EDCS-10401096.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulius Icco, a soldier of the I Alpine Cohort, who served for 35 years and died at 55.

EDCS-10401097.translation: Sextus Valerius Maximus, son of Sextus, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the 1st Class Cohort, in the centuria of Petronius, aged 20, with 20 years of service, is buried here. Caius Valerius Adiutor [dedicated this] to his most devoted brother.
EDCS-10401097.summary: This is a tombstone for Sextus Valerius Maximus, a soldier in the Roman navy, erected by his brother.

EDCS-10401098.translation: Valerius Gallus Tutus, of the Voltinia tribe, son of Lucius, a soldier of the 1st Class Cohort, aged 22 years and 9 days, is buried here.
EDCS-10401098.summary: This is a tombstone for Valerius Gallus Tutus, a soldier in the Roman navy.

EDCS-10401099.translation: Livia Vera, daughter of Quadratus, placed the doorways and doorposts of stone at her own expense.
EDCS-10401099.summary: This is a dedication for building materials (doorways and doorposts) provided by Livia Vera.

EDCS-10401101.translation: and would not dare; he painted the rights/laws on the ground with colors, Conculcanus.
EDCS-10401101.summary: This inscription is too fragmented to provide a meaningful summary.

EDCS-10401102.translation: to Rio, son of Caius, son of Marcius, the Greek.
EDCS-10401102.summary: This inscription is too fragmented to provide a meaningful summary.

EDCS-10401103.translation: aged 25, [dedicated this] to Ios, son of Iulius Iedomeneus, her husband, who showed her every obedience, out of his devotion.
EDCS-10401103.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, for a husband named Ios, honoring his devotion to his wife.

EDCS-10401104.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Pac[...]
EDCS-10401104.summary: This is the beginning of a funerary inscription, addressing the Di Manes.

EDCS-10401105.translation: Priscus, son of Timotheus, made [this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-10401105.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Priscus for himself and his family.

EDCS-10401108.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Valerius Martialis, and his freedmen Hermes and Mercurius.
EDCS-10401108.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Di Manes, mentioning Lucius Valerius Martialis and his freedmen.

EDCS-10401113.translation: And to the god Apollo Cobledulitavus, Marcus Pompeius Libo, son of Gaius Pompeius Sanctus, a priest of the Arenses, the priest of the Arenses, restored at his own expense the temple of the goddess Tutela and the public baths, both of which had formerly fallen into ruin through age. He paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10401113.summary: An inscription recording the restoration of a temple to the goddess Tutela and public baths by Marcus Pompeius Libo, a local priest, likely in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10401117.translation: To Jupiter Propitious, Augustus, protector of the people of Vesunna. Caius Pompeius Sextus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10401117.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter Propitious, dedicated by Caius Pompeius Sextus.

EDCS-10401128.translation: Secundus, freedman of Sottus, dedicated this at his own expense to the August Tutela Vesunnia.
EDCS-10401128.summary: This is a dedication to a protective deity by a freedman, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10401131.translation: Tiberius Claudius Comeliddus, son of Tiberius Claudius Vitalis, willingly fulfilled his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-10401131.summary: This is a votive inscription by Tiberius Claudius Comeliddus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401132.translation: To Annibertus, the centenarian, from Pedatura of the Franks of Vilatessa.
EDCS-10401132.summary: This is likely a funerary or commemorative inscription for Annibertus, a centenarian, with tribal affiliations.

EDCS-10401133.translation: Iulia Prisca, daughter of Caius, dedicated this at her own expense; Caius Iulius Maxsimus, a soldier, her brother, also contributed.
EDCS-10401133.summary: This is a dedication made by a sister, with a contribution from her brother who was a soldier, suggesting a family memorial or religious offering.

EDCS-10401134.text_edition: \n COR Aulus Pomp Dumnomotus tribunus militum legionis IV Scythicae praefectus fabrum amphitheatrum cum ornamentis omnibus de sua pecunia dedit Aulus Pomp Auli Pomp Tertulli filius s perficiendum curavit idemque dedicavit\n
EDCS-10401134.translation: Aulus Pomp Dumnomotus, son of Aulus Pomp Tertullus, tribune of the soldiers of the IV Scythica legion and prefect of the engineers, dedicated the amphitheater with all its furnishings at his own expense, and saw to its completion and dedicated it himself.
EDCS-10401134.summary: An inscription recording the dedication of an amphitheater by Aulus Pomp Dumnomotus, a military officer, likely in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10401137.translation: Titus Ligurius Tutor, son of Titus Ligurius Masculus, undertook the work of constructing this for the curator of the Roman citizens.
EDCS-10401137.summary: This records the completion of a public work or monument by Titus Ligurius Tutor, on behalf of a curator of Roman citizens.

EDCS-10401138.translation: Lucius Marullius Aeternus, son of Lucius Marullius Arabus, of the tribe Quirina, twice chief magistrate, gave the water supply and its conduits at his own expense.
EDCS-10401138.summary: An inscription recording the provision of water supply and its infrastructure by Lucius Marullius Aeternus, a local magistrate, likely in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10401141.translation: Publius Vinicius Secundus, son of Publius, of the tribe Papiria, aedile, twice chief magistrate, quaestor of the colony Colonia Iulia Paterna Claudia Narbonensis Martius, [dedicated] at his own expense.
EDCS-10401141.summary: An inscription listing the offices held by Publius Vinicius Secundus and stating he made a dedication at his own expense in Narbo Martius, likely in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10401150.translation: To the divine shades and to the memory of Apollinaris, the stable-keeper.
EDCS-10401150.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Apollinaris, who was a stable-keeper.

EDCS-10401152.translation: and to the memory of Amoris, of Lucius Antonius.
EDCS-10401152.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription, continuing a dedication to the memory of Amoris.

EDCS-10401153.translation: To the divine shades, Antimus dedicates this for Antiopes.
EDCS-10401153.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Antimus makes a dedication to the divine shades for Antiopes.

EDCS-10401154.translation: To the divine shades. Gnatusius, deceased, aged 25, his mother Secundina dedicated this at her own expense.
EDCS-10401154.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gnatusius, who died at age 25, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-10401155.translation: Aurelius Felicianus, her son, arranged for this to the divine shades of Artelia Sabina.
EDCS-10401155.summary: This is a funerary inscription arranged by Aurelius Felicianus for his mother, Artelia Sabina.

EDCS-10401156.translation: To the Divine Shades of Aurelius Primitivus.
EDCS-10401156.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Aurelius Primitivus.

EDCS-10401157.translation: To the Divine Shades of Tiberius Claudius.
EDCS-10401157.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Tiberius Claudius.

EDCS-10401158.summary: This inscription marks the tomb of Caletia.

EDCS-10401159.translation: To the Divine Shades and the memory of Celsus.
EDCS-10401159.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Celsus.

EDCS-10401160.translation: To the Divine Shades and the memory of Cornelia Reveta, formerly...
EDCS-10401160.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Cornelia Reveta.

EDCS-10401162.summary: This inscription appears to be part of a larger dedication, possibly funerary, to Flavius Charito.

EDCS-10401163.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the name Quintus Iulius and his father's name or a cognomen.

EDCS-10401164.translation: To the Divine Shades and memory of Crescens, son of Gaius Iulius Adiutor, of the voting tribe Quirina.
EDCS-10401164.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Crescens, son of Gaius Iulius Adiutor, indicating his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-10401165.translation: To Ate, mother, Caius Iulius Ulattius.
EDCS-10401165.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Caius Iulius Ulattius to his mother, Ate.

EDCS-10401166.summary: A fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary epitaph for Iulia Adruppa.

EDCS-10401167.translation: To the Divine Shades and the memory of Iulia Illia.
EDCS-10401167.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Iulia Illia.

EDCS-10401168.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld: For Julia Luguselva, my wife, and for my parents-in-law, Julius Armeni[us] and Julia Sacrina, Pompeius Paternus [erected this].
EDCS-10401168.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Pompeius Paternus for his wife and parents-in-law, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401169.translation: Livius Aesopus dedicated this from his own resources.
EDCS-10401169.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by Livius Aesopus for himself or a relative, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401171.translation: For Mamma and her own people.
EDCS-10401171.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription dedicating a monument to Mamma and her family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401172.translation: Senocarus set up this monument for his wife, Marulla, from his own resources.
EDCS-10401172.summary: This funerary inscription records the monument erected by Senocarus for his wife Marulla, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401175.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld and to the memory of Nonna.
EDCS-10401175.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Nonna, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401177.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld: For Pompeius Phoebus.
EDCS-10401177.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Pompeius Phoebus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401178.translation: Pompeius Dapsilis and Priscus dedicated this from their own resources to Gaius Pompeius Silvinus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-10401178.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Pompeius Dapsilis and Priscus for Gaius Pompeius Silvinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401179.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld and to the memory of Pompeia Nammiola.
EDCS-10401179.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Pompeia Nammiola, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401180.translation: Aulus Hirtius Pulcher to his wife, Pompeia Restituta, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-10401180.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Aulus Hirtius Pulcher to his wife, Pompeia Restituta, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401183.translation: Marcus Sulpicius, son of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe, greets [you].
EDCS-10401183.summary: This is a dedication or an epitaph, possibly a greeting, for Marcus Sulpicius, son of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401185.summary: This is a very brief inscription likely from a tombstone, identifying Verecundus as a fellow slave.

EDCS-10401200.translation: In the name of Christ, Bishop Saffarius built the house of God.
EDCS-10401200.summary: This inscription records Bishop Saffarius building a church, likely in the early Christian period.

EDCS-10401201.translation: Recessio, of good memory, having performed (this) for 7 days in October, (lived) 43 years.
EDCS-10401201.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death and possibly the duration of a specific action or office for a person named Recessio.

EDCS-10401202.translation: With good memory, for Victoria, most distinguished lady, January 22nd.
EDCS-10401202.summary: A dedication or memorial, possibly funerary, for Victoria, dated by month and day.

EDCS-10401203.translation: Cintugenus and Catius, sons, paid their vow willingly and deservedly to Jupiter Augustus.
EDCS-10401203.summary: This dedicatory inscription records two individuals, Cintugenus and Catius, fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Augustus, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401204.translation: Caius Secondius Florus, son of Secondus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Minerva in Magirra.
EDCS-10401204.summary: This dedicatory inscription records Caius Secondius Florus fulfilling a vow to Minerva, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401205.translation: Vegetus Creticus, a freedman, paid his vow willingly and deservedly to Mercury.
EDCS-10401205.summary: This dedicatory inscription records the freedman Vegetus Creticus fulfilling a vow to Mercury, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401218.translation: To Drusus Germanicus Caesar, Gaius Julius Congonnetodubnus, son of (tribe) Voltinia, Victor, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10401218.summary: This is a dedication to Drusus Caesar, likely made by Gaius Julius Victor, a Roman citizen from the Voltinia tribe.

EDCS-10401220.translation: To Gaius Julius Agedilus, son of Fabius, Macro from the territory of the Santones, a duplicarius of the Ala Atectorigiana Gallorum, having completed 32 years of service, a recalled veteran of the Divi Augusti, honoured with a DC (coinage) for the Caesares, DC for the Raeti, with a shield from the fortress of Ircavium, and with golden torcs and armlets, awarded by his fellow soldiers, his heirs Julia Matrona, daughter (of C. Iulius Primulus) and Gaius Julius Primulus, freedman, had this made in accordance with his will.
EDCS-10401220.summary: This epitaph honors Gaius Julius Macro, a veteran soldier from the Santones who served for 32 years and received military decorations, with his heirs ensuring his burial monument was erected.

EDCS-10401221.translation: To Gaius Julius Victor, son of Congonnetodubnus, grandson of Agedomopatis, a prefect of craftsmen, tribune of the soldiers of the First Cohort of Belgae, and priest of Rome and of Augustus at Confluentes, Gaius Julius, son of Voltinia.
EDCS-10401221.summary: This elaborate funerary inscription honors Gaius Julius Victor, detailing his military and civic offices, and is set up by his father.

EDCS-10401226.translation: Aurelia Potentina set this up for the departed spirits and the memory of her husband, Iustinius Paternus, a veteran of the First Legion Minervia.
EDCS-10401226.summary: This funerary inscription records Aurelia Potentina setting up a monument for her deceased husband, Iustinius Paternus, a veteran.

EDCS-10401227.translation: To Gaius Julius Marinus, son of Gaius Julius Ricoverugus, of the Voltinian tribe, first Augustal flamen, curator of Roman citizens, quaestor, vergobretus, Julia Marina, his daughter.
EDCS-10401227.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Julius Marinus, detailing his significant religious and civic offices within a Romanized Gallic context, and is set up by his daughter.

EDCS-10401234.translation: The husband, a deputy imperial dispenser, set this up for his most beloved wife; the husband, a deputy imperial dispenser, set this up for his most beloved wife.
EDCS-10401234.summary: This funerary inscription, which is repeated for emphasis, records a deputy imperial dispenser setting up a monument for his wife.

EDCS-10401235.translation: To the divine spirits and the eternal memory of Diceratus, a citizen of Remi.
EDCS-10401235.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Diceratus, a citizen of Remi, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401236.translation: To the divine spirits and the eternal memory of Ianuaris, of the Nervian nation, aged 35. His colleagues, who were paid laborers in the treasury, set this up.
EDCS-10401236.summary: This funerary inscription records the colleagues of Ianuaris, a 35-year-old Nervian laborer in the treasury, setting up a monument to his memory.

EDCS-10401237.translation: For the perpetual security of Marcus Vipstanus Sabinus, the banker. Successus, his freedman, and Sulpicius Privatus [made this].
EDCS-10401237.summary: This inscription records the establishment of something for the perpetual security of Marcus Vipstanus Sabinus, a banker, by his freedman Successus and Sulpicius Privatus.

EDCS-10401239.translation: To the divine spirits and for his own descendants. Marcus Aemilius Paternus and Lucius Aemilius Severus made this for Lucius Aemilius Paternus, son of Verter, and his descendants.
EDCS-10401239.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Aemilius Paternus and Lucius Aemilius Severus for Lucius Aemilius Paternus and his descendants.

EDCS-10401240.summary: This very short inscription seems to be a dedication or memorial to Lucius Paunus, with the initial 'A AT' possibly representing deities or a shortened phrase.

EDCS-10401242.translation: Catus, freedman of Vivus, [set this up] for himself while alive, and for his descendants. LCC I.
EDCS-10401242.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Catus, a freedman, for himself and his descendants, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10401243.translation: To the divine spirits. The mother made this for her daughter, Claudia Amanda.
EDCS-10401243.summary: This is a funerary inscription where a mother dedicated a monument to her daughter, Claudia Amanda.

EDCS-10401244.translation: To the divine spirits and the memory of Claudius, freedman.
EDCS-10401244.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Claudius, a freedman.

EDCS-10401245.translation: To the divine spirits and to the eternal memory of her husband, Claudius Rufus.
EDCS-10401245.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a wife to the eternal memory of her husband, Claudius Rufus.

EDCS-10401246.translation: To the divine spirits and to eternal memory. Primus, son of Corentius, most dutiful, saw to the setting up of this monument for Corritia Aetunessa.
EDCS-10401246.summary: This funerary inscription records Primus, son of Corentius, dedicating a monument to Corritia Aetunessa.

EDCS-10401247.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Divixta placed the monument.

EDCS-10401248.translation: To the Divine Shades. Divixta, daughter of Divixtus, [placed this] for her little grandson Frontonis, her husband.
EDCS-10401248.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a husband and grandson by Divixta.

EDCS-10401249.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Dumnomotus.

EDCS-10401251.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of FVLIINRE. Campanus, her husband, placed this.
EDCS-10401251.summary: This funerary inscription records Campanus dedicating a monument for his wife, FVLIINRE.

EDCS-10401252.translation: To the Divine Shades, while alive Caius Iulius Aemuli Larginus consecrated the tombs with the larger garden, as it is within the enclosure and boundary, with the sacred places and the monuments; all things pass.
EDCS-10401252.summary: This funerary inscription records Caius Iulius Aemuli Larginus dedicating tombs, a garden, and sacred spaces for himself while alive.

EDCS-10401253.translation: To the Divine Shades. The parents placed this for Iulia Amabilis.
EDCS-10401253.summary: This funerary inscription records that the parents placed a monument for Iulia Amabilis.

EDCS-10401254.translation: Caius Iulius To, freedman of Caius Iulius Victor, for himself and his wife and his children and their descendants.
EDCS-10401254.summary: This funerary inscription records Caius Iulius To dedicating a monument for himself, his wife, and descendants.

EDCS-10401256.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of Iulia Musice. She placed this for herself while alive.
EDCS-10401256.summary: This funerary inscription records Iulia Musice dedicating a monument for herself while alive.

EDCS-10401257.translation: To the Divine Shades of Iulia Primula.
EDCS-10401257.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the memory of Iulia Primula.

EDCS-10401259.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Marcus Terentius Marinus, son of Iulia Belinia.
EDCS-10401259.summary: This is a funerary dedication (dis manibus) for Marcus Terentius Marinus, likely set up by his mother Iulia Belinia.

EDCS-10401260.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed and to the memory of Lubius. Caius Ca [---].
EDCS-10401260.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Lubius, with the dedicator Caius Ca partially preserved.

EDCS-10401263.translation: For Magnilla, daughter of Vodeluteiacus. Lucanus, son of Lucanus, for his mother.
EDCS-10401263.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucanus setting up a monument for his mother, Magnilla.

EDCS-10401264.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed and to the memory of Maricia. Her mother Artemia placed this.
EDCS-10401264.summary: This funerary inscription states that Artemia erected this monument for her daughter Maricia.

EDCS-10401266.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed and to the memory of Minicia Albina.
EDCS-10401266.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication for Minicia Albina.

EDCS-10401267.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Nigrus, son of Venopis, and for himself and his family.
EDCS-10401267.summary: This funerary inscription dedicates the monument to Nigrus and his household, including himself.

EDCS-10401269.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed and to the memory of Paulus, son of Paulianus. He lived 13 years and 25 days. Iulius Aturios, his uncle, placed this.
EDCS-10401269.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Paulus, son of Paulianus, at the age of 13 years and 25 days, with the monument erected by his uncle Iulius Aturios.

EDCS-10401270.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Petronius Avitianus. He lived 4 years and 100 days. Senilis and Aveticcus, his parents, took care to have this made.
EDCS-10401270.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Petronius Avitianus, who died at the age of 4 years and 100 days, with his parents Senilis and Aveticcus commissioning the monument.

EDCS-10401271.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed and to the memory of Gnaeus Pompeius Remus.
EDCS-10401271.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gnaeus Pompeius Remus.

EDCS-10401272.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed and to the memory of Pomponia Carantilla, aged 8 years, leaving three children. Pomponius Drutedo, her husband, erected this.
EDCS-10401272.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Pomponia Carantilla at age 8, with her husband Pomponius Drutedo erecting the monument.

EDCS-10401273.translation: Julius Amathustinus erected this for his wife S. Materna.
EDCS-10401273.summary: A husband erected this funerary monument for his wife.

EDCS-10401274.translation: To the departed spirits and in memory of Silina Nicenis, freedwoman of Publicius.
EDCS-10401274.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits and memory of a freedwoman.

EDCS-10401275.translation: To the departed spirits and in memory of Sollemnis, son of Vipodualis, deceased at the age of 31.
EDCS-10401275.summary: A funerary inscription for Sollemnis, who died at age 31.

EDCS-10401276.translation: Caius Sulpicius Sanctus, while alive, erected this for himself and in memory of his patron Cinnamus.
EDCS-10401276.summary: A living individual dedicated this monument for himself and his patron.

EDCS-10401277.translation: His fellow freedmen erected this in memory of Tauratis.
EDCS-10401277.summary: Fellow freedmen erected this funerary monument for Tauratis.

EDCS-10401278.translation: Flavius Primulus erected this for the departed spirits and in memory of Taurica, his wife.
EDCS-10401278.summary: A husband erected this funerary monument for his wife.

EDCS-10401280.translation: His freedmen erected this for the departed spirits of Valerius Firmillus.
EDCS-10401280.summary: Freedmen erected this funerary monument for Valerius Firmillus.

EDCS-10401281.translation: To the departed spirits and in memory of Valeria Veneria, freedwoman of Regina.
EDCS-10401281.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits and memory of a freedwoman.

EDCS-10401289.translation: Burial of good memory of Orontes, on the 16th day before the Kalends of October, in the 14th year of the reign of our lord.
EDCS-10401289.summary: This inscription records the burial date of Orontes, likely during the 4th century CE based on the regnal year.

EDCS-10401290.summary: This inscription begins to record the burial details of Eutropius but is incomplete.

EDCS-10401291.translation: On the fourteenth day before the Kalends of June, the burial of Receptus.
EDCS-10401291.summary: This inscription records the burial of a person named Receptus on a specific date.

EDCS-10401294.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Julius Belinatepus.

EDCS-10401297.translation: Quintus Docius made this according to the will.
EDCS-10401297.summary: This funerary inscription states that Quintus Docius fulfilled a will.

EDCS-10401298.translation: Alogia, may you live in God.
EDCS-10401298.summary: This inscription is a Christian epitaph wishing Alogia life in God.

EDCS-10401299.translation: The burial of Basilia on the eleventh day before the Kalends of February, the Lord's Day, after the sixth consulship of Honorius.
EDCS-10401299.summary: This inscription records the burial of Basilia on a specific date during the consulship of Honorius VI.

EDCS-10401302.translation: Lucius Autius, son of Lucius, from Foro Iulii in the territory of Aniensis, a soldier of the 14th Legion Gemina, aged 35, with 15 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-10401302.summary: This is a soldier's tombstone for Lucius Autius of the 14th Legion Gemina, detailing his age and service length.

EDCS-10401303.translation: Gaius Julius Albus, soldier of the 2nd Legion, in the century of Laenatis, aged 27, with 7 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-10401303.summary: This tombstone records the death of Gaius Julius Albus, a soldier in the 2nd Legion, specifying his age and service.

EDCS-10401304.translation: Lucius Furius, son of Lucius, from Cremona in the territory of Aniensis, a soldier of the 14th Legion Gemina.
EDCS-10401304.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Furius, son of Lucius, as a soldier of the 14th Legion Gemina, originating from Cremona.

EDCS-10401307.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et memoriae aeternae vi veterani legionis VIII missi honesta missione qui natus tempora <i=F>unxit sua Caius sibi et fratri supra scribto sic sepulchrum <i=E>mp<e=I>nse vivus faciundum curavit et sub ascia dedicavit \n
EDCS-10401307.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for eternal memory: Caius, a veteran of the Eighth Legion, discharged with an honorable discharge, who reached the end of his life, had this tomb made for himself and his brother inscribed above, and dedicated it while alive under the axe.
EDCS-10401307.summary: This is a self-funded tomb inscription by a veteran of the Eighth Legion, dedicated to himself and his brother.

EDCS-10401308.translation: To the Divine Shades and the memory of Apricius.
EDCS-10401308.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the memory of Apricius.

EDCS-10401310.translation: To the Divine Shades of Julius Albinus Primus, his freedman.
EDCS-10401310.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Julius Albinus Primus by his freedman.

EDCS-10401311.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et Memoriae Otociliae Severae Lugudunensis Martius Augusti libertus coniugi karissimae posuit\n
EDCS-10401311.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for Memory: Martius, freedman of Augustus, set this up for his dearest wife, Otocilia Severa of Lugudunum.
EDCS-10401311.summary: This epitaph records a monument erected by Martius, a freedman of Augustus, for his wife Otocilia Severa from Lugudunum.

EDCS-10401323.translation: Gaius Caecilius, of the Galeria tribe, to Mars.
EDCS-10401323.summary: This is a dedication to Mars by Gaius Caecilius of the Galeria tribe.

EDCS-10401325.translation: Iulia Malla, daughter of Malluron, dedicated this from her own property in memory of her daughter Sulpicia Silvana, to the divine powers of the Augusti and the goddess Damona Matubergina.
EDCS-10401325.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulia Malla for her daughter, commemorating her and honoring the Augusti and the goddess Damona.

EDCS-10401345.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely indicating ownership or a tombstone.

EDCS-10401346.summary: This is a dedication to an emperor or a deified emperor named Andoirius.

EDCS-10401347.summary: This is a personal name inscription, possibly indicating origin or ownership.

EDCS-10401350.translation: Gaius fulfilled his vow to Cisonius Mercury, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10401350.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mercury by Gaius.

EDCS-10401352.translation: Marcus Marci Iuli Sancti, a polycratum (a type of jewel or ornament) for the sting of Marcus Iuli Sancti, a amethystinum (an amethyst gem or object) for scars, from M. M. (Marcus Marci).
EDCS-10401352.summary: This inscription lists medicinal remedies or amulets associated with Marcus Marci Iuli Sancti, possibly for sale or personal use.

EDCS-10401353.translation: Valerius Philerotis's italicum (a type of medicine or ointment) for diathesis (a medical condition), Valerius Philerotis's cycnium lene (a gentle swan-like substance) for EV C Valeri.
EDCS-10401353.summary: This inscription lists medicinal remedies or ointments belonging to Valerius Philerotis.

EDCS-10401360.summary: This is a record of a transaction, possibly a debt or payment, involving a freedman named S. ori.

EDCS-10401361.translation: Silvinus Vegetius, freedman of Lucius Amineius, 3 sextarii, 1 denarius, 1 as for honey-comb, 1 sextarius, 1 semuncia, 1 pitcher, 1 as.
EDCS-10401361.summary: This inscription details a list of commodities and their quantities, likely related to an estate or a sale by a freedman.

EDCS-10401362.translation: Cordula, clever, old, outstanding, aged 85. Caius E. Acrabi, 580.
EDCS-10401362.summary: This inscription appears to record the age and possibly some achievements or possessions of a woman named Cordula, along with another individual, Caius E. Acrabi, potentially indicating a funerary context or a record of status. The numbers '580' and 'DLXXX DLXXX' are difficult to interpret definitively without further context but could relate to property, debts, or a dating system.

EDCS-10401375.translation: Matugenos, son of Cosintos, of the Belini.
EDCS-10401375.summary: This is a brief funerary or dedicatory inscription identifying an individual named Matugenos, son of Cosintos, and associating him with the Belini tribe or family, likely from Roman Britain.

EDCS-10401377.summary: This inscription is a simple patronymic, identifying an individual named Spoltarius, son of Bladama, likely a funerary marker.

EDCS-10401381.summary: This inscription is a patronymic, indicating an individual named Campani, son of Campanius, possibly on a funerary monument.

EDCS-10401400.summary: This is a simple patronymic inscription, identifying an individual named Gamotus, son of Gamotus, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-10401403.summary: This inscription records the name Caius Iulius Sen[ecio?], likely a personal name on a tombstone or public monument.

EDCS-10401404.summary: This is a patronymic inscription, identifying an individual named Latinus, son of Latinus, possibly on a funerary marker.

EDCS-10401427.summary: This inscription names Marcus Satius and implies the presence of 'two', possibly brothers or a pair of individuals being commemorated, likely in a funerary context.

EDCS-10401482.summary: This inscription identifies Sallustius Mercator, possibly with a numeral or abbreviation 'V' that could indicate his age, rank, or affiliation, likely on a funerary or public monument.

EDCS-10401483.summary: This inscription is a patronymic, identifying an individual named Senoviri, son of Malluron, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-10401484.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying an individual named Tegullirus and his parent.

EDCS-10500001.text_edition: \n Augusto et Mercurio votum solverunt libentes merito Tiberius Claudius Potitus Titus Flavius Pinus\n
EDCS-10500001.translation: To Augustus and Mercury, Tiberius Claudius Potitus and Titus Flavius Pinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-10500001.summary: This is a votive inscription by Tiberius Claudius Potitus and Titus Flavius Pinus to the gods Augustus and Mercury.

EDCS-10500002.translation: Julius Venixxamus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Mercury Adsmerius.
EDCS-10500002.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a vow paid to the god Mercury Adsmerius by Julius Venixxamus.

EDCS-10500006.translation: For Claudia Varenilla, daughter of Claudius Varenus, the people of the Pictavi, Marcus Censorius Paullus, imperial legate with praetorian power of the province of Aquitania, designated consul, her husband, pleased with the honour, arranged for the funeral, burial place, statue, and monument to be provided at his own expense.
EDCS-10500006.summary: This is a funerary monument erected at public expense by Marcus Censorius Paullus for his wife Claudia Varenilla, daughter of Claudius Varenus, during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10500007.translation: For Alphia Faventina, Catilia and Faventius, freedman and steward from the inheritance, [dedicated this].
EDCS-10500007.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Alphia Faventina by Catilia and Faventius, identifying their status as freedman and steward.

EDCS-10500008.translation: To the divine spirits and memory of Gaius Flavius Sabinus Campanus of Teanum, a Roman knight, soothsayer of his time, singular in his talent, who lived 58 years, 5 months, and 5 days; his son Caius Flavius Sabinianus ordered this to be made for his most rare and loving father before he himself died.
EDCS-10500008.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Flavius Sabinus Campanus, a Roman knight and soothsayer, commissioned by his son, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-10500016.translation: Cavaria Assclepia placed this for her most dutiful mother Cavaria.
EDCS-10500016.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Cavaria Assclepia to her mother, Cavaria.

EDCS-10500017.translation: To the divine spirits of Cicelavius; Catullus [dedicated this].
EDCS-10500017.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a monument to the divine spirits of Cicelavius by Catullus.

EDCS-10500019.translation: To the divine spirits of his living patron, Diōra, son of Persicus, living, he consecrated this from his own resources while alive.
EDCS-10500019.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Diōra, son of Persicus, dedicating a monument to his living patron from his own resources.

EDCS-10500020.translation: His heir placed this for Fortionius Ianuarius, [in accordance with the] will.
EDCS-10500020.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fortionius Ianuarius, placed by his heir according to the will.

EDCS-10500021.translation: Hail! To the divine spirits and memory of Julia Maxumilla, his dearest wife, a good soul, who lived more or less 41 years, from the same household as Lucius Julius Frontonis Cavarianus; Julius Basileus, her husband, placed this.
EDCS-10500021.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Julia Maxumilla, wife of Julius Basileus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500022.translation: and to the memory of his son and to Iulius from Partilla.
EDCS-10500022.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the memory of a son and Iulius, possibly on a tomb. The date is uncertain.

EDCS-10500023.translation: To the Divine Spirits and to the memory of Licinia Senodonna. Licinius Paternus prepared this monument for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-10500023.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription set up by Licinius Paternus for himself and his family, dedicated to the Divine Spirits and the memory of Licinia Senodonna.

EDCS-10500024.translation: Of Marcellinus, freedmen of Vitalis and Lepidus.
EDCS-10500024.summary: This inscription refers to Marcellinus, a freedman of Vitalis and Lepidus, likely on a tombstone or memorial.

EDCS-10500025.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, to Santia and Macer.

EDCS-10500028.translation: to Sto[n]io, his son, heir by the will.
EDCS-10500028.summary: This inscription identifies an heir by testament for a person named Sto[n]io.

EDCS-10500029.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, to an individual named Quirina.

EDCS-10500034.translation: Selasciaturias [with] Prito, II, Durnovius, II, CX. Selasciatonos ACAV XX NI.
EDCS-10500034.summary: This inscription appears to record numerical units or measures associated with individuals named Selasciaturias, Prito, Durnovius, and Selasciatonos, possibly related to trade or a building project.

EDCS-10500035.translation: Recessio, to Valentio, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-10500035.summary: This inscription records a person named Recessio dedicating something to Valentio on a specific date in the Roman calendar.

EDCS-10500036.translation: Quintus Iulius Certus, son of Quintus, of the Teretina tribe, from Arles, a soldier of the 18th cohort of volunteers, is buried here.
EDCS-10500036.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Iulius Certus, a soldier from Arles serving in the 18th cohort of volunteers.

EDCS-10500038.translation: Aeternalis and Servilla, may you live in God.
EDCS-10500038.summary: This inscription offers a wish for eternal life in God to Aeternalis and Servilla, likely a posthumous dedication or blessing.

EDCS-10500040.translation: Regali, son of Coinitus, 20 years old, lies here, and Cintugenus, son of Decumon, [set this up] for Coinitus his father.
EDCS-10500040.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Regali and the dedication by Cintugenus for his father Coinitus.

EDCS-10500041.translation: Sabinus, son of Fulvus, 27 years old.
EDCS-10500041.summary: This is a short funerary inscription identifying Sabinus and his age.

EDCS-10500042.translation: For Anextlus, who died in Belgica, for his sister's son Anextlus, for his father.
EDCS-10500042.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication for Anextlus, noting his death in Belgica and his familial relationships.

EDCS-10500044.translation: Lepida, daughter of Valens, wife of Reginus; Lepida, daughter of Reginus, [set this up] for [her] devotion.
EDCS-10500044.summary: This funerary inscription honors Lepida, mentioning her father, husband, and daughter who likely erected the monument.

EDCS-10500048.translation: Frontus and Tarbeisonius performed the rites for Ratinus [or Ratinus and Brivatomus].
EDCS-10500048.summary: This inscription records a religious rite performed by Frontus and Tarbeisonius, likely a dedication or votive offering.

EDCS-10500053.translation: Fausta, may you live in God, may Faustinus the master always live.
EDCS-10500053.summary: This inscription is a Christian epitaph wishing eternal life to Fausta and Faustinus.

EDCS-10500054.translation: Gaius Rufinius, Julius Adlucus is the heir.
EDCS-10500054.summary: This inscription identifies Julius Adlucus as the heir of Gaius Rufinius.

EDCS-10500055.translation: In this tomb of good memory, Marinianus the monk, who lived 73 years, set up the monument; Generosus [made it].
EDCS-10500055.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Marinianus the monk and was set up by Generosus.

EDCS-10500057.summary: This brief inscription likely records a voluntary dedication or contribution by Verpanto and Romulus.

EDCS-10500058.translation: To Carina, wife, who lived 27 years, Titus Valerius [set this up].
EDCS-10500058.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Titus Valerius to his wife Carina, noting her age at death.

EDCS-10500060.translation: Martia the presbyteress offers gifts to Olebrius and Nepos alike.
EDCS-10500060.summary: This inscription records an offering made by Martia, a presbyteress, to Olebrius and Nepos.

EDCS-10500061.translation: In this tomb rests Iovinus of good memory, who lived 36 years. He died in peace on the 10th day before the Kalends of September. His wife Pola erected the monument.
EDCS-10500061.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iovinus, who lived 36 years, and notes his wife Pola as the dedicator.

EDCS-10500062.translation: Here lies Rusticus, who lived 51 years.
EDCS-10500062.summary: This inscription records the burial of Rusticus, who died at the age of 51.

EDCS-10500063.translation: Fulvius Priscinus, son of Fulvianus, took care to have this made for Hercules Augustus.
EDCS-10500063.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument to Hercules Augustus by Fulvius Priscinus.

EDCS-10500066.translation: To Caesar Germanicus, son of Augustus, Father of the Country, and to Etnosus: Anavus, freedman of Atticus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10500066.summary: This is a votive inscription by Anavus, freedman of Atticus, to Emperor Caesar Germanicus and to a deity named Etnosus.

EDCS-10500067.translation: To Mars Rigisamus, Tiberius Iulius Eunus, after seeing a vision.
EDCS-10500067.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to the god Mars Rigisamus by Tiberius Iulius Eunus, inspired by a vision.

EDCS-10500069.translation: To the god Mercury, Marcellus, freedman of Latina.
EDCS-10500069.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mercury by Marcellus, a freedman.

EDCS-10500070.translation: For the safety of the Emperors and the Roman people, Gracchus, son of Ategnutis, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the divine will of Augustus and Mars Mogetius.
EDCS-10500070.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Gracchus, son of Ategnutis, to Augustus and Mars Mogetius for the safety of the emperors and the Roman people.

EDCS-10500071.translation: For the safety of the Emperors and the Roman people, Caius Agileius Primus, one of the six Augustal priests and curator of Roman citizens, dedicated this sacred precinct to Minerva and the divine Drusilla in perpetuity, at his own expense.
EDCS-10500071.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a sacred precinct to Minerva and Drusilla by Caius Agileius Primus, an Augustal priest, for the well-being of the empire.

EDCS-10500072.translation: To the divine Solimara, Firmana, mother of Cobricus, dedicated this temple with its furnishings at her own expense.
EDCS-10500072.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple and its furnishings to the goddess Solimara by Firmana, mother of Cobricus.

EDCS-10500073.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Marcus Publilius Adventus, a soldier of the 30th Ulpian Victorious Legion, Pious and Faithful, and Batavinia Romana, his most devoted parents, took care to have this made for their son, [who lived] 11 months.
EDCS-10500073.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a tomb by the parents of Marcus Publilius Adventus, a soldier, for their son who died at 11 months old.

EDCS-10500074.translation: To Gaviae Quietae, daughter of Aemilius Afrius, duovir, by decree of the town council of the Bituriges Cubi, a place.
EDCS-10500074.summary: This inscription records a grant of public land to Gaviae Quietae, daughter of Aemilius Afrius, who was a duovir, by the council of the Bituriges Cubi.

EDCS-10500075.translation: To the divine shades, to Lalianus the leather-worker.
EDCS-10500075.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lalianus, a leather-worker.

EDCS-10500076.translation: To the divine shades, to Scorpianus.
EDCS-10500076.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Scorpianus.

EDCS-10500077.translation: Lucius Tarquinius Primus, the murrillo gladiator, lies here; he was a Roman and a member of the same mess.
EDCS-10500077.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Tarquinius Primus, a Roman murrillo gladiator, who was part of a military or gladiatorial mess.

EDCS-10500078.translation: To the divine shades and to the memory of Aetion, daughter of Mamercius Lupus.
EDCS-10500078.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Aetion, daughter of Mamercius Lupus.

EDCS-10500079.translation: To the divine shades, to Africana.
EDCS-10500079.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Africana.

EDCS-10500080.translation: To Arisella, to the divine shades.
EDCS-10500080.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Arisella.

EDCS-10500082.translation: To the divine shades, to Attianus.
EDCS-10500082.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Attianus.

EDCS-10500083.summary: This is a tombstone for Centaurus, a child who died at the age of three.

EDCS-10500084.translation: To the divine shades, to Aveta, aged 3 years.
EDCS-10500084.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Aveta, a child who died at the age of three.

EDCS-10500085.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deceased Augurina.

EDCS-10500087.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deceased Aunilla.

EDCS-10500089.translation: To the Divine Spirits, Aurelius Theopeompiades, aged 5.
EDCS-10500089.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deceased Aurelius Theopeompiades, who died at the age of five.

EDCS-10500090.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deceased Blandula.

EDCS-10500092.translation: To the Divine Spirits, Camelius, aged 20 years.

EDCS-10500093.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deceased Canidus.

EDCS-10500094.translation: To Gaius Cappel, aged 5 and a half years.

EDCS-10500110.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for someone named Gnata.

EDCS-10500112.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulius Messor.
EDCS-10500112.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulius Messor.

EDCS-10500114.translation: To the spirits of the underworld and to the memory of Iulia Paullina. Tenatius Martinus (dedicated this) to his wife, aged 50.
EDCS-10500114.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Tenatius Martinus to his wife, Iulia Paullina, aged 50.

EDCS-10500115.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Verecunda.
EDCS-10500115.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Verecunda.

EDCS-10500117.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iuniano.
EDCS-10500117.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for someone named Iuniano.

EDCS-10500118.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Iunimus.

EDCS-10500119.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Iuvenalis.

EDCS-10500120.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Legitimus, son of Melissus.
EDCS-10500120.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Legitimus, son of Melissus.

EDCS-10500121.translation: His mother made this for Elpidinus.
EDCS-10500121.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by a mother for her son, Elpidinus.

EDCS-10500122.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Lera.
EDCS-10500122.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Lera.

EDCS-10500128.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the underworld spirits for Ariani.

EDCS-10500148.translation: To the Divine Spirits: Primi, son of PR, Sigin.
