EDCS-10500163.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Severa.
EDCS-10500163.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Severa.

EDCS-10500164.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Severilla.
EDCS-10500164.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Severilla.

EDCS-10500165.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Siv.
EDCS-10500165.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Siv.

EDCS-10500166.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Silvanus.
EDCS-10500166.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Silvanus.

EDCS-10500167.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Soiana.
EDCS-10500167.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Soiana.

EDCS-10500168.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Sulpicius Sollemnis, who lived [many] years, and Silva, who lived 63 years.
EDCS-10500168.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of Sulpicius Sollemnis and Silva.

EDCS-10500171.translation: To the spirits of the departed Flavia.
EDCS-10500171.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Flavia.

EDCS-10500172.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Tota.
EDCS-10500172.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Tota.

EDCS-10500173.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Toutilla.
EDCS-10500173.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Toutilla.

EDCS-10500175.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Vebrumna.
EDCS-10500175.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Vebrumna.

EDCS-10500176.summary: A funerary inscription for Vexora, who died at the age of 27.

EDCS-10500177.summary: A funerary dedication to the Divine Manes by or for Avitus.

EDCS-10500195.translation: Arad, son of Rasia, may all things be from Vesituas Tansna.
EDCS-10500195.summary: An inscription, likely a dedication or epitaph, with names and a divine invocation, possibly from a provincial context.

EDCS-10500196.summary: A simple funerary epitaph stating that Baudardus rests here.

EDCS-10500197.summary: A simple funerary epitaph stating that Lunidia rests here.

EDCS-10500198.translation: Meroflidis of good memory rests here.
EDCS-10500198.summary: A funerary epitaph for Meroflidis, noting her good memory.

EDCS-10500199.translation: This tomb encloses Sperandeus, properly buried, who strove always to live a pious life; he died on the ninth day before the Ides of July.
EDCS-10500199.summary: A funerary epitaph detailing the life and death of Sperandeus, who died on July 7th.

EDCS-10500200.summary: An inscription identifying Fabia as the daughter of Dami, likely part of a larger inscription or a simple label.

EDCS-10500202.translation: To the Divine Numen of the Emperors and the Genius of Apollo, Atepomarus, son of Craxantus, and Julius Gnatus, son of Atrectus, have given from their own resources.
EDCS-10500202.summary: A dedication made by two individuals, Iulius Atrectus and Iulius Gnatus, to the Divine Numen of the Emperors and the Genius of Apollo.

EDCS-10500203.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Monimae Cesti filiae et Servillae uxsori sic suae et filiae et alterae filliae sic quae vocatur NA IMPR\n
EDCS-10500203.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Monima, daughter of Cestus, and for Servilla, his wife, and for her daughter, and for another daughter who is called NA IMPR.
EDCS-10500203.summary: This epitaph commemorates Monima, her mother Servilla, and two daughters, one of whom is named NA IMPR.

EDCS-10500204.translation: Martialis, son of [---], fulfills his vow willingly and deservedly to the Divine Numen of the Emperors and the Genius of [Apollo?].
EDCS-10500204.summary: An inscription recording a vow fulfilled by Martialis, son of [---], to the Divine Numen of the Emperors and the Genius of Apollo, possibly dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-10500207.translation: A deposition of Allovira, of good memory.
EDCS-10500207.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Allovira, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500210.translation: Elvontius, son of Ieurus, Aneunos, Olicnus, Lugurix, son of Aneunicnus.
EDCS-10500210.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly related to a funerary monument or a property marker, likely of Celtic origin.

EDCS-10500212.translation: Andecarius Ferox, son of Atrianus and Atuana, arranged this in accordance with the will of Atrianus.
EDCS-10500212.summary: This epitaph indicates that Andecarius Ferox commissioned the monument according to the will of Atrianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500214.translation: To the divine spirits of the Emperors, Filbenus, son of Censorinus.
EDCS-10500214.summary: This dedication honors the divine spirits of the Emperors and identifies the dedicator as Filbenus, son of Censorinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500216.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Cantius, son of Nammius.
EDCS-10500216.summary: This epitaph is a dedication to the underworld spirits for Cantius, son of Nammius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500217.translation: To the spirits of the underworld and to the memory of Claudius Fidus; may his bones rest well; aged 65.
EDCS-10500217.summary: This epitaph is a dedication to the underworld spirits and memory of Claudius Fidus, who died at the age of 65.

EDCS-10500220.translation: To the memory of Ianuaris, to the spirits of the underworld.
EDCS-10500220.summary: This epitaph is a dedication to the memory of Ianuaris and the underworld spirits, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500221.translation: To the spirits of the underworld and to the memory of Aelianus Suadutionis, a citizen of the Bituriges Cubi, aged 25.
EDCS-10500221.summary: This epitaph is a dedication to the underworld spirits and memory of Aelianus Suadutionis, a citizen of the Bituriges Cubi, aged 25.

EDCS-10500222.summary: This epitaph records the memory of Lupula, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500224.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, to the memory of Priscinus.
EDCS-10500224.summary: This epitaph is a dedication to the underworld spirits and memory of Priscinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500226.translation: To the Divine Manes, in memory of Publius Truitus.
EDCS-10500226.summary: This is a funerary dedication ('Dis Manibus') for Publius Truitus, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-10500227.translation: To the Divine Manes, in memory of Silvester.
EDCS-10500227.summary: This is a funerary dedication ('Dis Manibus') for Silvester, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-10500232.summary: This inscription marks a burial place or memorial ('umbra') for Rimanirius.

EDCS-10500234.summary: This is a memorial inscription ('memoria') for Virillius, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-10500236.translation: Baudulfus, archpriest, who died on the 13th day before the Kalends of December, rests in this tomb.
EDCS-10500236.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Baudulfus, an archpriest, with a specific date of death.

EDCS-10500237.translation: Flavia Cuba, daughter of Firmanus, dedicated this monument to her god Mars Augustus.
EDCS-10500237.summary: This is a dedication by Flavia Cuba to the god Mars Augustus, likely a votive or shrine inscription.

EDCS-10500238.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph or identification of Pollius Paternus, son of Sabinus.

EDCS-10500239.translation: Carassonius, son of Cartullus, a monument to the Divine Powers of the Emperors.
EDCS-10500239.summary: This inscription records a monument erected by Carassonius to honor the Divine Powers of the Emperors.

EDCS-10500240.translation: Dico, son of Niron, a monument to the Divine Powers of the Emperors.
EDCS-10500240.summary: This inscription records a monument erected by Dico to honor the Divine Powers of the Emperors.

EDCS-10500241.translation: Venixsamus placed this from his own resources for the Divine Powers of the Emperors.
EDCS-10500241.summary: This inscription records Venixsamus dedicating a monument at his own expense to the Divine Powers of the Emperors.

EDCS-10500243.translation: To the Divine Shades, in memory of Claudius.
EDCS-10500243.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Divine Shades for Claudius, likely from a tomb or memorial.

EDCS-10500252.translation: To Emperor Augustus, Atespatus, son of Crixus, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly. To Livia Augusta, Atespatus, son of Crixus, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10500252.summary: This inscription records a double vow fulfillment by Atespatus, son of Crixus, to Emperor Augustus and Livia Augusta, likely a funerary or dedicatory monument.

EDCS-10500253.translation: Here rests Siggecondis, handmaiden of God. She lived 39 years. She died on the 8th day before the Kalends of June in the year 1000.
EDCS-10500253.summary: This Christian funerary inscription records the death and age of Siggecondis, dating to the year 1000 (likely from the Roman era or a later period using Roman dating conventions).

EDCS-10500254.translation: To Vimpuro, Stepaprod Ivavus, freedman of Firminus, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10500254.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfillment by Stepaprod Ivavus, freedman of Firminus, to a person named Vimpuro, likely a dedicatory monument.

EDCS-10500261.translation: To Nerio, Cassia, daughter of Nemia, fulfilled her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10500261.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfillment by Cassia, daughter of Nemia, to Nerio, likely a dedicatory monument.

EDCS-10500286.translation: Sextus Cliternius, a soldier of the 14th legion, with seven years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-10500286.summary: This inscription identifies Sextus Cliternius, a soldier of the 14th legion with seven years of service, as being buried here, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-10500288.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Quintus Carisius, likely a name on a tombstone or ownership marker.

EDCS-10500289.translation: To Lucius Cassius Faustus, freedman of Lucius, in honor of his fellow freedman Lucius Cassius Firmus.
EDCS-10500289.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Lucius Cassius Faustus to his fellow freedman Lucius Cassius Firmus, likely a funerary or memorial monument.

EDCS-10500291.translation: Bratronos, son of Nantontos, Epadatextoricos, to Leucutius, his companion.
EDCS-10500291.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Bratronos, son of Nantontos, and Epadatextoricos to Leucutius, their companion, likely a funerary or memorial monument.

EDCS-10500292.translation: To the Divine Shades and the memory of Titus Proculeius Irenaeus, Caesius Pacatus, his father, erected this monument during his lifetime for himself and his family.
EDCS-10500292.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument erected by Caesius Pacatus for his deceased son Titus Proculeius Irenaeus and for himself and his family, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-10500293.translation: To the Divine Spirits and the memory of Paetinus Paetinius, a decurion of the state of the Aulercian Eburovices, he erected this monument to himself while alive.
EDCS-10500293.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Paetinus Paetinius, a decurion, erected by himself.

EDCS-10500296.text_edition: \n Artis <grammatices> doctor morumque magister Blaesianus Biturix Musarum semper amator hic iacet aeterno devinctus membra sopore\n
EDCS-10500296.translation: Blaesianus Biturix, teacher of grammar and master of morals, always a lover of the Muses, lies here, bound in eternal sleep.
EDCS-10500296.summary: This epitaph commemorates Blaesianus Biturix, a teacher of grammar and morals and a lover of the Muses.

EDCS-10500297.translation: Gaius Annius Sabinianus erected this monument to himself and his son while alive, and also to the Divine Spirits and memory of Sabina Apollinaris.
EDCS-10500297.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Annius Sabinianus, dedicated to himself, his son, and Sabina Apollinaris, erected by himself.

EDCS-10500298.translation: To the Divine Spirits and the memory of Gaius Annius Togimarus, Maevia Paulina, his wife, erected this monument to herself and her family while alive.
EDCS-10500298.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Annius Togimarus and his family, erected by his wife Maevia Paulina.

EDCS-10500299.translation: To the Divine Spirits and the memory of Annia Anniola, who lived 10 years and 10 months, Geminantius, her father, erected this monument to his dearest daughter and himself while alive.
EDCS-10500299.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Annia Anniola, erected by her father Geminantius.

EDCS-10500300.translation: To the Divine Spirits and the memory of Anniola, Anillus erected this monument.
EDCS-10500300.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Anniola, erected by Anillus.

EDCS-10500301.translation: To the Divine Spirits and the memory of Apinossa Adname.
EDCS-10500301.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Apinossa Adname.

EDCS-10500303.translation: To the Divine Spirits and the memory of Divixtus, Moxius, his father, erected this monument to him while alive.
EDCS-10500303.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Divixtus, erected by his father Moxius.

EDCS-10500304.translation: To the Divine Spirits and the memory of Herennius Divixtus, he erected this monument to himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-10500304.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Herennius Divixtus, erected by himself.

EDCS-10500305.translation: To the Divine Spirits and the memory of Julius Diophantus, he made this at his own expense, Rorilus.
EDCS-10500305.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Julius Diophantus, set up by Rorilus.

EDCS-10500306.translation: To the Divine Spirits and the memory of Julia Annonia, Magnus erected this monument to his daughter and himself while alive.
EDCS-10500306.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Julia Annonia and Magnus, erected by Magnus.

EDCS-10500307.translation: To the spirits of the departed, the father Insidiator set up this monument for his living daughter Iulia Insidiola and for himself.
EDCS-10500307.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Insidiola, set up by her father.

EDCS-10500309.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Iustinus and his family, while alive, set up this monument for themselves and their relatives.
EDCS-10500309.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iustinus and his family, set up by them while alive.

EDCS-10500310.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Lavanus and Noma, while alive, set up this monument.
EDCS-10500310.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lavanus and Noma, set up by them while alive.

EDCS-10500311.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Atul.
EDCS-10500311.summary: A funerary epitaph, incomplete, dedicated to Atul.

EDCS-10500313.translation: Illius, while alive, set up this monument.
EDCS-10500313.summary: A funerary epitaph, incomplete, set up by Illius while alive.

EDCS-10500314.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Caius Sulpicius Fidus, aged three years; his father Sulpicius Angelo set this up.
EDCS-10500314.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Sulpicius Fidus, aged three, set up by his father.

EDCS-10500316.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Sulpicia Regina; Sulpicius Regenus, father, and Iullitta, mother, while alive, set this up for themselves.
EDCS-10500316.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sulpicia Regina, set up by her parents.

EDCS-10500317.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Tullius Liberinus.
EDCS-10500317.summary: A funerary epitaph, incomplete, dedicated to Tullius Liberinus.

EDCS-10500318.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Julius Liberinus.
EDCS-10500318.summary: A funerary epitaph, incomplete, dedicated to Julius Liberinus.

EDCS-10500320.summary: A funerary epitaph, incomplete, possibly naming two individuals, Graecina and Dodica.

EDCS-10500325.translation: Lepidianus, son of Lepidus, set this up at his own expense, gladly fulfilling his vow deservedly.
EDCS-10500325.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lepidianus fulfilling a vow, likely set up on a public monument or religious site.

EDCS-10500327.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of Parthia Quarta.
EDCS-10500327.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Parthia Quarta, likely from a tomb or cenotaph.

EDCS-10500328.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of Iulius Narcissus, aged 39.
EDCS-10500328.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iulius Narcissus, likely from a tomb or cenotaph.

EDCS-10500332.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of Veneria and Luttus Marcianus, a citizen of Lugdunum; they set this up themselves while alive.
EDCS-10500332.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Veneria and Luttus Marcianus, who set up their own tomb while alive.

EDCS-10500333.translation: Aemilius Me menus Sev[---] I AE.
EDCS-10500333.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its exact purpose, but likely records a name and possibly a status or office.

EDCS-10500334.translation: Atimetus, freedman, to the Divine Shades. He made it himself.
EDCS-10500334.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Atimetus, a freedman, dedicating a monument to himself or for the Divine Shades.

EDCS-10500335.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of Caius F. Alpinus.
EDCS-10500335.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Caius F. Alpinus, likely from a tomb or cenotaph.

EDCS-10500336.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of Marcellus Nertinus; Caius Te[---] erected this as heir by testament.
EDCS-10500336.summary: This funerary inscription records that an heir, Caius Te[---], erected the monument for Marcellus Nertinus according to his will.

EDCS-10500337.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of Reginus and Pompaeus; they (set it up) for themselves while alive.
EDCS-10500337.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Reginus and Pompaeus, who prepared their own tomb while alive.

EDCS-10500338.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of Simplex Sinturonius.
EDCS-10500338.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Simplex Sinturonius, likely from a tomb or cenotaph.

EDCS-10500340.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for the memory of Iulius Cintusmus.
EDCS-10500340.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iulius Cintusmus.

EDCS-10500341.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for the memory of Iulius Attiolius and his wife Iulia Avita, the heirs N N.
EDCS-10500341.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iulius Attiolius and Iulia Avita, set up by their heirs.

EDCS-10500342.translation: Carigo Daetiva took care to erect this for the spirits of the departed and for their memory.
EDCS-10500342.summary: Carigo Daetiva erected this monument for the departed.

EDCS-10500344.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for the memory of Sulpicius, son of Mascius.
EDCS-10500344.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Sulpicius, son of Mascius.

EDCS-10500347.translation: For the spirits of the departed and for the memory of his son Paullinus, also for the memory of Paullinus his father, also for Nertacus his grandfather; Nertacus erected this while alive.
EDCS-10500347.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument by Nertacus for his son, father, and grandfather.

EDCS-10500348.translation: On the eighth day before the Ides of November died Cenos, wife of Petrus.
EDCS-10500348.summary: This inscription records the death date of Cenos, wife of Petrus.

EDCS-10500349.translation: Mutenia took care of this from her own funds.
EDCS-10500349.summary: Mutenia paid for the erection of this monument herself.

EDCS-10500353.translation: Tiberius Iulius Iulianus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Hercules.
EDCS-10500353.summary: This is a votive inscription by Tiberius Iulius Iulianus to the god Hercules.

EDCS-10500355.translation: Iunianus the son took care to erect this while alive for the spirits of the departed and for the memory of Iunius and Iuniana.
EDCS-10500355.summary: Iunianus the son erected this funerary monument for his father Iunius and mother Iuniana.

EDCS-10500357.translation: Sacer Peroco willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the DVORI.
EDCS-10500357.summary: This is a votive inscription by Sacer Peroco to the DVORI.

EDCS-10500358.translation: Calenus placed this as a tribune from the college.
EDCS-10500358.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Calenus, who held the position of tribune within a college, likely around the Imperial period.

EDCS-10500359.summary: This inscription is a simple naming of Octa Tullia, identifying her father as Budarax, likely a funerary or ownership marker from the Roman period.

EDCS-10500361.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et memoriae Aemili Combrici\n
EDCS-10500361.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for the memory of Aemilia Combrica.
EDCS-10500361.summary: This is an epitaph dedicated to the memory of Aemilia Combrica.

EDCS-10500365.translation: Tepidus, son of Comistrus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the august Apollo.
EDCS-10500365.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Apollo by Tepidus, son of Comistrus, indicating fulfillment of a religious promise, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10500366.translation: Allia, wife of Titus Labienus, daughter of Titus Iulius Paullinus, gave this gift to Bellinus.
EDCS-10500366.summary: This inscription records a gift given by Allia to Bellinus, identifying her paternal lineage and her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500367.translation: To the Genius of the Arverni, Sextus Orgius Suavis, of the Haedui.
EDCS-10500367.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Genius of the Arverni people by Sextus Orgius Suavis, an individual identified with the Haeduan tribe, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10500371.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Lucius Iulius Cadgatus, also called Tripondios, the marble worker.
EDCS-10500371.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the underworld spirits for Lucius Iulius Cadgatus, also known as Tripondios, a marble worker, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500376.translation: To the spirits of the departed and eternal memory for Mansueta.
EDCS-10500376.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed and eternal memory for Mansueta, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500377.translation: To the spirits of the departed and eternal memory for Moligoetus.
EDCS-10500377.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed and eternal memory for Moligoetus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500378.translation: To the spirits of the departed and eternal memory forever for Paterculus.
EDCS-10500378.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed and eternal memory for Paterculus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500379.translation: Sextilia, dearest wife, and Vivius Cobrunnus, son of Titus.
EDCS-10500379.summary: This inscription seems to be a funerary dedication or memorial, likely for Sextilia, with her husband Vivius Cobrunnus, possibly mentioning his father Titus, from the Roman period.

EDCS-10500381.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to Vercius and Aelianus.

EDCS-10500382.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, to Vettus and Flavia.

EDCS-10500391.translation: Lupa of good memory rests in this tomb; she lived in peace for 10 years, died on the 8th day before the Kalends of December, in the 4th indiction, in the reign of our lord Theobald the king.
EDCS-10500391.summary: This inscription records the death of Lupa, who lived 10 years and died on November 24th in the 4th indiction during the reign of King Theobald.

EDCS-10500393.translation: Understand, you who read this, that the deacon Emellius lies covered by this tomb; he had lived thirty-five years when cruel death took away the young man. He died on the 5th day before the Kalends of August in the 37th year of the reign of lord Chlotharius the king.
EDCS-10500393.summary: This inscription commemorates Emellius, a deacon who died at age 35 on July 28th in the 37th year of King Chlotharius's reign.

EDCS-10500395.translation: Remestus of good memory rests here; he lived in peace for 43 years, died on the 6th day before the Ides of February, in the 16th year of the reign of lord Theodobert.
EDCS-10500395.summary: This inscription records the death of Remestus, who lived 43 years and died on February 8th in the 16th year of King Theodobert's reign.

EDCS-10500399.translation: His body, indeed, had fulfilled the debt of nature and the fragile flesh is taken by the damp earth, but the caves of the tomb do not hold him; rather, the heavens do, for the just deeds made him happy. Buried in this tomb is the levite of the lord Innocentius, blessed in his morals, whose name was passed down from his grandfather. He lived a kind life, having barely completed his third year...
EDCS-10500399.summary: This inscription, possibly incomplete, commemorates Innocentius, a levite who lived a virtuous life.

EDCS-10500401.translation: Sacred Georgia, devoted to Christ with a good mind and faith, lies in this tomb. Because of her, her father, under great pressure from a crowd of suitors, chose God's bed with greater fortune.
EDCS-10500401.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Georgia, who was devoted to Christ and influenced her father's choice of marriage.

EDCS-10500402.translation: Vincomalus was a lover of the poor, a lover of the church, a doctor; he lived in peace.
EDCS-10500402.summary: This inscription commemorates Vincomalus, described as a lover of the poor and the church, and a doctor.

EDCS-10500406.translation: To the divine powers of Augustus, and to the god Jupiter Sabasius, Gaius Iulius Carassounus gladly paid his vow, as deserved.
EDCS-10500406.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Iulius Carassounus to the divine powers of Augustus and Jupiter Sabasius.

EDCS-10500407.translation: To the divine powers of the Augusti, and to the god Mars Vorocius, Gaiolus, son of Gaius, gladly paid his vow, as deserved.
EDCS-10500407.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaiolus, son of Gaius, to the divine powers of the Augusti and Mars Vorocius.

EDCS-10500408.translation: To Decimus Antonius Urbicus, son of Decimus, of the Teretina tribe, from Arles.
EDCS-10500408.summary: This is a funerary or honorary inscription for Decimus Antonius Urbicus, likely a citizen of Arles.

EDCS-10500409.translation: To Lucius Fufius Equestris, soldier of the 17th cohort of Lugudunum, assigned to the mint. In the century of Ianuarius, the plot is 4 feet in front and 4 feet in the rear.
EDCS-10500409.summary: This inscription records a land plot allocated to Lucius Fufius Equestris, a soldier serving with the mint in Lugudunum.

EDCS-10500410.translation: To Sextus Cervius Maius. 7 units [of land?] in front, 4 feet in the rear.
EDCS-10500410.summary: This inscription appears to mark a land plot, possibly funerary or agricultural, belonging to Sextus Cervius Maius.

EDCS-10500411.summary: This is a simple inscription, likely part of a tombstone or monument, identifying Gaius Iulius Cantussius.

EDCS-10500415.translation: In this tomb rests Dulcetia of good memory, lived 35 years, died the 6th day before the Ides of July in the 10th year of the reign of our lord King Theoderic.
EDCS-10500415.summary: This is a late antique or early medieval tomb inscription recording the death of Dulcetia under King Theoderic.

EDCS-10500416.translation: In this tomb rests Golmodus of good memory, lived 30 years and 6 months.
EDCS-10500416.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the lifespan of Golmodus.

EDCS-10500420.translation: In this tomb rests in peace Maria, who carried [children? or life?], seven years and five months. Noted on the 19th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-10500420.summary: This tomb inscription records the life and death of Maria, likely a child, with a date noted in a late Roman or early medieval style.

EDCS-10500421.translation: Balsimius of good memory rests here in peace, lived 60 years, died in the 13th indiction, during the reign [of the emperor/king].
EDCS-10500421.summary: This tomb inscription records the death of Balsimius, dated by indiction and reign, suggesting a late antique or early medieval context.

EDCS-10500422.translation: Concordia of good memory rests in this tomb, lived 10 years, died the 2nd of December.
EDCS-10500422.summary: This tomb inscription records the death of Concordia, likely a child, with a specific date.

EDCS-10500423.translation: Here rests in peace Laetus, the deacon, lived 66 years, died the 15th day before the Kalends of July in the 13th indiction, during the reign of our lord King Theobert.
EDCS-10500423.summary: This tomb inscription records the death of Laetus, a deacon, dated by indiction and the reign of King Theobert, indicating a post-Roman context.

EDCS-10500424.translation: In this tomb rests Sagria, of good memory, who lived for two years and passed away in peace on the eighth day before the Kalends of September, in the ninth indiction, during the reign of King Theodobert.
EDCS-10500424.summary: A tomb inscription recording the death of Sagria at a young age during the reign of King Theodobert.

EDCS-10500426.translation: Sacred to Mercury and Augustus. Apr Ieuru, son of Aprostasgi.
EDCS-10500426.summary: A dedication to Mercury and Augustus by an individual named Apr Ieuru.

EDCS-10500427.translation: In this tomb rests Caesarius, of good memory, who lived in Lentino for 80 years and passed away in peace on the third day before the Kalends [of an unspecified month] in the year [unspecified].
EDCS-10500427.summary: A tomb inscription recording the death of Caesarius, who lived in Lentino for 80 years.

EDCS-10500428.translation: Bassinus, son of Bassulus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars.
EDCS-10500428.summary: A votive inscription to Mars by Bassinus, son of Bassulus.

EDCS-10500429.translation: To the god Mercury, from Sextus Sulpicius Magninus.
EDCS-10500429.summary: A dedication to the god Mercury by Sextus Sulpicius Magninus.

EDCS-10500430.translation: Sacred to Mercury, from Vindonius Silvanus.
EDCS-10500430.summary: A dedication to Mercury by Vindonius Silvanus.

EDCS-10500432.translation: Sacred to Mercury, from Vindonius Silvanus.
EDCS-10500432.summary: A dedication to Mercury by Vindonius Silvanus.

EDCS-10500439.translation: To the divine spirits of the Emperors and to the god Mercury Dumiatus, Matutinius Victorinus gave this gift.
EDCS-10500439.summary: A dedication to the Imperial cult and Mercury Dumiatus by Matutinius Victorinus.

EDCS-10500440.translation: Romogillius Regalius, son of Macri, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the divine spirits of the Emperors.
EDCS-10500440.summary: A votive inscription to the Imperial cult by Romogillius Regalius, son of Macri.

EDCS-10500451.translation: In this tomb rests in peace Iulianeta, of good memory, who passed away at 45 years of age in the ninth year of the reign of our lord Alaric.
EDCS-10500451.summary: A tomb inscription recording the death of Iulianeta at the age of 45 during the reign of King Alaric.

EDCS-10500452.translation: In this tomb rests Barbario, a deacon of good memory, who lived 70 years and passed away on the third day before the Kalends of March in the eighth year of the reign.
EDCS-10500452.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the death of Barbario, a deacon, with details of his age and the regnal year.

EDCS-10500453.translation: In this tomb rests Candidus of good memory, in peace, who lived three years, four months, and eighteen days, and passed away on the third day before the Ides of May in the fifteenth year of the reign of the lord Theudorich.
EDCS-10500453.summary: This tomb inscription records the death of Candidus, including his age in years, months, and days, and the regnal year of Theudorich.

EDCS-10500454.translation: In this tomb rests Irena of good memory, in peace, who lived 20 years, and passed away on the eleventh day before the Kalends of November in the fourth year of the reign of our lord Teudobert.
EDCS-10500454.summary: This tomb inscription commemorates Irena, detailing her age and the regnal year of Teudobert.

EDCS-10500455.translation: In this tomb rests Pioni of good memory, in peace, who passed away at the age of sixty-three on the third day before the Kalends of May in the twentieth year of the reign of our lord Teodobert the king.
EDCS-10500455.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Pioni, specifying his age at death and the regnal year of King Teodobert.

EDCS-10500456.translation: In this tomb rests Palladius of good memory, who lived 17 years, and passed away on the Kalends of September in the fifth indiction of King Teudorich.
EDCS-10500456.summary: This tomb inscription records the death of Palladius, noting his age, the date, and the reign of King Teudorich.

EDCS-10500457.translation: In this tomb lies John of good memory, aged 37 years.
EDCS-10500457.summary: This is a simple tomb inscription stating that John of good memory, aged 37, lies in this tomb.

EDCS-10500458.translation: Iulia Severa fulfilled her vow for Sianna, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10500458.summary: This votive inscription records Iulia Severa fulfilling a vow made on behalf of Sianna.

EDCS-10500459.translation: To the departed spirits, in memory of Priscinius.
EDCS-10500459.summary: This is a dedication to the Manes (departed spirits) in memory of Priscinius.

EDCS-10500460.summary: This is a dedication to Acutibilis, an individual from the Arverni tribe.

EDCS-10500462.translation: Augustali, Iulia Postuminula, granted this plot to her excellent husband by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10500462.summary: This funerary inscription records Iulia Postuminula granting a burial plot to her husband, decided by the town council (decurions).

EDCS-10500463.translation: The Cadurci tribe publicly erected this monument in recognition of his merits to Marcus Lucterius Leon, son of Lucterius Senecianus, who had held all the highest offices in his homeland and served as priest of the Altar of Augustus at the confluence of the Arar and Rhodanus rivers.
EDCS-10500463.summary: A public monument erected by the Cadurci tribe to Marcus Lucterius Leon, a priest and local official, for his merits, likely in the Roman period.

EDCS-10500465.summary: A tombstone recording the death and age of a person named Doryphorus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10500466.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Firmia Magna. Firmius, her husband, [erected this].
EDCS-10500466.summary: A funerary dedication for Firmia Magna by her husband Firmius, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-10500470.translation: Gregory, an exile, son of an exile and of Peter, lies buried in this tomb. His own hands, however, born on Spanish soil, have completed his final, lamentable day in Cadurci.
EDCS-10500470.summary: An epitaph for Gregory, an exile from Spain, who died in Cadurci, likely in the late Roman or early post-Roman period.

EDCS-10500471.translation: Tomb of the neophyte Paul, who preceded [us] in the peace of the Lord, on the Lord's Day, the Nones of November, when Leo was consul for the third time.
EDCS-10500471.summary: The tomb of Paul, a neophyte, marking his death on a specific date in the late Roman Empire, indicated by the consulship of Leo.

EDCS-10500472.translation: To Lucius Bantius Celsus, a guardsman. Secundus, his freedman, [erected this] at his own expense.
EDCS-10500472.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman, Secundus, for his former master Lucius Bantius Celsus, a guardsman, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10500473.translation: To Zmaragdus, the Steward, Quaestor, and Master, by decree of the town council, for the family of Tiberius Caesar, which is in the mines.
EDCS-10500473.summary: An inscription honoring Zmaragdus for his service as an official to the family of Emperor Tiberius in the mining administration, likely Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10500474.translation: Alcovindus, son of Suoliccenus, son of Saturnius, a Cadurcus.
EDCS-10500474.summary: An ethnic and genealogical inscription identifying Alcovindus as a member of the Cadurci tribe, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10500477.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Junia Tertiola. Her daughters Tertia and Junia Prima made this [stone] at their own expense; her brother also dedicated the marble stone at his own expense.
EDCS-10500477.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Junia Tertiola by her daughters and brother, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-10500481.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Domitia Lurandia [dedicated this] for Albinius Senator.
EDCS-10500481.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Domitia Lurandia for Albinius Senator.

EDCS-10500488.summary: A simple dedication by an individual named Peregrinus, likely a tombstone or a dedication to a deity, from the Roman period.

EDCS-10500489.translation: To Mars Tritullus, the farmer, they willingly and deservedly paid their vow.
EDCS-10500489.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars Tritullus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10500490.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, with parts of names remaining.

EDCS-10500491.translation: To the departed spirits and to the memory of Gemina, his most sweet wife. Anticus, her husband, [dedicated this].
EDCS-10500491.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a husband to his deceased wife, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-10500494.translation: To the departed spirits. Hermeros [dedicated this].
EDCS-10500494.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-10500495.translation: To the honor and memory of Lucius Pomponius Bassulus and Lucius Pomponius Balbinus, his most dutiful sons. Lucius Julius Bassianus, their father, and Pomponia Regola, their mother, built and dedicated this temple from its foundation to its completion, along with the surrounding buildings.
EDCS-10500495.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a temple and associated buildings by parents in honor of their deceased sons, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10500497.translation: To the departed spirits. Camerianus dedicated this to Petronia, his wife, at his own expense.
EDCS-10500497.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a husband to his deceased wife, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-10500499.translation: Lucius Severius Severus, son of Lucius Severius, who held all offices in the city and who established this villa from the ground up, and Decimus Severius, the elder of his sons, established [this] for the health of themselves and their family.
EDCS-10500499.summary: This inscription records the establishment of a villa and the provision for the health of the family by Lucius Severius Severus and his son, likely dating to the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10500500.translation: [---] daughter of Pomp[---] of Valicus, a friend [dedicated this].
EDCS-10500500.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning a daughter of someone named Pomp[---] and a friend, likely funerary or dedicatory.

EDCS-10500502.translation: [---] M[---] Materna, prompted by her will and divine inspiration, gave this statue of Father Liber to Sergius Secundinus, her son, deservedly.
EDCS-10500502.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription of a statue of Liber Pater by a mother to her son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10500503.translation: Sextus Talonius Musicus placed this at his own expense to Adidon and Augustus, Scutari the bishop, while alive, as God.
EDCS-10500503.summary: A dedication to deities and a bishop by Sextus Talonius Musicus, likely a private monument from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10500504.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld and to Gaius Julius Paternus, lector of the ironworks, who had held all civic offices in his city, his friend, who arranged for this to be placed for himself while alive and dedicated it under the axe.
EDCS-10500504.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Julius Paternus for himself and his friend, Sextus Donnius Priscianus, a lector of ironworks, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10500505.translation: Gutuater, prefect of the colony, lector of the ironworks, before I rest here, I saw both my children, Nonnius Ferox, flamen, twice duovir.
EDCS-10500505.summary: An epitaph for Gutuater, a high-ranking local official, mentioning his children and career achievements, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-10500510.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld and eternal memory of Marcus Julius Cometalis, to Maria, his dearest wife.
EDCS-10500510.summary: A funerary dedication to Marcus Julius Cometalis by his wife Maria, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10500512.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld and eternal memory of Terentius Amatius, Festa arranged for this to be placed for her brother while alive and dedicated the monument.
EDCS-10500512.summary: A funerary dedication by Festa for her brother Terentius Amatius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500515.translation: The tomb of Scutarius, saint and most blessed bishop of this city.
EDCS-10500515.summary: An inscription identifying the tomb of Bishop Scutarius, likely from late antiquity or the early Christian period.

EDCS-10500518.translation: To Salus (Health) for the human race, Sergius Primus placed this, deservedly. To Salus for the human race, Lucius Sergius Primus placed this, deservedly, to the goddess Salus.
EDCS-10500518.summary: A dedication to the goddess Salus (Health) by Sergius Primus, possibly during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500520.translation: To Etruscilla, wife of our Emperor Augustus, from the free citizenry of the Vellavii.
EDCS-10500520.summary: This inscription is a dedication from the Vellavii to Etruscilla, wife of the emperor, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-10500523.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld and eternal memory of Julia Marcia, Marciola her mother placed this.
EDCS-10500523.summary: A funerary dedication to Julia Marcia by her mother Marciola, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500524.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, Rufius Rufinus placed this for his most chaste wife, Julia Nocturna.
EDCS-10500524.summary: A funerary dedication by Rufius Rufinus to his wife Julia Nocturna, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500525.summary: A very brief inscription likely marking a tomb or memorial, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10500543.translation: To the spirits of the departed and the eternal memory of Licentiossa, who died at the age of 19.
EDCS-10500543.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Licentiossa, who died at nineteen years of age.

EDCS-10500544.translation: To the memory of Domitius Domitianus, who died.
EDCS-10500544.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating the deceased Domitius Domitianus.

EDCS-10500546.translation: To the eternal memory of Aveta.
EDCS-10500546.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the memory of Aveta.

EDCS-10500547.translation: Cara, his wife, placed this for the spirits of the departed and the memory of Martianus.
EDCS-10500547.summary: Cara dedicated this funerary monument to her husband Martianus.

EDCS-10500548.translation: His mother placed this for the spirits of the departed and the memory of Iulius Marullinus.
EDCS-10500548.summary: The mother of Iulius Marullinus dedicated this funerary monument to him.

EDCS-10500551.translation: To the spirits of the departed and the eternal memory of Lucentius, who died at the age of 31.
EDCS-10500551.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucentius, who died at thirty-one years of age.

EDCS-10500555.translation: Attinus, father, and Pollina, mother, erected this monument for Alpinius, a boy.
EDCS-10500555.summary: Attinus and Pollina, parents, erected this funerary monument for their son Alpinius.

EDCS-10501617.translation: Iccavos Oppianicnos vowed to Brigindo Cantalo.
EDCS-10501617.summary: This is a dedication by Iccavos Oppianicnos to the deity Brigindo Cantalo.

EDCS-10502129.translation: They took care to have the temple with its adornments, which his father had promised to have built, erected at his own expense, to the divine Emperors and Minerva, for Marcus Petronius Giamillus, son of Giamillus.
EDCS-10502129.summary: Marcus Petronius Giamillus completed the construction of a temple and its furnishings to the divine Emperors and Minerva, fulfilling his father's vow.

EDCS-10701804.translation: Silvanus the stonemason gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-10701804.summary: Silvanus, a stonemason, gladly fulfilled a vow made to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-10701805.translation: To the Divine Manes. For his dearest wife and Montanus his son and his mother-in-law.
EDCS-10701805.summary: This funerary inscription honors the deceased wife, son, and mother-in-law of Sextus Valerius Lucanus.

EDCS-11401175.translation: To the Divine Manes. Of Lucius Aelius Aelianus, the son.
EDCS-11401175.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Aelius Aelianus, the son.

EDCS-11401177.translation: To the Divine Manes. Of Sullogus.
EDCS-11401177.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sullogus.

EDCS-11401186.translation: A monument for Addedomarus, for his deceased son Orbiotalis.
EDCS-11401186.summary: This inscription records a monument erected by Addedomarus for his deceased son Orbiotalis.

EDCS-11401189.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Urbicus.
EDCS-11401189.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Urbicus.

EDCS-11800782.summary: This inscription likely marks a workshop or a product of the Maccari workshop.

EDCS-11800783.translation: Atticus Belexis gladly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Erriapus.
EDCS-11800783.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Atticus Belexis fulfilling a vow to the god Erriapus.

EDCS-11801040.summary: This inscription appears to be a personal message, possibly a tombstone, for Ierax and Pyramus.

EDCS-11801041.summary: This inscription lists three names, Petraites, Prudens, and Hermes, possibly individuals associated with a tomb or monument.

EDCS-11801043.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely a tombstone or a dedication, with no clear date or context.

EDCS-12000411.translation: Annia Iuliana, the heir and wife, arranged for the erection of statues for Marcus Annius Severus and his relatives, for whom he had ordered statues to be erected in his will.
EDCS-12000411.summary: This funerary inscription records that Annia Iuliana erected statues in accordance with the will of her husband, Marcus Annius Severus, honoring him and his relatives.

EDCS-12000420.translation: To the Divine Spirits, for the memory of Pompeia Primilla, daughter of Quintus. Quintus Pompeius Avitus and Cominia Primilla, daughter of Lucius, [erected this] for their most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-12000420.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their daughter, Pompeia Primilla, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12000423.translation: Albus, son of Albus, [erected this] for his deceased father Albinus, son of Silvanus, and for his wife Annereni, daughter of Marinus, while she was still alive.
EDCS-12000423.summary: This epitaph records the erection of a monument by a son for his deceased father and living wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000424.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, Titullus, son of Cintugnatus, [and] his mother Edunxe, gladly and deservedly paid their vow.
EDCS-12000424.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter by a man named Titullus and his mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000426.translation: To the Genius of Caius Aconius Taurus Veturius.
EDCS-12000426.summary: This is a dedication to the genius of a person named Caius Aconius Taurus Veturius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000427.translation: Coerana, daughter of Eranus, aged two years, lies here.
EDCS-12000427.summary: This is a tombstone commemorating a young girl named Coerana, who died at the age of two, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000428.translation: Scinni Fonney, gladly and deservedly paid her vow to Arrius, son of Spurius.
EDCS-12000428.summary: This is a votive inscription indicating that Scinni Fonney fulfilled a vow to Arrius, son of Spurius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000433.translation: Sabinus, to the god Ilunnus, gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-12000433.summary: This is a votive inscription by Sabinus to the god Ilunnus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000435.translation: To Belgonus, the god, Julius Certus willingly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-12000435.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Belgonus, dedicated by Julius Certus, likely dating to the Roman period when local deities were worshipped.

EDCS-12000436.text_edition: \n Tutelae pro salute Iustini Iulius Paris votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-12000436.translation: For the safety of Iustinus, Julius Paris willingly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-12000436.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated by Julius Paris to the goddess Tutela for the health of Iustinus, likely dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-12000437.translation: Vitalis, son of Bonxus(?), willingly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-12000437.summary: This is a votive inscription by Vitalis, possibly the son of Bonxus, who fulfilled a vow, likely dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-12000438.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely belonging to a tombstone or a dedication, mentioning Saturninus, son of Honestus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000441.translation: Laureia, daughter of Gesellus, willingly paid her vow as deserved.
EDCS-12000441.summary: This is a votive inscription by Laureia, daughter of Gesellus, who fulfilled a vow, likely dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-12000442.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Antistia Severiana, dearest wife. Caius Antistius Eutychianus, husband(?).
EDCS-12000442.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Antistia Severiana by her husband, Caius Antistius Eutychianus, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12000443.translation: On the death of Gaius Antistius Protogenes, and of the living Antistia Erotene, wife, and of the deceased Antistia Byblis, daughter.
EDCS-12000443.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the deaths of Gaius Antistius Protogenes, his wife Antistia Erotene, and their daughter Antistia Byblis, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12000451.summary: This is likely an epitaph or dedication for a freedman named Philetus, who belonged to Claudius Catullus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000452.translation: To the Divine Spirits and the memory of Iulia Secundilla. Sarmesibia, his granddaughter, took care to have this made and dedicated it under the axe.
EDCS-12000452.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a granddaughter for Iulia Secundilla, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000453.text_edition: \n Tutelae Adehio et Capito Adei Harbelestegis structores votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-12000453.translation: To Tutela, Adehius and Capito, sons of Adehius Harbelestegis, willingly paid their vow as deserved.
EDCS-12000453.summary: This is a votive inscription by Adehius and Capito, sons of Adehius Harbelestegis, to the goddess Tutela, likely dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-12000454.translation: Here lies Flavinus of the unit of Mattiaci Seniorum, who lived for forty-five and a half years and left behind great cruelty to his wife and sons.
EDCS-12000454.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavinus, a soldier from the Mattiaci, dating possibly to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000455.translation: To the spirits of the underworld and in memory of Polychronus, deceased, aged 40. Thorybius erected this.
EDCS-12000455.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Polychronus, who died at the age of 40, set up by Thorybius, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12000459.translation: Ponticus, freedman of Attilius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the divine Mercury.
EDCS-12000459.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury, dedicated by Ponticus, a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000464.text_edition: \n Numinibus Augustorum et Magnae Matri Deum Augustae Lucius Pomponius Sexti Pomponi Paterni sacerdotis Arensis filius Quirina Paternus aram taurobolicam posuit dedicavitque\n
EDCS-12000464.translation: To the divine powers of the Emperors and to the Augusta Magna Mater Deum (Great Mother of the Gods), Lucius Pomponius Paternus, son of Sextus Pomponius Paternus, priest of the Arenses, belonging to the tribe Quirina, set up and dedicated an altar for a taurobolium (bull sacrifice).
EDCS-12000464.summary: A private individual dedicated a taurobolic altar to imperial deities and the Great Mother of the Gods, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-12000466.translation: Cessorina, wife of Ulpius Exoratus, soldier of the Legion XXII Adnamatinia, placed this.
EDCS-12000466.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ulpius Exoratus, a soldier of the XXII Legion, dedicated by his wife, Cessorina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000471.translation: Suadugena, a dear parent, placed this to the Divine Shades and memory of Claudius Placidas, a citizen of the Petrucori.
EDCS-12000471.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Claudius Placidas, a citizen of the Petrucori, dedicated by his parent Suadugena, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000472.translation: The guardian official (tutor) Secundus, son of Bassinus, placed this at his own expense.
EDCS-12000472.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription set up by Secundus for Bassinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000474.translation: To the Divine Shades and memory of Bassiania Viblina.
EDCS-12000474.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bassiania Viblina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000477.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription for Lucius Iulius Expectatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000478.translation: Iulius Potitianus, his freedman, placed this to the Divine Shades of Iulia Marina.
EDCS-12000478.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulia Marina, dedicated by her freedman Iulius Potitianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000480.translation: To the Divine Shades of Saturninus.
EDCS-12000480.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Saturninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000481.translation: His mother and father took care of this for Tocus, son of Blandus.
EDCS-12000481.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tocus, son of Blandus, set up by his parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000485.translation: Lucius Annius Saturio gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-12000485.summary: A private vow fulfilled by Lucius Annius Saturio to the god Mercury, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-12000486.summary: An ownership record of a slave named Helenus by his master Aulus Lycius, probably dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12000488.translation: On the third day before the Nones of May, the return of Mustela, deposited during the consulship of our lord Gratian Augustus for the third time and the most illustrious Equitius.
EDCS-12000488.summary: A legal or administrative record of an item or person named Mustela being returned or deposited during the consulship of Gratian and Equitius in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-12000490.translation: I declare to the persons written below, Lentinus and Tasgillus, that they should be present at Pluto and Proserpina; let them depart from here. Just as this puppy has harmed no one, so may the accusers not be able to win this lawsuit, just as the mother of this puppy could not defend it, so may their advocates not be able to defend them. So may they be turned away from this lawsuit, just as this puppy has been turned away and cannot get up. Just as animals have been silenced in this monument and cannot get up, so may they also be mute.
EDCS-12000490.summary: A curse or imprecation inscribed on a monument, likely in a provincial setting, intended to silence enemies and prevent them from winning a lawsuit, invoking underworld deities and possibly referring to a tomb.

EDCS-12000493.translation: Sacred to the gods, to the shades below. Sereni's daughter, Iulia Secundina, dedicated this to her deceased mother, who lived 40 years.
EDCS-12000493.summary: A funerary dedication by Sereni for his daughter Iulia Secundina, who died at the age of 40, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12000494.translation: To the gods below, to the shades. Tascius Paullinus to his wife, Iulia Rufina.
EDCS-12000494.summary: A funerary dedication from Tascius Paullinus to his wife Iulia Rufina, typical of Roman imperial burial inscriptions.

EDCS-12000495.translation: To the gods below, to the shades. Lucius Secolcera [dedicated this to?] Sil Forens S.
EDCS-12000495.summary: A fragmented funerary dedication to the shades, mentioning Lucius Secolcera and Sil Forens, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12000496.translation: Lentinus [dedicated this] to his wife Florina.
EDCS-12000496.summary: A funerary dedication from Lentinus to his wife Florina, a common type of Roman imperial tomb inscription.

EDCS-12000498.translation: To the gods below, to the shades and to the memory of Verneria.
EDCS-12000498.summary: A funerary dedication to the shades and memory of Verneria, characteristic of Roman sepulchral inscriptions.

EDCS-12000501.translation: To his most beloved wife, Iulia Rufina, who lived 23 years, and to their daughter, Julia. Receptius, son of Divixus, [dedicated this].
EDCS-12000501.summary: A funerary dedication by Receptius, son of Divixus, to his beloved wife Iulia Rufina (aged 23) and their daughter Julia, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12000502.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a bench by Merca Postumus.

EDCS-12000503.translation: Privata for herself and Gaius Julius Tauricus.

EDCS-12000504.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Mavida by Cacculla.

EDCS-12000507.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Cintusmus, identified as a garrigarius.

EDCS-12000513.summary: This inscription is a memorial dedication for Aurora.

EDCS-12000515.translation: To the departed spirits of Blaesus.

EDCS-12000517.translation: To the departed spirits of Camledu.

EDCS-12000520.translation: To the departed spirits of Cerialis.
EDCS-12000520.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirit of Cerialis.

EDCS-12000522.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Clasicus.

EDCS-12000523.translation: To the departed spirits of Claudia Aucta.
EDCS-12000523.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirit of Claudia Aucta.

EDCS-12000525.translation: To the departed spirits of Cornelius Hermes and his slave Ulatoanius.
EDCS-12000525.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Cornelius Hermes and his slave Ulatoanius.

EDCS-12000526.translation: To the departed spirits of Asiatica, 70 years old.
EDCS-12000526.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirit of Asiatica, who died at the age of 70.

EDCS-12000530.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Flavius Macer.
EDCS-12000530.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Flavius Macer.

EDCS-12000532.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Gaudilla.

EDCS-12000533.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Germanicus.

EDCS-12000534.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Graccha, for 1 year and 4 months.

EDCS-12000535.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Lucius Graecus.
EDCS-12000535.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Graecus.

EDCS-12000537.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: His heirs placed this for Hermeoloni, son of Coblius. Antitheus and Salluce, daughter of T., placed this for Sempronius Hermetus, son of Biroigallus.
EDCS-12000537.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription with multiple dedicants and recipients, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-12000544.translation: To the spirits of the underworld and to the memory of Martianus.

EDCS-12000545.translation: To the eternal spirits of the underworld, [for] Mansueto and Mansueta.
EDCS-12000545.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the underworld for two individuals named Mansueto and Mansueta.

EDCS-12000546.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, [for] Materna.
EDCS-12000546.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the underworld for an individual named Materna.

EDCS-12000559.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, [for] Secundus.
EDCS-12000559.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the underworld for an individual named Secundus.

EDCS-12000560.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Senilus.
EDCS-12000560.summary: This is a dedication to the underworld deities by Senilus.

EDCS-12000562.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Silvira.
EDCS-12000562.summary: This is a dedication to the underworld deities by Silvira.

EDCS-12000565.translation: To the spirits of the underworld and to Suaduila.

EDCS-12000566.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Suavius.
