EDCS-12000567.translation: To the spirits of the underworld and to the memory of Taurilla.
EDCS-12000567.summary: This is a dedication to the underworld deities and to the memory of Taurilla.

EDCS-12000570.summary: This is a dedication to the memory of Thalia.

EDCS-12000577.translation: Marcus Catius Quirina Diocharus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Jupiter, Best and Greatest.
EDCS-12000577.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter by Marcus Catius Quirina Diocharus.

EDCS-12000579.translation: To the spirits of the underworld and to the memory of Mansuetus.
EDCS-12000579.summary: This is a dedication to the underworld deities and to the memory of Mansuetus.

EDCS-12000583.translation: Primus sends greetings to the goddess Subremia.
EDCS-12000583.summary: This is a greeting to the goddess Subremia by Primus.

EDCS-12000585.text_edition: \n Numini Augusti deae Souconae Divixtus Silani filius\n
EDCS-12000585.translation: To the divine power of the Emperor and the goddess Soucona, Divixtus, son of Silanus.
EDCS-12000585.summary: A dedication by an individual named Divixtus to the numen of the Emperor and the local goddess Soucona, probably from Roman Gaul.

EDCS-12000586.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Bodolenus as the son of Ebrotus.

EDCS-12000587.translation: To the divine powers of the Emperors and to the god Mercury, Livius Coi [dedicated this].
EDCS-12000587.summary: This dedication to the divine powers of the Emperors and Mercury was made by Livius Coi, likely a private offering.

EDCS-12200190.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a funerary epitaph or ownership mark for individuals named Hibernus and Anthrax.

EDCS-12400047.translation: For Emperor Caesar Lucius [Domitius] Aurelianus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power, consul for the third time, father of the country; by the civitas of the Vellavorum, 13 miles.
EDCS-12400047.summary: This inscription records the construction of a road, 13 miles long, by the civitas of the Vellavorum, dedicated to Emperor Aurelian (reigned 270-275 CE).

EDCS-12400053.translation: To our Lords Emperors Marcus Julius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus and Marcus Julius Philippus, the most noble Caesar, by the civitas of the Vellavorum, 3 miles.
EDCS-12400053.summary: The civitas of the Vellavorum records the construction of a road, 3 miles long, dedicated to Emperor Philip the Arab and his son, Caesar Philip, likely in the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-12400063.translation: For Emperor Caesar Marcus Cassianius Latinus Postumus, the Invincible, Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power, father of the country, consul for the fourth time; by the civitas of the Gabali.
EDCS-12400063.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the civitas of the Gabali to the usurper Emperor Postumus (reigned 260-269 CE).

EDCS-12400065.translation: For Emperor Caesar Gaius Vibius Trebonianus Gallus, Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power, twice consul, proconsul, father of the country, and for Emperor Caesar Gaius Vibius Afinius Gallus Veldumnianus Volusianus, Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power, twice consul, proconsul, father of the country.
EDCS-12400065.summary: This text is an dedication by the local community to co-emperors Trebonianus Gallus and his son Volusianus, who ruled together from 251-253 CE.

EDCS-12400070.translation: For our Lord Emperor Marcus Philippus Augustus and Marcus Julius Philippus, the most noble Caesar, by the civitas of the Arverni, 21 leagues.
EDCS-12400070.summary: The civitas of the Arverni records a distance of 21 leagues, dedicated to Emperor Philip the Arab and his son, Caesar Philip, likely in the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-12400073.translation: Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the divine Nerva, Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 5th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country; by the Augustonemetum community of the Arverni, 17 leagues.
EDCS-12400073.summary: This inscription records a distance of 17 leagues by the Arverni community at Augustonemetum, dedicated to Emperor Hadrian (reigned 117-138 CE).

EDCS-12400074.translation: Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 5th time, imperator for the 11th time, father of the country, consul for the 3rd time, designated for the 4th time; by Augustonemetum, 21 miles.
EDCS-12400074.summary: This inscription records a road of 21 miles by the Augustonemetum community, dedicated to Emperor Claudius (reigned 41-54 CE).

EDCS-12400075.translation: For Emperor Caesar Gaius [Messius] Trajanus Quintus [De]cius Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician [power], [---]
EDCS-12400075.summary: A dedication to Emperor Decius (reigned 249-251 CE) that is incomplete.

EDCS-12400079.translation: Emperor Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 5th time, emperor 11 times, father of his country, consul for the 3rd time and designated for the 4th, [dedicates this] 21 miles from Augustonemetum.
EDCS-12400079.summary: This is a milestone inscription from 21 miles outside Augustonemetum, dating to the reign of Emperor Claudius.

EDCS-12400080.translation: Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, son of the divine Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the divine Nerva, chief priest.
EDCS-12400080.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that names Emperor Hadrian, likely dedicating a public work during his reign.

EDCS-12400081.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus Maximus Germanicus, with tribunician power for the 5th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of his country, by the Arverni for 36 leagues.
EDCS-12400081.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Aurelian and records a tribute or grant of roads by the Arverni people.

EDCS-12400083.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Cassianio Latinio Postumo Pio Felici Invicto Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli III patri patriae civitate Arvernorum leugae XXXV\n
EDCS-12400083.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Cassianius Latinus Postumus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul for the 3rd time, father of his country, by the Arverni for 35 leagues.
EDCS-12400083.summary: This inscription honors the usurper emperor Postumus and records a tribute or grant of roads by the Arverni people.

EDCS-12400084.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 6th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of his country, proconsul, by the Lemovices for 34 leagues.
EDCS-12400084.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Gordian III and records a tribute or grant of roads by the Lemovices people.

EDCS-12400086.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 6th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of his country, proconsul, by the Lemovices for 30 leagues.
EDCS-12400086.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Gordian III and records a tribute or grant of roads by the Lemovices people.

EDCS-12400096.translation: To Emperor Caesar [Gaius] Pius Esuvius Tetricus Pius Felix Augustus, by the civitas Lemovices for 10 [leagues?], by the civitas Lemovices for 35 leagues.
EDCS-12400096.summary: This inscription honors the usurper emperor Tetricus I and possibly records road lengths associated with the Lemovices people.

EDCS-12400100.text_edition: \n Domino orbis et pacis Imperatori Caesari Marco Annio Floriano Pio Felici Invicto Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate patri patriae proconsuli civitas Petrucoriorum leugam\n
EDCS-12400100.translation: To the lord of the world and of peace, Emperor Caesar Marcus Annius Florianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, father of his country, proconsul, by the civitas Petrucoriorum for [number illegible] league.
EDCS-12400100.summary: This inscription honors the usurper emperor Florianus and records a contribution or road length by the Petrucorii people.

EDCS-12400101.translation: To our lords, Emperors Caesars Gaius Valerius Diocletian Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Marcus Aurelius Maximian Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, and to Flavius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximian, most noble Caesars, by the civitas Nitiobrogum for 6 leagues.
EDCS-12400101.summary: This inscription honors the Tetrarchs (Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, and Galerius) and records a tribute or road length by the Nitobroges people.

EDCS-12400102.translation: To our lord Emperor Flavius Valerius Constantius, Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power.
EDCS-12400102.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantius I, likely as part of a public work or milestone, and records his titles.

EDCS-12400103.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Imperatore Caesare Flavio Valerio Constantino Pio nobilissimo Caesare divi Constanti Pii Augusti\n
EDCS-12400103.translation: To our Lord the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantine, most noble and pious Caesar, son of the deified Constantius Pius Augustus.
EDCS-12400103.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine the Great, likely for a public work or building, dated to his reign (306-337 CE).

EDCS-12400111.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander, pious, son of the deified Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Magnus, grandson of the deified Septimius Severus. 11 leagues from Limonum and 10 leagues from the borders.
EDCS-12400111.summary: This inscription records a milestone or boundary marker relating to Emperor Severus Alexander, dating it to his reign (222-235 CE).

EDCS-12400163.translation: To the Emperor Nerva Trajan, son of the deified Nerva, Caesar Augustus Germanicus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power, consul for the 27th time.
EDCS-12400163.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Trajan, likely for a public work, noting his extensive titles and consulship, suggesting a date around 103 CE.

EDCS-12400168.translation: Emperor Nerva Caesar Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul for the third time, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-12400168.summary: This is a formal titulature of Emperor Nerva, listing his key titles and honors, likely from an official monument dated to his reign (96-98 AD).

EDCS-12400169.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantius, the greatest, most noble Caesar, the pious, fortunate, unconquered emperor, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul for the 4th time, [and] 14th year.
EDCS-12400169.summary: This is an inscription honoring Caesar Constantius (likely Constantius Chlorus), listing his titles and possibly the date of his reign or a specific event.

EDCS-12400170.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Pius Esuvius Tetricus, pious, fortunate, unconquered Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul, proconsul. 16 leagues from Civitas Pictorum and 20 leagues from the borders.
EDCS-12400170.summary: This inscription records a milestone or boundary marker for the usurper Tetricus I, likely related to the province of Aquitania, dated to his reign (271-274 CE).

EDCS-12400171.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Claudius Tacitus, unconquered, pious, fortunate Augustus, pontifex maximus, father of the fatherland, holding tribunician power, consul for the second time. 16 leagues from Civitas Pictorum and 20 leagues from the borders.
EDCS-12400171.summary: This inscription records a milestone or boundary marker for Emperor Tacitus, likely related to the province of Aquitania, dated to his short reign (275-276 CE).

EDCS-12400172.translation: To our lord Marcus Aurelius, with tribunician power.
EDCS-12400172.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Aurelius, likely the emperor, listing his title of tribunician power, suggesting it was erected during his reign.

EDCS-12400175.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland. 9 leagues from Limonum and 7 leagues from the borders.
EDCS-12400175.summary: This is a milestone or boundary marker for Emperor Antoninus Pius, specifying distances from Limonum and borders, dated to his reign (138-161 CE), likely around 140-142 CE.

EDCS-12400176.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland. 10 leagues from Limonum and 6 leagues from the borders.
EDCS-12400176.summary: This is a milestone or boundary marker for Emperor Antoninus Pius, specifying distances from Limonum and borders, dated to his reign (138-161 CE), likely around 140-142 CE.

EDCS-12400177.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the deified Nerva, Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time. 10 leagues from Limonum and 6 leagues from the borders.
EDCS-12400177.summary: This is a milestone or boundary marker for Emperor Hadrian, specifying distances from Limonum and borders, dated to his reign (117-138 CE), likely around 124 CE.

EDCS-12400179.translation: To our lords Flavius Valerius Constantius, the greatest, most noble Caesar, the state of the Pictones [erected this over a distance of] 10 leagues.
EDCS-12400179.summary: This inscription from the civitas of the Pictones honors Caesar Constantius (likely Constantius Chlorus) and indicates a measure of distance, possibly related to a road or boundary.

EDCS-12400227.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Claudius Tacitus, pious, fortunate, unconquered Augustus. 13 leagues from Avaricum.
EDCS-12400227.summary: This inscription records a milestone or boundary marker for Emperor Tacitus, indicating a distance from Avaricum, dated to his short reign (275-276 CE).

EDCS-12800260.summary: This is a simple inscription, likely a funerary epitaph or ownership mark for Gaius Salarius Artus.

EDCS-12800264.summary: This is a simple inscription, likely a funerary epitaph or ownership mark for Lucius Titius Thyrsus.

EDCS-12800265.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Maternianos, son of Marcus Balbus.
EDCS-12800265.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a tomb or offering to Maternianos, son of Marcus Balbus, to the Manes (spirits of the dead).

EDCS-12800271.summary: This is a brief inscription indicating that Priscinus was the maker of the object or monument.

EDCS-12800366.translation: To the divine spirit of Augustus and Minerva, Galerius Catulus and his wife Nonia dedicated this.
EDCS-12800366.summary: This dedication, likely from the Roman Imperial period, records a dedication to the divine Augustus and Minerva by Galerius Catulus and his wife.

EDCS-12800399.summary: This very brief inscription, likely Roman Republican or early Imperial, simply records the name Publius Cornelius.

EDCS-13302575.translation: Ariomeres, slave of lord Martinus, pray for me.
EDCS-13302575.summary: This inscription, possibly from late antiquity, is a private request for prayer from Ariomeres, a slave, to lord Martinus.

EDCS-13302927.translation: They erected this votive offering to the god Gomferanus and gladly paid their vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-13302927.summary: This votive inscription, likely from Roman Gaul or a nearby province, records the grateful fulfillment of a vow to the god Gomferanus.

EDCS-13302928.translation: All the marble workers gladly paid their vow to the god Erriapus.
EDCS-13302928.summary: This votive inscription, likely from Roman Gaul or a nearby province, records the grateful fulfillment of a vow to the god Erriapus by marble workers.

EDCS-13302929.translation: Albinus, son of Paulinus, set this up in a vision to Erriapo.
EDCS-13302929.summary: This votive inscription, likely from Roman Gaul or a nearby province, records a dedication to Erriapo by Albinus, son of Paulinus, prompted by a vision.

EDCS-13302930.translation: Amandus paid his vow to the god Erriapo.
EDCS-13302930.summary: This votive inscription, likely from Roman Gaul or a nearby province, records the fulfillment of a vow to the god Erriapo by Amandus.

EDCS-13302931.translation: Anicianus gladly paid his vow to the god Erriapo, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-13302931.summary: This votive inscription, likely from Roman Gaul or a nearby province, records the grateful fulfillment of a vow to the god Erriapo by Anicianus.

EDCS-13302933.translation: Borsus, son of Euticus, paid his vow to Erriapo, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-13302933.summary: This votive inscription, likely from Roman Gaul or a nearby province, records the grateful fulfillment of a vow to Erriapo by Borsus, son of Euticus.

EDCS-13302934.translation: Faustina paid her vow to the god Erriape, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-13302934.summary: This votive inscription, likely from Roman Gaul or a nearby province, records the grateful fulfillment of a vow to the god Erriape by Faustina.

EDCS-13302935.translation: To the god Erriapo, Quintus Fufius Spectatus.
EDCS-13302935.summary: This is an inscription dedicating something to the god Erriapo by Quintus Fufius Spectatus.

EDCS-13302936.translation: Ingenuus, son of Spurius, willingly fulfilled his vow to Erriapo as was deserved.
EDCS-13302936.summary: This inscription records Ingenuus, son of Spurius, fulfilling a vow to Erriapo.

EDCS-13302938.translation: Quintus Minicius Ingenuus willingly fulfilled his vow to Erriapo as was deserved.
EDCS-13302938.summary: This inscription records Quintus Minicius Ingenuus fulfilling a vow to Erriapo.

EDCS-13302939.translation: Publius Nuce willingly fulfilled his vow to the god Erriapo for the safety of Navigius as was deserved.
EDCS-13302939.summary: This inscription records Publius Nuce fulfilling a vow to the god Erriapo for the safety of Navigius.

EDCS-13302940.translation: Primus, servant of Sembedo, willingly fulfilled his vow to Erriapo as was deserved.
EDCS-13302940.summary: This inscription records Primus, a servant of Sembedo, fulfilling a vow to Erriapo.

EDCS-13302941.translation: Severus, a stonemason, freedman of Sennetarus, willingly fulfilled his vow to Erriapo as was deserved.
EDCS-13302941.summary: This inscription records Severus, a stonemason and freedman, fulfilling a vow to Erriapo.

EDCS-13302942.translation: Tauricus, son of Taurinus, willingly fulfilled his vow to the god Erriape as was deserved.
EDCS-13302942.summary: This inscription records Tauricus, son of Taurinus, fulfilling a vow to the god Erriape.

EDCS-13302943.translation: Vetustus, son of Venustus, willingly fulfilled his vow to the god Erriapo as was deserved.
EDCS-13302943.summary: This inscription records Vetustus, son of Venustus, fulfilling a vow to the god Erriapo.

EDCS-13302944.translation: Vincentius happily fulfilled his vow to the god Eriapo for his own safety and that of his family.
EDCS-13302944.summary: This inscription records Vincentius fulfilling a vow to the god Eriapo for his own and his family's safety.

EDCS-13302946.translation: Amaradus willingly fulfilled his vow to Silvanus as was deserved.
EDCS-13302946.summary: This inscription records Amarádus fulfilling a vow to Silvanus.

EDCS-13302947.translation: To the god Silvanus, Tauriscus of the Taurini gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-13302947.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Silvanus made by Tauriscus of the Taurini.

EDCS-13302950.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or identifies an individual named Calestinus Muntanus.

EDCS-13302956.translation: Galus and Teixsossix are buried here.
EDCS-13302956.summary: This inscription records the burial of Galus and Teixsossix.

EDCS-13302958.translation: Artahe Rufo, son of IIFIS, gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-13302958.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Artahe made by Rufo, son of IIFIS.

EDCS-13302960.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Tiberius Claudius Rufus gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-13302960.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus made by Tiberius Claudius Rufus.

EDCS-13302966.translation: To the god Mars Sutugius, Marcus Mansuetius.
EDCS-13302966.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Mars Sutugius by Marcus Mansuetius.

EDCS-13302967.translation: To the god Sutugius, Burus son of [---], according to the vow of his father.
EDCS-13302967.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Sutugius by Burus, fulfilling his father's vow.

EDCS-13302968.translation: To the god Sutugius, Iulia Secundina gladly and deservedly paid her vow.
EDCS-13302968.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Sutugius made by Iulia Secundina.

EDCS-13302969.translation: To the god Lentinus, Lenti's daughter, Albinus son of Alpini, and Albina daughter of Alpini, gladly and deservedly paid their vows.
EDCS-13302969.summary: This inscription records a joint votive offering to the god Lentinus by Lenti's daughter, Albinus son of Alpini, and Albina daughter of Alpini.

EDCS-13302970.translation: Martialis Mina gladly and deservedly paid her vow.
EDCS-13302970.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Martialis Mina.

EDCS-13302972.translation: Carpentus, a god, to whom he willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-13302972.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Carpentus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-13302973.translation: Pompeius Modestus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the god Eberrius.
EDCS-13302973.summary: This is a votive inscription by Pompeius Modestus to the god Eberrius.

EDCS-13302976.translation: Secundus, son of Secundio, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the goddess Fortuna.
EDCS-13302976.summary: This is a votive inscription by Secundus, son of Secundio, to the goddess Fortuna.

EDCS-13302981.translation: Albinus, son of Orgoti, vowed to Mars with a golden bowl.
EDCS-13302981.summary: This is a votive inscription by Albinus, son of Orgoti, dedicating a golden bowl to Mars.

EDCS-13302984.translation: Sacred to Vulcan and Mars, from Chios, Paulinus in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-13302984.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Vulcan and Mars by Paulinus from Chios.

EDCS-13302985.translation: Aurelius Amor and Alcima willingly and deservedly paid their vow to the most holy divine power.
EDCS-13302985.summary: This is a votive inscription by Aurelius Amor and Alcima to a divine power.

EDCS-13302988.translation: He paid his vow to Erotenis, his wife.
EDCS-13302988.summary: This is a votive inscription, seemingly mentioning a vow paid to a wife named Erotenis.

EDCS-13302992.text_edition: \n Plotinae Imperatoris Traiani Caesaris Augusti Germanici Caius Iulius Serenus in nomine suo et Iuliae Luci filiae Iuliolae uxoris\n
EDCS-13302992.translation: Gaius Iulius Serenus, in his own name and that of his daughter Iuliola, daughter of Lucius, and his wife Iulia, to Plotina, wife of the Emperor Trajan Caesar Augustus Germanicus.
EDCS-13302992.summary: This is a dedication from Gaius Iulius Serenus and his family to Empress Plotina, wife of Emperor Trajan, likely for a private religious or public benefaction, dated to Trajan's reign (98-117 CE).

EDCS-13303007.translation: Publius Valerius Proculus, son of Publius, and...
EDCS-13303007.summary: This inscription begins the dedication by Publius Valerius Proculus, son of Publius, but is incomplete.

EDCS-13303027.translation: Christ, give your servant Aemiliana rest and eternal life.
EDCS-13303027.summary: This is a Christian epitaph requesting eternal rest and life for Aemiliana.

EDCS-13303030.translation: Taurus Sabinus gladly fulfilled his vow to the god Ilixon, as was deserved.
EDCS-13303030.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Ilixon, dedicated by Taurus Sabinus.

EDCS-13303031.translation: Avienus gladly fulfilled his vow to the god Ilunni, as was deserved.
EDCS-13303031.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Ilunni, dedicated by Avienus.

EDCS-13303032.translation: T. Rufus Boni gladly fulfilled his vow to the god Ilunni, as was deserved.
EDCS-13303032.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Ilunni, dedicated by T. Rufus Boni.

EDCS-13303037.translation: Silvinus, son of Verecundus, gladly fulfilled his vow to the god Baias, as was deserved.
EDCS-13303037.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Baias, dedicated by Silvinus.

EDCS-13303038.translation: Bulio gladly fulfilled his vow to the god Osoni, as was deserved.
EDCS-13303038.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Osoni, dedicated by Bulio.

EDCS-13303040.translation: Annus and Montanianus and Senixsio, his sons, from love and piety, dedicated this to the spirits of the departed, for their father O., who died, and for themselves, and the companions of Spariani jointly erected it.
EDCS-13303040.summary: This funerary inscription honors O. and his sons, dedicated by Annus, Montanianus, and Senixsio, possibly by the companions of Spariani.

EDCS-13303041.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Ingenus.
EDCS-13303041.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription mentioning Ingenus.

EDCS-13303047.text_edition: \n Caius Antistius Antistiae Rufinae libertus Threptus IIIIIIvir Augustalis sedes de sua pecunia dedit\n
EDCS-13303047.translation: The freedman Threptus, one of the six imperial priests, dedicated this seat from his own funds to the Augustan cult.
EDCS-13303047.summary: This is a dedication of a seat by a freedman to the Augustan cult, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13303048.text_edition: \n @(Obitus) Vinusius Viohossii filius Cahenna Sambilii filia uxsor sic\n
EDCS-13303048.translation: The death of Vinusius, son of Viohossus, Cahenna, daughter of Sambilius, his wife.
EDCS-13303048.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of a married woman named Cahenna and her husband Vinusius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13303049.text_edition: \n Dibus Axoniebus Inua pro filia Urbicus\n
EDCS-13303049.translation: For the gods of Axonia, Urbicus [dedicated this] for his daughter.
EDCS-13303049.summary: This is a votive offering by Urbicus to the gods of Axonia for his daughter, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13303050.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the underworld gods, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13303053.text_edition: \n Deae Tutelae Boudigae Marcus Aurelius Lunaris IIIIIIvir Augustalis coloniarum Eboraci et Lindi provinciae Britanniae inferioris aram quam voverat ab Eboraci sic avectus votum solvit libens merito Perpetuo et Corneliano consulibus\n
EDCS-13303053.translation: Marcus Aurelius Lunaris, one of the six imperial priests of the colonies of Eboracum and Lindum in the province of Lower Britain, freed from his vow and gladly and deservedly fulfilled the altar which he had vowed, having been conveyed from Eboracum, with Perpetuus and Cornelianus as consuls.
EDCS-13303053.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Boudiga by Marcus Aurelius Lunaris, a high-ranking local official, commemorating the fulfillment of a vow during the consulship of Perpetuus and Cornelianus, likely in the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13303057.translation: To Julianus, who departed on the seventh day before the Kalends of June, in the consulship of Tatianus, may he rest well in peace.
EDCS-13303057.summary: This funerary epitaph wishes peace to Julianus, who died during Tatianus' consulship.

EDCS-13303058.translation: Valerius Silvanus dedicated this sacred precinct to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and to Emperor Tiberius Caesar Augustus with his own money.
EDCS-13303058.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Emperor Tiberius Caesar Augustus, funded by Valerius Silvanus.

EDCS-13303060.translation: Magni's freedman dedicated this at his own expense to the divine power of the Augusti and to the Tutela of Apollo Matuicus.
EDCS-13303060.summary: This is a dedication by a freedman to the divine powers of the Emperors and Apollo Matuicus.

EDCS-13303063.translation: Saturninius Macarius, son of Cnaeus, of the Namnetes tribe, aged 23 years and [some months].
EDCS-13303063.summary: This inscription records the age and tribal origin of Saturninius Macarius, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-13303064.translation: Rufinius Adnametus, son of Africanius, gave this offering to the divine spirit and genius of Lucius Caesar.
EDCS-13303064.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Rufinius Adnametus to the divine spirit and genius of Lucius Caesar, likely a military or imperial cult dedication.

EDCS-13303066.translation: To the departed spirits of Epistatus.
EDCS-13303066.summary: This inscription is a short dedication to the departed spirit of Epistatus, typically found on a tomb.

EDCS-13303067.translation: To the departed spirits of Ianuaris, aged...
EDCS-13303067.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication to the departed spirit of Ianuaris, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-13303068.translation: To the departed spirits of Iopis, aged 80 years.
EDCS-13303068.summary: This inscription records the age of Iopis, dedicated to the departed spirits, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-13303069.summary: This inscription simply records the name and parentage of Candidus, possibly as an epitaph or ownership mark.

EDCS-13303070.translation: Adelphius fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly to the divine spirit of Augustus and to the god Bassoledulitanus.
EDCS-13303070.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Adelphius to the imperial cult and a local deity, likely a votive offering.

EDCS-13303071.translation: Tetricus, son of Trericus, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly to the divine spirit of Augustus and to the god Adagrius for the health of his son Sedatus; Tetricus, son of Trericus, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly to the divine spirit of Augustus and to the god Adacrius for the health of his son.
EDCS-13303071.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Tetricus, son of Trericus, to the imperial cult and the god Adagrius for the health of his son Sedatus.

EDCS-13303077.translation: To the departed spirits and memory of Ioblicus and Aelius, they set up this monument for themselves and their living family.
EDCS-13303077.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Ioblicus and Aelius for themselves and their descendants, a funerary dedication.

EDCS-13303078.translation: To the departed spirits and memory of Publius Senecius Capri.
EDCS-13303078.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the departed spirits and memory of Publius Senecius Capri, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-13303079.translation: To the Divine Manes. Vilius Aurilio erected this monument for himself while alive.
EDCS-13303079.summary: A private funerary monument erected by Vilius Aurilio for himself.

EDCS-13303081.translation: To the Divine Manes and the memory of Corneli Victoris and his wife Iulia Mallonia, they erected [this] while alive.
EDCS-13303081.summary: A private funerary monument erected by Corneli Victoris and Iulia Mallonia for themselves.

EDCS-13303082.summary: A very brief inscription, likely referring to a funerary monument.

EDCS-13303084.translation: To the divine spirit of the Emperor and the god Mercury, Carissa erected an altar at the command of Sabini with her own money, sacred to the divine spirits of the Emperors and to Mercury; Biga, at the command of the priest, paid her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-13303084.summary: A dedication of an altar to the imperial numen and Mercury, funded by Carissa and with a vow fulfilled by Biga.

EDCS-13303085.translation: To the Divine Manes and the memory of S. P. Lepidus, his father erected [this].
EDCS-13303085.summary: A private funerary monument erected by the father of S. P. Lepidus.

EDCS-13303086.translation: To the Divine Manes and the memory of Caius Amuliolus.
EDCS-13303086.summary: A private funerary inscription for Caius Amuliolus.

EDCS-13303088.translation: Flavius Sabinus dedicated [this] to the god Silvanus, having been freed from illness, he paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-13303088.summary: A votive dedication to the god Silvanus by Flavius Sabinus after recovering from illness.

EDCS-13303089.translation: Iulia, daughter of Seurus, paid her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-13303089.summary: A votive inscription by Iulia, daughter of Seurus.

EDCS-13303339.translation: The pottery, made from the estates of our Emperor, from the Vocconian potteries, was made by Augustalis, the slave of Publicus Crescens.
EDCS-13303339.summary: An inscription from a pottery workshop indicating the origin of the materials and the maker, likely from the imperial estates.

EDCS-13303345.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hibernus Anthrax.

EDCS-13303346.translation: May Sucellus be favourable to us.
EDCS-13303346.summary: This is a votive dedication to the god Sucellus.

EDCS-13303394.translation: From Marcus Antonius Scaurus: a restorative for eye disease, from Marcus Antonius Scaurus: a remedy for suppuration, from Marcus Antonius Scaurus: a mixture for clear vision.
EDCS-13303394.summary: This inscription lists medical preparations sold by Marcus Antonius Scaurus, likely for sale on a shop or stall.

EDCS-13400252.text_edition: \n Lucius Valerius Veranus Sergia IIvir bis hanc viam restituit Cae Valerianus amicus\n
EDCS-13400252.translation: Lucius Valerius Veranus and Sergius, two-time chief magistrates, restored this road; Cae Valerianus, a friend [paid for it].
EDCS-13400252.summary: This is an inscription recording the restoration of a road by two chief magistrates, Lucius Valerius Veranus and Sergius, with a friend Cae Valerianus possibly contributing, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500327.translation: For Augustus Apollo and the goddess Sirona, and by the rites of the villagers of Nogeomgum, Pietonius Rufus [dedicated this].
EDCS-13500327.summary: This is a dedication by Pietonius Rufus to Augustus Apollo and the goddess Sirona, likely related to local villagers' rites.

EDCS-13900499.text_edition: \n Nymphis Augustis Eutyches Auggustorum nnostrorum votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-13900499.translation: Eutyches gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the August Deities of our Emperors.
EDCS-13900499.summary: This is a votive inscription by Eutyches to the August Deities, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900534.translation: [...] and Alcima willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-13900534.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by two individuals, Alcima and an unnamed person, who willingly discharged their obligation.

EDCS-14200124.translation: [To the Great Mother of the Gods] Ideae, for the health of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Felix Augustus Britannicus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 15th time, consul twice, twice designated consul, father of the country, Caius Iulius Drutedo and Balorice performed the taur(obolium), in accordance with their vow.
EDCS-14200124.summary: This is a religious inscription recording a taurabolium sacrifice performed by Caius Iulius Drutedo and Balorice for the health of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, likely in the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-14200125.translation: To the spirits of the departed and in memory of Lucius Carneolius, aged 51 years and 6 months, who served for 25 years in the centuria of K(a)ius Galliorum. Marcus Carneolius ordered this monument to be made with his money for his excellent father and dedicated it under the axe.
EDCS-14200125.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcus Carneolius for his father, Lucius Carneolius, a soldier of 51 years.

EDCS-14800022.translation: From Saturninus: a saffron preparation for clear vision. From Flavius Maximnus: for vigour. From Flavius Maximnus: Saturninus' O[intment?].
EDCS-14800022.summary: This inscription lists medicinal preparations, possibly for sale, associated with Saturninus and Flavius Maximnus.

EDCS-15000018.translation: Natalis Martialis and Sintus, provisioners, with their guilds, willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-15000018.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Natalis Martialis and Sintus, along with their associated guilds, likely as part of their professional duties.

EDCS-15000050.translation: For the god Sutugius, Iulia Secundina willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-15000050.summary: This is a votive dedication by Iulia Secundina to the god Sutugius.

EDCS-15000052.translation: For the god Martius Sutugius, [from] Mansuetus.
EDCS-15000052.summary: This is a dedication to the god Martius Sutugius by Mansuetus.

EDCS-15000053.translation: Lentina, daughter of Lentus, and Albina, daughter of Albinus, freely and deservedly fulfilled their vow to the god Lentinus.
EDCS-15000053.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by two women, Lentina and Albina, to the god Lentinus, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15000056.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Vius [dedicated this].
EDCS-15000056.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by an individual named Vius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15000057.translation: To the Spirits of the departed, Cunctilionia, daughter of Caius, [dedicated this] to her dearest husband.
EDCS-15000057.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a husband by his wife, Cunctilionia, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15200181.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Antonio Gordiano Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate VI consuli II patri patriae proconsuli civitate Lemovicum leugae XXX\n
EDCS-15200181.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 6th time, consul twice, father of the country, proconsul, from the territory of the Lemovices, 30 leugae away.
EDCS-15200181.summary: This is a milestone inscription indicating a distance of 30 leugae from the territory of the Lemovices, referencing Emperor Gordian III, likely from the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-15300297.translation: In this small tomb lies Valho, a devout woman, who lived 68 years and died on the 17th day before the Kalends of January, when Cethegus was the most distinguished consul.
EDCS-15300297.summary: This epitaph records the death of Valho, a devout woman, providing her age and the date of her death in relation to the consulship of Cethegus, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-15300298.translation: In the 8th year of our Emperors Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augusti.
EDCS-15300298.summary: This inscription marks a date within the 8th regnal year of Emperors Septimius Severus and Caracalla, likely indicating a public work or event from the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-15700007.translation: Of Titus, son of Marcus, [son of] Cnaeus Sergius.
EDCS-15700007.summary: This inscription appears to be part of a longer text, possibly a funerary or dedicatory inscription, naming three generations of Roman men, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-16300376.translation: To the Spirits of the departed and to the memory of Julia Secundilla, her daughter Nepotilla, born in Sarmesibia, had this made and dedicated it under the axe.
EDCS-16300376.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Julia Secundilla, erected by her daughter Nepotilla, who also performed the 'sub ascia' ritual, indicating it is a tombstone from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16400005.translation: To the Spirits of the departed and to the memory of Marcus Polychronus, deceased, aged 40 years. Thorybius, his father, [erected this].
EDCS-16400005.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Marcus Polychronus, aged 40, and was set up by his father Thorybius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16400017.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Agelon Bassiarius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16400018.translation: To the Spirits of the departed and to the memory of Claudius Placidi, a citizen of the Petrucorii, his dear parent Suadugena placed this.
EDCS-16400018.summary: This funerary inscription honors Claudius Placidi, a citizen of the Petrucorii, and was placed by his parent Suadugena, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16500148.translation: Lucius Iulius Aeto made [this] for Sabinus.
EDCS-16500148.summary: This is a dedication of a monument or object by Lucius Iulius Aeto for Sabinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16800439.translation: To Maia, Helenus son of Alycius.
EDCS-16800439.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Maia by Helenus, son of Alycius.

EDCS-17000092.translation: Marcus Petronius, son of Aemilius, took care to dedicate from his own resources the temple, along with its furnishings, which his father had piously vowed.
EDCS-17000092.summary: This is a dedication of a temple to the Divine Augusti and the goddess Minerva, completed by Marcus Petronius, son of Aemilius, fulfilling a vow made by his father.

EDCS-18300001.translation: From Katidianus Cirrus to Vitalio Nectarius.
EDCS-18300001.summary: This is a personal note or receipt, possibly a delivery record, from Katidianus Cirrus to Vitalio Nectarius.

EDCS-18300823.translation: From Caius Julius Atilianus, a pyx for wiping away tears; from Caius Julius Atilianus, a myrrh mixture for treating eye infections; from Caius Julius Atilianus, a cygnion for stinging eyes.
EDCS-18300823.summary: This list records multiple medicinal or cosmetic items provided by Caius Julius Atilianus, likely for sale or personal use.

EDCS-19800003.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Eliomorus dedicates.
EDCS-19800003.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Eliomorus.

EDCS-20500268.text_edition: \n Leontio Leontio Deidio Iovino inbolaverunt sic manus pedis quicumqui sic levavit annue culi qui i immer<g=I>o irue \n
EDCS-20500268.translation: Leontius and Leontius Deidius Iovinus dedicated it. Whoever lifts this with hand or foot, may anger of the gods be upon him.
EDCS-20500268.summary: This is a curse inscription, likely from a tomb, warning against desecration.

EDCS-20500269.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et memoriae Iulio Quinto defuncto annorum XXI POS POS CVN\n
EDCS-20500269.translation: To the departed spirits and the memory of Julius Quintus, who died at the age of 21.
EDCS-20500269.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young man named Julius Quintus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20500270.summary: This is a personal inscription identifying 'Fromatri Combaromarus, son of Ricnus'.

EDCS-20500271.translation: Macer gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-20500271.summary: This is a votive inscription recording that Macer willingly fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-20500273.translation: Namarius, his brother, (dedicated this) to Monucorius, husband of Belicicra, and to Seno, his wife.
EDCS-20500273.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Namarius to his brother Monucorius, husband of Belicicra, and his wife Seno.

EDCS-24200268.translation: Marcus Mansuetus Titullinus gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Fortuna Augusta.
EDCS-24200268.summary: This is a votive inscription recording that Marcus Mansuetus Titullinus willingly fulfilled a vow to Fortuna Augusta.

EDCS-24200270.text_edition: \n Cesido urciu CXXI congialdi XXV Melauso urciu LVI souxtu CC scutra V Atticco trisextia LXX congialdi XXV souxtu CXXV Veriduco congialdi XIIII trisextia XXX suxtu C Cintumo souxtu CXXX\n
EDCS-24200270.translation: Cesidus: 121 urns, 25 congius jars. Melausus: 56 urns, 200 measures. Atticcus: 70 measures, 25 congius jars, 125 measures. Veriducus: 14 congius jars, 30 measures, 100 measures. Cintumus: 130 measures.
EDCS-24200270.summary: This inscription records quantities of measures of liquids, likely wine or oil, possibly related to a contract or inventory.

EDCS-24200271.text_edition: \n Lucio Iulio Luci filio Bellico hoc monumentum heredem non sequetur\n
EDCS-24200271.translation: This monument will not pass to the heir of Lucius Julius Bellicus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-24200271.summary: This is a funerary inscription that explicitly states the monument is not to be inherited, likely indicating a specific burial plot arrangement.

EDCS-25601425.translation: Gaius Julius Carassounus gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Divine Augustus and the god Iovis Sabasius.
EDCS-25601425.summary: This is a votive inscription recording that Gaius Julius Carassounus willingly fulfilled a vow to the Divine Augustus and the god Iovis Sabasius.

EDCS-25601428.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Martialis, likely from an individual or group named Lagona.

EDCS-25700606.translation: Flavius Anastasius Paulus Probus Sabinianus Pompeius Anastasius, a man of note, count of the horse guards, and ordinary consul.
EDCS-25700606.summary: This inscription is a personal titulature of Flavius Anastasius Paulus Probus Sabinianus Pompeius Anastasius, who held high military and consular office, likely dating to his consulship.

EDCS-25800088.translation: Volusia Veneria, aged 13; Quintus Volusius Secundus, aged 15 years and 11 months and 25 days.
EDCS-25800088.summary: This inscription records the ages of two individuals, Volusia Veneria and Quintus Volusius Secundus, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-26201030.translation: Of Marcus Tuccius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Tromentina, of Galeo.

EDCS-32300731.translation: How well-matched the sacred gifts of the lamb's body appear, let the great pearl and golden gifts bring forth; let the Solomonian vessels yield to the metals. Art and faith make these things more pleasing, which were given to you, Christ. May the gifts of the blessed Felicis be such as the shepherd Abel then gave, and to whom you see the heart, and whom you equate in piety, Sirapta, who deservedly gave two coins.
EDCS-32300731.summary: This is a poetic inscription likely found in a Christian context, detailing offerings and piety, mentioning Christ, Abel, Felicis, and Sirapta.

EDCS-32300732.translation: Although envious death may threaten with its swift maw, you do not have the power to hold sway over the holy. For after Christ overcame fierce Tartarus on returning, you lie conquered beneath his feet by the merits of the just. The tombs that hold the sacred, world-radiating limbs of the pontiffs are covered here; the spirit inhabits the stars. The flowers of the twin Ruricii, with whom Rome was joined by the parental pinnacle, came forth. The eloquent vein, cultivated with worldly wisdom, came forth. By action, mind, step, hope, name, and blood, they are bound together, exulting equally, the grandfather here, the grandson there, each in his own time, founding pious temples of their patron. This one founded Augustinus, that one Petrus; this one upright, that one pious, this one serious, that one serene, competing with each other as to who would be greater, bestowing abundant wealth upon the poor from their riches, and redeeming the sins of the world with a scattering hand. We believe they are among the apostolic choirs. Happy are they who thus bought eternal rights in heaven from fleeting nobility.
EDCS-32300732.summary: This extensive epitaph commemorates the Ruricii family, highlighting their piety, patronage of churches, and virtuous lives, connecting them to apostolic traditions and heavenly rewards.

EDCS-32300733.translation: Although trembling old age pressed upon the pontiff, the people nevertheless wished their father to remain. Or if the debts of nature could be altered, the flock would have hastened their journey for their shepherd. But since this was not permitted, let this hope comfort the people: that faith brought him, deserving, to the stars without end, preserving his immaculate body for God with modesty. Exocius, with patience reigning victoriously in his heart, was an anchor amidst such great storms; free from bitterness in spirit, nourished by sweetness, he did not know how to return anger for offenses. A cultivator of temples, recreating citizens with hymns, he was a faithful balm for the wounds of his homeland. Having held the pontificate for fifteen years, he departs to the ancient fathers, the people mourning. It is not fitting, therefore, for him to weep with empty complaints, he whom the court of heaven holds after the darkness of the world.
EDCS-32300733.summary: This epitaph honors Exocius, a pontiff who served for fifteen years, emphasizing his piety, patience, and role as a spiritual leader, and his eventual heavenly reward.

EDCS-32300736.summary: This is a simple memorial inscription for Galla, indicating her death and remembrance.

EDCS-32300737.translation: Abraham, rightly to be joined with holy patrons, whom I do not hesitate to call your colleagues, for they so precede you that you too will soon follow. He grants a share of the kingdom, a portion for the martyr, born near the Euphrates, who suffered imprisonment for Christ and, at the age of five, his bonds loosened, having escaped famine, you hasten alone to the western shores of Susis, to the cruel king, as far as the soil. But the signs of confession follow your virtue, and you make the spirits of evil flee, making the fugitive flee. And the crowd of demons, when you come, orders them to yield, you command the demons to go. You are exiled, and you seek exile among all, and no office captivates you. The honor bestowed upon you is more burdensome. You shun Roman structures and the clamor of Byzantium, and the walls shattered by Titus the arrow-bearer; the wall of Alexandria does not hold you, and you scorn the homes of Antiochus and Elisaea of Byrsa. You disregard the fields of the water-dwellers, populous Ravenna, and those which have their name from wool-bearing swine; this corner pleases you, and a poor retreat, and a hut whose roof would be pressed down by thatch. Here you yourself build a venerable temple to God, you yourself, having first become a temple of God with your body. The end of your course and life's journey is finished; a double crown awaits your sweat. Thousands of the holy paradise now surround you. Abraham now has you as a fellow traveler. Now you enter the homeland, from which Adam fell. Now you can go to the fountain of your river.
EDCS-32300737.summary: This inscription is a poetic epitaph for a Christian martyr named Abraham, celebrating his piety, suffering for Christ, and eventual heavenly reward, likely dating to the late antique period based on the religious and stylistic content.

EDCS-32300738.translation: The enemy, and Adam, you drive from Paradise by deceit. Behold, God grants his servants access to the heavens. Thus, your death prepared better things for man; you banish him from earth, here He gives him the stars. Blessed Gallus proves these things, a witness and an advocate, noble on earth, rich in ascending to the polis. Supported by Christ's help, and not yet an adult in years, he sought greater things, hating the hearth gods with love. He fled his father's embrace and left his mother, seeking an abbot to guide him. There the raw novice began from a noble age to endure the weapons of the Lord's warfare. Finally, with the holy master Quintianus instructing him, man, proven in heart, is more precious than gold. Then he was transferred to the royal palace of King Theuderich, where he lived with pious love. Soon, when the master, leaving earthly things, sought the stars, the care of the flock passed to the disciple. For ruling the pontificate, he so guided the reins that he was a father by love in his duties, gentle, patient, good, just, loving, not given to offense, but a place of forgiveness if any injury occurred. Where there could be fury, there was triumph. Nourishing the people with his voice like a mother nursing her infants, drizzling sweet honey with seasoned salt. Exercising this work, he foresaw the future gifts, that nothing of the flock would perish by the shepherd. Thus the father governs the Church for five years, and yet, scarcely living for thirteen years, he journeyed by a better way to the holy celestial realms, not oppressed by the pyre's urn, but held in the embrace of God.
EDCS-32300738.summary: This is a metrical epitaph for a bishop, likely Bishop Gallus, recounting his early piety, monastic training under Quintianus, service in the royal court of Theuderich, and his episcopal tenure, probably dating to the Merovingian period.

EDCS-32300739.translation: Here lie the remains of Pope, a Roman by birth, famous by nation, and a pious pastor to his people. He raised this temple on his own estate with his own work, the pontifical structure which he received. He ruled the cathedra in peace for 62 years. The years of his life which remained in the world were 62 years. Migrating from the world, while the Frankish king ruled.
EDCS-32300739.summary: This inscription records the death and burial of Pope, a Roman bishop, noting his long tenure of 62 years ruling his see and the construction of a church on his property, likely dating to the early medieval period under Frankish rule.
